frontmatter.segment: Internal certification staff - Auditor / Customer Specialist (mixed role: ~30-40% Audits, remainder Customer Specialist work for one large key account plus several smaller accounts)

notes.body:
<!-- Write analysis prose in neutral third-person English. Keep participant quotes verbatim. -->

# Interview: P03

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- The participant has worked at the company for about 4 years, hired as an Auditor and later
  also taking on Customer Specialist responsibilities. The current split is roughly 30-40%
  Audit work and the remainder Customer Specialist work, driven largely by one large,
  support-intensive key account plus several smaller accounts.
- Two researchers (Speaker 1, leading; Speaker 2, supporting) walk the participant through how
  customer requests reach her, what data she needs and when, and what costs her the most time,
  ending with an open "green field" question about a future tool.
- The participant is not involved in TD (technical documentation) assessment itself; she
  coordinates who performs it and is fully involved in Audits herself.
- Tone was constructive and detail-oriented; the participant proactively shared a live screen
  walkthrough of her Appendix ABC and her personal Excel project-tracking list.
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Also ich würde sagen, bei mir ist es gerade eher, dass ich vielleicht sage 3040% Audits und der Rest Customer Specialist. Genau. bedingt sich so 'n bisschen durch diesen einen großen Kunden, wo irgendwie ja, der 'n bisschen betreuungsintensiver ist."
>
> Translation: "I'd say for me right now it's more like maybe 30-40% audits and the rest Customer Specialist. That's a bit driven by this one large customer, who is somewhat more support-intensive."
Code: #code/role-split-context

> "Bei den Großen da arbeiten wir auch eigentlich mit UCI, heißt da stellen Sie wirklich über UCI dann auch diesen Service Request und ja im Idealfall mit dem passenden Formular dazu. ... bei den kleineren dann das Gefühl, die schicken es lieber per Mail."
>
> Translation: "For the large customers we actually work with UCI [internal customer portal], meaning they really submit the service request through UCI, ideally with the matching form. ... for the smaller ones I have the feeling they prefer to send it by email."
Code: #code/intake-channel-variation

> "Tatsächlich ist es mir über UCI lieber, eigentlich aus dem Grund, weil ich klar dann irgendwie mit dieser Anfrage arbeiten muss, aber die ersten Schritte, die wir machen, ist eigentlich, dass der PC ein Projekt anlegt ... bei U.C.I. ist eigentlich so 'n bisschen klarer die Verantwortung, O.K., jetzt ist die P.C. am Zug."
>
> Translation: "I actually prefer it via UCI, really because the responsibility is a bit clearer: OK, now it's the Project Coordinator's turn. Via email, if they forget to CC the Project Coordinator, I have to manually forward it and actively ask them to open a project."
Code: #code/intake-channel-responsibility-clarity

> "Jetzt ist es tatsächlich in aktueller Fall so, dass ich das dann irgendwie nicht mehr öffnen konnte, aber da habe ich jetzt schon mal an UCI-Support geschrieben."
>
> Translation: "Right now it's actually the case that I could no longer open it, but I've already written to UCI support about that."
Code: #code/tool-bug-in-progress

> "Ja, also gerade bei den Formblättern, stellen die sich manchmal schlauer und mal dümmer an, da irgendwie die Häkchen richtig zu machen oder das auszufüllen ... das gibt es schon öfter mal dass ich das wieder zurückschicke."
>
> Translation: "Yes, especially with the forms, they sometimes manage better and sometimes worse to get the checkboxes right or fill it in correctly ... it happens fairly often that I send it back."
Code: #code/form-field-entry-errors

> "Sagen wir mal zu 90 Prozent muss zu dieser Application gehört auch dieser Appendix ABC dazu. ... das ist meistens nicht so, dass sie da überhaupt den Appendix ABC mitschicken, geschweige denn da schon die Änderung irgendwie drin haben, weil den Augenblick so ganz bewusst ist, wann ändere ich diesen Appendix ABC?"
>
> Translation: "About 90 percent of the time, this Appendix ABC has to be part of the Application. ... it's usually not the case that they even send the Appendix ABC along, let alone already have the change reflected in it, because it's often not clear at what point the Appendix ABC should be changed."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "Also einerseits dann mit den Daten, die sie dann haben ... Also immer dieser Cross-Check ... da verliere ich glaube ich am meisten Zeit ... es gibt hier in einer Basic UDI verschiedene intended users. Dürfen sie eigentlich gar nicht haben. ... dann müssen die sich erstmal fünf Wochen absprechen, dass sie irgendwie dann wieder eine neue Version schicken."
>
> Translation: "On one hand with the data they have ... always this cross-check ... I think that's where I lose the most time ... there are different intended users on one Basic UDI here. They aren't actually allowed to have that. ... then they first have to coordinate among themselves for five weeks before sending a new version."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "Wir haben immer nur ein Appendix ABC. ... Wenn er eins davon ändern möchte, dann schickt er alles noch mal quasi und die eine Zeile ist geändert."
>
> Translation: "We only ever have one Appendix ABC. ... If he wants to change one of them, he sends everything again, essentially, with the one row changed."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-versioning-context

> "Heißt in dieser Application ID, oder in dieser Application steht so ein bisschen beschrieben, was gemacht wird ... aber ihr habt Recht, so genau Wissen weiß ich nicht. Das sollte sich dann im Idealfall aus dem Formblatt von der Application ergeben."
>
> Translation: "So in this Application ID, or in this Application, there's a bit of a description of what's being done ... but you're right, I don't know exactly. That should ideally be derivable from the Application's form."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-versioning-context

> "Ja, also generell würde ich Rolle von der oder dem PC zu definieren, dass die wirklich in PSE die ganzen Timelines pflegen dafür zuständig sind ... aber jetzt für die Projekte von meinen Kunden, da also im Endeffekt, wenn ich hier nicht da regelmäßig schreibe ... passiert da nichts."
>
> Translation: "Well, generally I would define the PC's [Project Coordinator's] role as being responsible for maintaining all the timelines in PSE ... but for my customers' projects, if I don't write there regularly, nothing happens."
Code: #code/timeline-update-ownership-gap

> "Das ist so, wo ich denke, das ist so ein bisschen Doppelarbeit ... wenn ich die Rechte hätte, in der Zeit, wo ich ihr dann noch mal die E-Mail schreibe, dass ihr die Timeline anfasst ... könnt ihr es einfach direkt selber updaten. ... Also entweder die machen es selbstständig oder uns werden die Rechte gegeben, da auch was anzupassen."
>
> Translation: "That's where I think it's a bit of duplicate work ... if I had the rights, in the time it takes me to write an email asking them to touch the timeline ... you could just update it directly yourselves. ... So either they do it on their own, or we get the rights to adjust it too."
Code: #code/timeline-update-ownership-gap

> "Bei mir ist es auch oft so, dass ich irgendwie Supplier Audit kalkuliere, da kann ich mir wieder anscheinend alles aus dem Daumen schütteln ... Genauso ist es tatsächlich bei Change Notifications, da gibt es nicht so eine richtig offizielle Vorlage. ... das ist nichts, was in ROXPA ist und so ein bisschen inoffiziell läuft."
>
> Translation: "For me it's often the case that I sort of calculate a Supplier Audit out of thin air ... it's the same for Change Notifications, there isn't really an official template. ... it's not in ROXPA [the official process documentation system] and runs a bit unofficially."
Code: #code/no-official-cost-template

> "Fände tatsächlich eigentlich ganz cool, wenn es für alle Situationen irgendwie was offizielles gibt."
>
> Translation: "I would actually find it pretty nice if there were something official for all situations."
Code: #code/no-official-cost-template

> "Also brauche ich eine Multiplied Body Review Fee, brauche ich eine Certification Review Fee oder in welchen Fällen ... muss da was berechnet werden ... dann merke ich einfach auch oft, das wissen beide einfach selber nicht und dann entscheiden sie einfach irgendwas."
>
> Translation: "Do I need a Multiplied Body Review Fee, do I need a Certification Review Fee, or in which cases ... does something need to be calculated ... I often notice that neither of them actually knows themselves, and then they just decide something."
Code: #code/fee-type-ambiguity

> "Ich vermute, irgendjemand hat sich ja das mal ausgedacht mit dieser Fee ... aber es ist wirklich nicht so, dass die Regeln klar sind."
>
> Translation: "I assume someone came up with this fee at some point ... but it's really not the case that the rules are clear."
Code: #code/fee-type-ambiguity

> "Aber tatsächlich haben die sich noch nie auf diese Fees gestürzt. ... Wo sie dann irgendwie nachhaken, ist dann wie viele, also ist das gerechtfertigt, dass so und so viele Stunden dafür veranschlagt sind."
>
> Translation: "But they've actually never pounced on these fees. ... Where they do sometimes push back is on how many hours are being budgeted for it."
Code: #code/fee-type-ambiguity

> "Also wenn wir jetzt sagen, er möchte ein MDR-Zertifikat neu haben ... müssen wir halt alles was auf dieser Appendix ABC ist ... angucken. Wenn er da 100 Artikel schon reinschreibt, zwar alle unter den gleichen Code, aber dann verschiedene Basic UDIs ... dann müssten wir halt schon wieder vielleicht uns mehrere angucken."
>
> Translation: "If he wants a new MDR certificate ... we have to look at everything that's on this Appendix ABC ... If he already lists 100 articles, all under the same code but with different Basic UDIs ... then we might have to look at several of them again."
Code: #code/cost-timeline-calculation-basis

> "Nee, tatsächlich wär das eigentlich gar nichts. Er müsste es uns einfach nur mitteilen. Und dann könnten wir im nächsten Zyklus, wenn wir uns das wieder samplen, könnten wir uns das wieder samplen."
>
> Translation: "No, actually that wouldn't be anything [additional]. He'd just have to notify us. And then in the next sampling cycle, we could sample it again."
Code: #code/sampling-rule-flexibility

> "Also sagen wir mal diese EMDN-Codes und diese MDA-Codes und MDN-Codes, die sind ja im Endeffekt auch tatsächlich noch für TÜV ... aber die Kunden, die ich habe, egal ob groß oder klein, also die können damit schon was anfangen."
>
> Translation: "Well, let's say these EMDN codes and MDA codes and MDN codes are, in the end, really still for the certification body [TÜV] itself ... but the customers I have, regardless of whether large or small, can already do something with them."
Code: #code/customer-code-awareness

> "Das wär tatsächlich ganz cool, ehrlich gesagt. Ich habe das nicht. ... im Endeffekt einfach nur, wo ich auch wirklich so Kleinigkeiten einfach reinschreibe ... das wäre schon tatsächlich cool, wenn das irgendwie übersichtlicher dargestellt werden könnte."
>
> Translation: "That would actually be pretty cool, honestly. I don't have that. ... in the end it's just where I write down small things ... it would actually be cool if that could be displayed in a clearer way."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Also ich habe jetzt hier zum Beispiel 'ne Liste, wo ich erstmal verschiedene Reiter habe ... und im Endeffekt ist hier klar, okay, das ist das Enddate von der dritten Runde ... ich schreibe mir da tatsächlich irgendwie auch auf ... damit ich nicht in Tagen wieder denke, was ist denn da der letzte Stand."
>
> Translation: "So I have a list here, for example, where I have different tabs ... and in the end it's clear here, OK, that's the end date of the third round ... I actually write it down there ... so that I don't again spend days wondering what the last status was."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Meistens schreibe ich mir da irgendwie noch dazu, irgendwie via Mail oder via UCI, weil das ist jetzt auch immer, dann denkt man, hey, ich bin gar keine Mail dazu. ... diese zwei Kanäle sind auch manchmal eher ein Hindernis, dass man das irgendwie nachverfolgen kann."
>
> Translation: "Usually I also note down whether it was via email or via UCI, because otherwise you think, hey, I don't have an email about that. ... these two channels are also sometimes more of an obstacle to being able to track it."
Code: #code/dual-channel-communication-friction

> "Tatsächlich finde ich es sonst eigentlich bei UCI jetzt ganz gut, dass wenn man sich daran hält, dass man dann pro Projekt halt die Kommunikation einfach da nachvollziehen kann, ich erst irgendwie 1000 Mails nach."
>
> Translation: "Actually, otherwise I find UCI quite good, in that if you stick to it, you can trace the communication per project there, rather than searching through a thousand emails."
Code: #code/dual-channel-communication-friction

> "Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet, dass ich irgendwie sehe, was ist gerade meine Aufgabe ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne ... dass man nicht manuell da immer jedem anderen hinterherlaufen muss."
>
> Translation: "What I would actually want ... is something that really depicts this workflow, so I can see what my current task is ... whose turn it is, so to speak ... so that you don't have to manually chase after everyone who should currently have the ball."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Wäre halt richtig cool, wenn das irgendwie alles nicht in Excel wäre, sondern die Informationen in Daten irgendwie gespeichert wäre, da Cross-Checks automatisch möglich sind, bestimmte Sachen gar nicht einzugeben sind durch den Kunden, weil das nicht geht regulatorischer aus regulatorischer Sicht."
>
> Translation: "It would be really cool if all of this weren't in Excel, but the information were stored as data instead, so that cross-checks are automatically possible, and certain things simply can't be entered by the customer because it's not allowed from a regulatory point of view."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "Vielleicht geht das dann ja auch aus der bestehenden Appendix ABC-Liste, dass man das hochlädt ... ob die da eine Live-Schnittstelle irgendwie brauchen."
>
> Translation: "Maybe that could also work from the existing Appendix ABC list, that you upload it ... whether they need some kind of live interface [to SAP]."
Code: #code/sap-interface-idea

> "Ja, das wäre natürlich auch eine Möglichkeit, dass der Appendix ABC ... die Daten von EUDAMED kommen. ... ich bin aber zu wenig drin, was für Daten da jetzt wirklich in EUDAMED noch drin sind, die vielleicht wir unbedingt bräuchten."
>
> Translation: "Yes, that would of course also be a possibility, that the Appendix ABC's data comes from EUDAMED [European Database on Medical Devices]. ... but I'm not familiar enough with what data is actually in EUDAMED that we would necessarily need."
Code: #code/eudamed-interface-idea

> "Könnte ich mir jetzt vielleicht auch vorstellen, dass die da mehr durchgeleitet werden ... hier was möchtest du machen ... dann brauchen Sie vielleicht gar kein Formblatt mehr ausfüllen ... vielleicht schon die Infos eingetragen sind, die Sie vorher eingegeben haben."
>
> Translation: "I could also imagine that they get guided through it more ... here, what do you want to do ... then maybe they wouldn't need to fill out a form at all anymore ... maybe the information they entered before is already filled in."
Code: #code/guided-intake-vision

## Theme Match

`02_themes` contains 3 confirmed themes at the start of this interview:
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, and `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`. Every new
P03 code was compared against these, plus against the standalone preliminary pain points in
`03_pains` from P01 and P02.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (3rd interview):** P03's own informally-maintained
  Excel status list and her "wo liegt der Ball" (whose turn is it) wish directly confirm
  [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]] from a
  third distinct role/segment. Per the sample-relative check in [[Definitions]] ("Confidence"),
  3 of 3 interviews processed so far now support this mechanism directly and consistently, so
  confidence is raised from Medium to High.
- **Direct confirmation, new theme promoted from a P01 standalone pain point:** P03's
  statements on Appendix ABC data quality (customers not submitting or updating Appendix ABC
  correctly, invalid intended-user combinations only caught mid-assessment, slow ~5-week
  customer correction cycles) directly confirm the same underlying mechanism as the P01 pain
  point [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (Appendix ABC being relied on as authoritative despite being error-prone). This pain point is
  promoted to theme [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]].
- **Contradicting evidence on an existing theme:** P03 states that, in her experience, her
  customers — large or small — already understand and can work with regulatory codes, in
  tension with [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
  (based on P01/P02 evidence that customers frequently misjudge code relevance). This is
  recorded as Contradicting Evidence on that theme rather than treated as a fresh confirmation
  or a rebuttal; interview count is not increased since P03 does not directly report customers
  guessing codes. A plausible explanation is a role-based difference in exposure: P03 is less
  involved in Application-stage code review than P01/P02.
- **Related pattern, not merged:** P03's dual-channel (email/UCI) communication-tracking
  friction is adjacent to, but not the same specific mechanism as, the P02 pain point
  [[../03_pains/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
  (P02: no project-object link, requiring manual reference numbers; P03: two disconnected
  channels making it hard to know where the current information lives). Logged as related
  evidence; that pain point's interview count is not increased.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/timeline-update-ownership-gap`,
  `#code/no-official-cost-template`, `#code/fee-type-ambiguity`, and
  `#code/form-field-entry-errors` describe mechanisms not evidenced in P01 or P02, so they
  remain standalone preliminary pain points pending a second interview (see
  [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).

> "Tatsächlich ist es mir über UCI lieber, eigentlich aus dem Grund, weil ich klar dann irgendwie mit dieser Anfrage arbeiten muss, aber die ersten Schritte, die wir machen, ist eigentlich, dass der PC ein Projekt anlegt ... bei U.C.I. ist eigentlich so 'n bisschen klarer die Verantwortung, O.K., jetzt ist die P.C. am Zug."
>
> Translation: "I actually prefer it via UCI, really because the responsibility is a bit clearer: OK, now it's the Project Coordinator's turn. Via email, if they forget to CC the Project Coordinator, I have to manually forward it and actively ask them to open a project."
Code: #code/intake-channel-responsibility-clarity

> "Jetzt ist es tatsächlich in aktueller Fall so, dass ich das dann irgendwie nicht mehr öffnen konnte, aber da habe ich jetzt schon mal an UCI-Support geschrieben."
>
> Translation: "Right now it's actually the case that I could no longer open it, but I've already written to UCI support about that."
Code: #code/tool-bug-in-progress

> "Ja, also gerade bei den Formblättern, stellen die sich manchmal schlauer und mal dümmer an, da irgendwie die Häkchen richtig zu machen oder das auszufüllen ... das gibt es schon öfter mal dass ich das wieder zurückschicke."
>
> Translation: "Yes, especially with the forms, they sometimes manage better and sometimes worse to get the checkboxes right or fill it in correctly ... it happens fairly often that I send it back."
Code: #code/form-field-entry-errors

> "Sagen wir mal zu 90 Prozent muss zu dieser Application gehört auch dieser Appendix ABC dazu. ... das ist meistens nicht so, dass sie da überhaupt den Appendix ABC mitschicken, geschweige denn da schon die Änderung irgendwie drin haben, weil den Augenblick so ganz bewusst ist, wann ändere ich diesen Appendix ABC?"
>
> Translation: "About 90 percent of the time, this Appendix ABC has to be part of the Application. ... it's usually not the case that they even send the Appendix ABC along, let alone already have the change reflected in it, because it's often not clear at what point the Appendix ABC should be changed."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "Also einerseits dann mit den Daten, die sie dann haben ... Also immer dieser Cross-Check ... da verliere ich glaube ich am meisten Zeit ... es gibt hier in einer Basic UDI verschiedene intended users. Dürfen sie eigentlich gar nicht haben. ... dann müssen die sich erstmal fünf Wochen absprechen, dass sie irgendwie dann wieder eine neue Version schicken."
>
> Translation: "On one hand with the data they have ... always this cross-check ... I think that's where I lose the most time ... there are different intended users on one Basic UDI here. They aren't actually allowed to have that. ... then they first have to coordinate among themselves for five weeks before sending a new version."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "Wir haben immer nur ein Appendix ABC. ... Wenn er eins davon ändern möchte, dann schickt er alles noch mal quasi und die eine Zeile ist geändert."
>
> Translation: "We only ever have one Appendix ABC. ... If he wants to change one of them, he sends everything again, essentially, with the one row changed."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-versioning-context

> "Heißt in dieser Application ID, oder in dieser Application steht so ein bisschen beschrieben, was gemacht wird ... aber ihr habt Recht, so genau Wissen weiß ich nicht. Das sollte sich dann im Idealfall aus dem Formblatt von der Application ergeben."
>
> Translation: "So in this Application ID, or in this Application, there's a bit of a description of what's being done ... but you're right, I don't know exactly. That should ideally be derivable from the Application's form."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-versioning-context

> "Ja, also generell würde ich Rolle von der oder dem PC zu definieren, dass die wirklich in PSE die ganzen Timelines pflegen dafür zuständig sind ... aber jetzt für die Projekte von meinen Kunden, da also im Endeffekt, wenn ich hier nicht da regelmäßig schreibe ... passiert da nichts."
>
> Translation: "Well, generally I would define the PC's [Project Coordinator's] role as being responsible for maintaining all the timelines in PSE ... but for my customers' projects, if I don't write there regularly, nothing happens."
Code: #code/timeline-update-ownership-gap

> "Das ist so, wo ich denke, das ist so ein bisschen Doppelarbeit ... wenn ich die Rechte hätte, in der Zeit, wo ich ihr dann noch mal die E-Mail schreibe, dass ihr die Timeline anfasst ... könnt ihr es einfach direkt selber updaten. ... Also entweder die machen es selbstständig oder uns werden die Rechte gegeben, da auch was anzupassen."
>
> Translation: "That's where I think it's a bit of duplicate work ... if I had the rights, in the time it takes me to write an email asking them to touch the timeline ... you could just update it directly yourselves. ... So either they do it on their own, or we get the rights to adjust it too."
Code: #code/timeline-update-ownership-gap

> "Bei mir ist es auch oft so, dass ich irgendwie Supplier Audit kalkuliere, da kann ich mir wieder anscheinend alles aus dem Daumen schütteln ... Genauso ist es tatsächlich bei Change Notifications, da gibt es nicht so eine richtig offizielle Vorlage. ... das ist nichts, was in ROXPA ist und so ein bisschen inoffiziell läuft."
>
> Translation: "For me it's often the case that I sort of calculate a Supplier Audit out of thin air ... it's the same for Change Notifications, there isn't really an official template. ... it's not in ROXPA [the official process documentation system] and runs a bit unofficially."
Code: #code/no-official-cost-template

> "Fände tatsächlich eigentlich ganz cool, wenn es für alle Situationen irgendwie was offizielles gibt."
>
> Translation: "I would actually find it pretty nice if there were something official for all situations."
Code: #code/no-official-cost-template

> "Also brauche ich eine Multiplied Body Review Fee, brauche ich eine Certification Review Fee oder in welchen Fällen ... muss da was berechnet werden ... dann merke ich einfach auch oft, das wissen beide einfach selber nicht und dann entscheiden sie einfach irgendwas."
>
> Translation: "Do I need a Multiplied Body Review Fee, do I need a Certification Review Fee, or in which cases ... does something need to be calculated ... I often notice that neither of them actually knows themselves, and then they just decide something."
Code: #code/fee-type-ambiguity

> "Ich vermute, irgendjemand hat sich ja das mal ausgedacht mit dieser Fee ... aber es ist wirklich nicht so, dass die Regeln klar sind."
>
> Translation: "I assume someone came up with this fee at some point ... but it's really not the case that the rules are clear."
Code: #code/fee-type-ambiguity

> "Aber tatsächlich haben die sich noch nie auf diese Fees gestürzt. ... Wo sie dann irgendwie nachhaken, ist dann wie viele, also ist das gerechtfertigt, dass so und so viele Stunden dafür veranschlagt sind."
>
> Translation: "But they've actually never pounced on these fees. ... Where they do sometimes push back is on how many hours are being budgeted for it."
Code: #code/fee-type-ambiguity

> "Also wenn wir jetzt sagen, er möchte ein MDR-Zertifikat neu haben ... müssen wir halt alles was auf dieser Appendix ABC ist ... angucken. Wenn er da 100 Artikel schon reinschreibt, zwar alle unter den gleichen Code, aber dann verschiedene Basic UDIs ... dann müssten wir halt schon wieder vielleicht uns mehrere angucken."
>
> Translation: "If he wants a new MDR certificate ... we have to look at everything that's on this Appendix ABC ... If he already lists 100 articles, all under the same code but with different Basic UDIs ... then we might have to look at several of them again."
Code: #code/cost-timeline-calculation-basis

> "Nee, tatsächlich wär das eigentlich gar nichts. Er müsste es uns einfach nur mitteilen. Und dann könnten wir im nächsten Zyklus, wenn wir uns das wieder samplen, könnten wir uns das wieder samplen."
>
> Translation: "No, actually that wouldn't be anything [additional]. He'd just have to notify us. And then in the next sampling cycle, we could sample it again."
Code: #code/sampling-rule-flexibility

> "Also sagen wir mal diese EMDN-Codes und diese MDA-Codes und MDN-Codes, die sind ja im Endeffekt auch tatsächlich noch für TÜV ... aber die Kunden, die ich habe, egal ob groß oder klein, also die können damit schon was anfangen."
>
> Translation: "Well, let's say these EMDN codes and MDA codes and MDN codes are, in the end, really still for the certification body [TÜV] itself ... but the customers I have, regardless of whether large or small, can already do something with them."
Code: #code/customer-code-awareness

> "Das wär tatsächlich ganz cool, ehrlich gesagt. Ich habe das nicht. ... im Endeffekt einfach nur, wo ich auch wirklich so Kleinigkeiten einfach reinschreibe ... das wäre schon tatsächlich cool, wenn das irgendwie übersichtlicher dargestellt werden könnte."
>
> Translation: "That would actually be pretty cool, honestly. I don't have that. ... in the end it's just where I write down small things ... it would actually be cool if that could be displayed in a clearer way."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Also ich habe jetzt hier zum Beispiel 'ne Liste, wo ich erstmal verschiedene Reiter habe ... und im Endeffekt ist hier klar, okay, das ist das Enddate von der dritten Runde ... ich schreibe mir da tatsächlich irgendwie auch auf ... damit ich nicht in Tagen wieder denke, was ist denn da der letzte Stand."
>
> Translation: "So I have a list here, for example, where I have different tabs ... and in the end it's clear here, OK, that's the end date of the third round ... I actually write it down there ... so that I don't again spend days wondering what the last status was."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Meistens schreibe ich mir da irgendwie noch dazu, irgendwie via Mail oder via UCI, weil das ist jetzt auch immer, dann denkt man, hey, ich bin gar keine Mail dazu. ... diese zwei Kanäle sind auch manchmal eher ein Hindernis, dass man das irgendwie nachverfolgen kann."
>
> Translation: "Usually I also note down whether it was via email or via UCI, because otherwise you think, hey, I don't have an email about that. ... these two channels are also sometimes more of an obstacle to being able to track it."
Code: #code/dual-channel-communication-friction

> "Tatsächlich finde ich es sonst eigentlich bei UCI jetzt ganz gut, dass wenn man sich daran hält, dass man dann pro Projekt halt die Kommunikation einfach da nachvollziehen kann, ich erst irgendwie 1000 Mails nach."
>
> Translation: "Actually, otherwise I find UCI quite good, in that if you stick to it, you can trace the communication per project there, rather than searching through a thousand emails."
Code: #code/dual-channel-communication-friction

> "Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet, dass ich irgendwie sehe, was ist gerade meine Aufgabe ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne ... dass man nicht manuell da immer jedem anderen hinterherlaufen muss."
>
> Translation: "What I would actually want ... is something that really depicts this workflow, so I can see what my current task is ... whose turn it is, so to speak ... so that you don't have to manually chase after everyone who should currently have the ball."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Wäre halt richtig cool, wenn das irgendwie alles nicht in Excel wäre, sondern die Informationen in Daten irgendwie gespeichert wäre, da Cross-Checks automatisch möglich sind, bestimmte Sachen gar nicht einzugeben sind durch den Kunden, weil das nicht geht regulatorischer aus regulatorischer Sicht."
>
> Translation: "It would be really cool if all of this weren't in Excel, but the information were stored as data instead, so that cross-checks are automatically possible, and certain things simply can't be entered by the customer because it's not allowed from a regulatory point of view."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "Vielleicht geht das dann ja auch aus der bestehenden Appendix ABC-Liste, dass man das hochlädt ... ob die da eine Live-Schnittstelle irgendwie brauchen."
>
> Translation: "Maybe that could also work from the existing Appendix ABC list, that you upload it ... whether they need some kind of live interface [to SAP]."
Code: #code/sap-interface-idea

> "Ja, das wäre natürlich auch eine Möglichkeit, dass der Appendix ABC ... die Daten von EUDAMED kommen. ... ich bin aber zu wenig drin, was für Daten da jetzt wirklich in EUDAMED noch drin sind, die vielleicht wir unbedingt bräuchten."
>
> Translation: "Yes, that would of course also be a possibility, that the Appendix ABC's data comes from EUDAMED [European Database on Medical Devices]. ... but I'm not familiar enough with what data is actually in EUDAMED that we would necessarily need."
Code: #code/eudamed-interface-idea

> "Könnte ich mir jetzt vielleicht auch vorstellen, dass die da mehr durchgeleitet werden ... hier was möchtest du machen ... dann brauchen Sie vielleicht gar kein Formblatt mehr ausfüllen ... vielleicht schon die Infos eingetragen sind, die Sie vorher eingegeben haben."
>
> Translation: "I could also imagine that they get guided through it more ... here, what do you want to do ... then maybe they wouldn't need to fill out a form at all anymore ... maybe the information they entered before is already filled in."
Code: #code/guided-intake-vision
sections.Theme Match:
`02_themes` contains 3 confirmed themes at the start of this interview:
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, and `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`. Every new
P03 code was compared against these, plus against the standalone preliminary pain points in
`03_pains` from P01 and P02.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (3rd interview):** P03's own informally-maintained
  Excel status list and her "wo liegt der Ball" (whose turn is it) wish directly confirm
  [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]] from a
  third distinct role/segment. Per the sample-relative check in [[Definitions]] ("Confidence"),
  3 of 3 interviews processed so far now support this mechanism directly and consistently, so
  confidence is raised from Medium to High.
- **Direct confirmation, new theme promoted from a P01 standalone pain point:** P03's
  statements on Appendix ABC data quality (customers not submitting or updating Appendix ABC
  correctly, invalid intended-user combinations only caught mid-assessment, slow ~5-week
  customer correction cycles) directly confirm the same underlying mechanism as the P01 pain
  point [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (Appendix ABC being relied on as authoritative despite being error-prone). This pain point is
  promoted to theme [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]].
- **Contradicting evidence on an existing theme:** P03 states that, in her experience, her
  customers — large or small — already understand and can work with regulatory codes, in
  tension with [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
  (based on P01/P02 evidence that customers frequently misjudge code relevance). This is
  recorded as Contradicting Evidence on that theme rather than treated as a fresh confirmation
  or a rebuttal; interview count is not increased since P03 does not directly report customers
  guessing codes. A plausible explanation is a role-based difference in exposure: P03 is less
  involved in Application-stage code review than P01/P02.
- **Related pattern, not merged:** P03's dual-channel (email/UCI) communication-tracking
  friction is adjacent to, but not the same specific mechanism as, the P02 pain point
  [[../03_pains/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
  (P02: no project-object link, requiring manual reference numbers; P03: two disconnected
  channels making it hard to know where the current information lives). Logged as related
  evidence; that pain point's interview count is not increased.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/timeline-update-ownership-gap`,
  `#code/no-official-cost-template`, `#code/fee-type-ambiguity`, and
  `#code/form-field-entry-errors` describe mechanisms not evidenced in P01 or P02, so they
  remain standalone preliminary pain points pending a second interview (see
  [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).

Ich vermute, irgendjemand hat sich ja das mal ausgedacht mit dieser Fee ... aber es ist wirklich nicht so, dass die Regeln klar sind.

Aber tatsächlich haben die sich noch nie auf diese Fees gestürzt. ... Wo sie dann irgendwie nachhaken, ist dann wie viele, also ist das gerechtfertigt, dass so und so viele Stunden dafür veranschlagt sind.

Also wenn wir jetzt sagen, er möchte ein MDR-Zertifikat neu haben ... müssen wir halt alles was auf dieser Appendix ABC ist ... angucken. Wenn er da 100 Artikel schon reinschreibt, zwar alle unter den gleichen Code, aber dann verschiedene Basic UDIs ... dann müssten wir halt schon wieder vielleicht uns mehrere angucken.
Nee, tatsächlich wär das eigentlich gar nichts. Er müsste es uns einfach nur mitteilen. Und dann könnten wir im nächsten Zyklus, wenn wir uns das wieder samplen, könnten wir uns das wieder samplen.

Also sagen wir mal diese EMDN-Codes und diese MDA-Codes und MDN-Codes, die sind ja im Endeffekt auch tatsächlich noch für TÜV ... aber die Kunden, die ich habe, egal ob groß oder klein, also die können damit schon was anfangen.

Das wär tatsächlich ganz cool, ehrlich gesagt. Ich habe das nicht. ... im Endeffekt einfach nur, wo ich auch wirklich so Kleinigkeiten einfach reinschreibe ... das wäre schon tatsächlich cool, wenn das irgendwie übersichtlicher dargestellt werden könnte.

Also ich habe jetzt hier zum Beispiel 'ne Liste, wo ich erstmal verschiedene Reiter habe ... und im Endeffekt ist hier klar, okay, das ist das Enddate von der dritten Runde ... ich schreibe mir da tatsächlich irgendwie auch auf ... damit ich nicht in Tagen wieder denke, was ist denn da der letzte Stand.

Meistens schreibe ich mir da irgendwie noch dazu, irgendwie via Mail oder via UCI, weil das ist jetzt auch immer, dann denkt man, hey, ich bin gar keine Mail dazu. ... diese zwei Kanäle sind auch manchmal eher ein Hindernis, dass man das irgendwie nachverfolgen kann.

Tatsächlich finde ich es sonst eigentlich bei UCI jetzt ganz gut, dass wenn man sich daran hält, dass man dann pro Projekt halt die Kommunikation einfach da nachvollziehen kann, ich erst irgendwie 1000 Mails nach.

Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet, dass ich irgendwie sehe, was ist gerade meine Aufgabe ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne ... dass man nicht manuell da immer jedem anderen hinterherlaufen muss.

Wäre halt richtig cool, wenn das irgendwie alles nicht in Excel wäre, sondern die Informationen in Daten irgendwie gespeichert wäre, da Cross-Checks automatisch möglich sind, bestimmte Sachen gar nicht einzugeben sind durch den Kunden, weil das nicht geht regulatorischer aus regulatorischer Sicht.
Vielleicht geht das dann ja auch aus der bestehenden Appendix ABC-Liste, dass man das hochlädt ... ob die da eine Live-Schnittstelle irgendwie brauchen.

Ja, das wäre natürlich auch eine Möglichkeit, dass der Appendix ABC ... die Daten von EUDAMED kommen. ... ich bin aber zu wenig drin, was für Daten da jetzt wirklich in EUDAMED noch drin sind, die vielleicht wir unbedingt bräuchten.

Könnte ich mir jetzt vielleicht auch vorstellen, dass die da mehr durchgeleitet werden ... hier was möchtest du machen ... dann brauchen Sie vielleicht gar kein Formblatt mehr ausfüllen ... vielleicht schon die Infos eingetragen sind, die Sie vorher eingegeben haben.

# Interview: P04

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- The participant ("Andrea") has worked at the company since 2023 as a Lead Auditor and
  Customer Specialist. She also holds authorization for packaging and sterilization audits
  (ethylene oxide and steam) for low-risk devices, and for Technical Documentation (TD)
  assessment for one product code, excluding clinical data assessment.
- She describes her experience with the internal audit-planning tool ("MACE Audit") as still
  partial; she started using it in July and expects roughly a year before feeling fully
  comfortable with multi-task project setup.
- The interviewer clarifies early on that the discussion should focus on the new "MACE
  Application" software (the end-to-end customer request/application/assessment/certification
  platform being designed), not the existing MACE Audit tool, though Audit data will feed into
  it.
- She has 3-4 MDR (Medical Device Regulation) customers directly and other customers under MD
  support/ISO; she is based in Italy.
- Tone was reflective and detailed; she proactively screen-shared a regional, Italy-specific
  planning tool ("MITAP") she uses for audit scheduling.
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed.

## Meaning Units and Codes

I have also authorization for packaging and sterilization for for low risk devices for ethylene oxide and stim sterilization and for one code as a technical documentation assessor without clinical data assessment."

That is quite complicated. ... Probably, yes, most critical could be assessment left behind because they are most difficult to be, let's say, taken by the assessor because most part of the assessment have been done. ... probably the best would be yes a call, a call just I mean the quickest way would be a call just to show how to where to link how the process it is."

## Theme Match

`02_themes` contains 4 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P03):
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`, and
`Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone
document`. Every new P04 code was compared against these, plus against the standalone
preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P03.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (4th interview):** P04's description of the
  project-status/planning gap — no company-provided tool exists for tracking Technical
  Documentation (TD) assessment or Change Notification progress (only a personal, regional
  planning tool for audits, which she expects may be discontinued), and the Assessment Plan
  Cloud (APC) tool being "static" rather than showing live deficiency-report status — directly
  confirms [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]
  for a fourth distinct interview. Confidence remains High (4 of 4 interviews now, 100% ≥ 25%
  sample-relative threshold).
- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (3rd interview) — confidence raised:** P04's
  description of Appendix ABC as the most critical and time-consuming customer document,
  scaling sharply in review burden with SKU/Basic UDI (Unique Device Identification) count,
  and requiring full manual re-verification on every new version because of customer data
  errors, directly confirms
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  for a third interview (P01, P03, P04). Per the sample-relative check in [[Definitions]] (3 of
  4 interviews processed so far = 75%, above the 25% threshold; repetition now at the typical
  3+ level), Confidence is raised from Medium to High.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/deficiency-report-reminder-gap`,
  `#code/conflict-of-interest-manual-check`, and `#code/archival-handover-incompleteness`
  describe mechanisms not evidenced in P01-P03, so they remain standalone preliminary pain
  points pending a second interview (see [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).
- **No match, background/out of scope:** `#code/customer-service-awareness-gap` and
  `#code/objectivity-perception-external` describe organizational/market-perception topics
  (customer awareness of the company's full service range and size; external perception of
  notified-body/laboratory-service impartiality) that are tangential to the MACE Application
  workflow-digitization scope and are not evidenced elsewhere; recorded as background only.
- **Positive pattern candidate (single interview):** `#code/mitap-audit-planning-tool-positive`
  describes a regionally-built planning tool the participant finds useful for audit
  scheduling and visual progress tracking. Below the two-interview threshold for a
  positive-pattern note; retained as a research gap.
- **Related evidence, not merged:** `#code/tool-familiarity-preference` (preference for
  building the new tool around already-used software like Outlook/Teams to reduce the
  training curve) does not match an existing pain point or theme; it is a forward-looking
  design preference rather than a description of current friction, and is logged as a
  candidate idea rather than a new artifact.

sections.Theme Match:
`02_themes` contains 4 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P03):
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`, and
`Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone
document`. Every new P04 code was compared against these, plus against the standalone
preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P03.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (4th interview):** P04's description of the
  project-status/planning gap — no company-provided tool exists for tracking Technical
  Documentation (TD) assessment or Change Notification progress (only a personal, regional
  planning tool for audits, which she expects may be discontinued), and the Assessment Plan
  Cloud (APC) tool being "static" rather than showing live deficiency-report status — directly
  confirms [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]
  for a fourth distinct interview. Confidence remains High (4 of 4 interviews now, 100% ≥ 25%
  sample-relative threshold).
- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (3rd interview) — confidence raised:** P04's
  description of Appendix ABC as the most critical and time-consuming customer document,
  scaling sharply in review burden with SKU/Basic UDI (Unique Device Identification) count,
  and requiring full manual re-verification on every new version because of customer data
  errors, directly confirms
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  for a third interview (P01, P03, P04). Per the sample-relative check in [[Definitions]] (3 of
  4 interviews processed so far = 75%, above the 25% threshold; repetition now at the typical
  3+ level), Confidence is raised from Medium to High.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/deficiency-report-reminder-gap`,
  `#code/conflict-of-interest-manual-check`, and `#code/archival-handover-incompleteness`
  describe mechanisms not evidenced in P01-P03, so they remain standalone preliminary pain
  points pending a second interview (see [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).
- **No match, background/out of scope:** `#code/customer-service-awareness-gap` and
  `#code/objectivity-perception-external` describe organizational/market-perception topics
  (customer awareness of the company's full service range and size; external perception of
  notified-body/laboratory-service impartiality) that are tangential to the MACE Application
  workflow-digitization scope and are not evidenced elsewhere; recorded as background only.
- **Positive pattern candidate (single interview):** `#code/mitap-audit-planning-tool-positive`
  describes a regionally-built planning tool the participant finds useful for audit
  scheduling and visual progress tracking. Below the two-interview threshold for a
  positive-pattern note; retained as a research gap.
- **Related evidence, not merged:** `#code/tool-familiarity-preference` (preference for
  building the new tool around already-used software like Outlook/Teams to reduce the
  training curve) does not match an existing pain point or theme; it is a forward-looking
  design preference rather than a description of current friction, and is logged as a
  candidate idea rather than a new artifact.

notes.body:
<!-- Write analysis prose in neutral third-person English. Keep participant quotes verbatim. -->

# Interview: P05

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- The participant ("Kat") works in SPOS (Special Operations and Support) within MHS
  (Medical Health Services), a US-based team responsible for onboarding brand-new
  certification clients (companies not previously certified with any Quality Management
  System, or QMS).
- Her role begins after Sales has secured client agreement to a quotation; for International
  Vigilance and Post-Market Surveillance regulation clients (IVDR/MDR), she is involved
  earlier to help Sales generate the technical quote itself. She is the "technical piece" of
  the onboarding project team (alongside a Relationship Manager and a Project Coordinator),
  and identifies as an auditor rather than a Technical Documentation (TD) reviewer.
- Her scope covers: collecting application review documents from the client (including the
  Appendix ABC), submitting them to the cert body for Application Review, generating internal
  planning documents (assessment plan, sampling plan for regulation clients, Application
  Management Checklist), scheduling and personally conducting the client's first audit cycle
  as lead auditor, and writing the final audit/certification submission package. Once the
  certificate is issued, she performs a formal handoff to Operations and typically has no
  further contact with the client.
- This segment is new relative to P01-P04: it is scoped specifically to first-time client
  onboarding (a bounded lifecycle ending in handoff), not ongoing account management.
- The interviewer clarifies the scope is the new, unrelated "MACE Application" software (the
  end-to-end request-to-certification platform), not the existing "MACE Audit" tool, though
  Audit data will eventually feed into it.
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "So yes, I work for SPOS, which is Special Operations and Support. ... one of our primary functions is ... to onboard new clients. ... Sales can handle ISO and MDSAP quoting themselves, however. So after a client has agreed to the initial quote, regardless of what scheme it's for, that's when they kind of get formally passed to SPOS ... a relationship manager, a project coordinator, and then SPOS themselves, which is me, is the project manager or technical expert."
Code: #code/onboarding-role-scope-handoff

> "And then after the audit is over ... I write the audit report. ... Submit that to the cert body ... And once all of those boxes are checked ... they issue a certificate and then I do a formal handoff to operations and then I may never see that client again."
Code: #code/onboarding-role-scope-handoff

> "For regulation clients, I come in a little bit earlier because I'm helping them generate the quote because IVDR quotes are a little more technically involved."
Code: #code/onboarding-role-scope-handoff

`02_themes` contains 4 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P04):

document`. Every new P05 code was compared against these, plus against all standalone
preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P04.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened, confidence raised (3rd interview):** P05

  producing incorrect code sets that staff must catch and correct. This directly confirms

sections.Context (Step 1 - before coding):
- The participant ("Kat") works in SPOS (Special Operations and Support) within MHS
  (Medical Health Services), a US-based team responsible for onboarding brand-new
  certification clients (companies not previously certified with any Quality Management
  System, or QMS).
- Her role begins after Sales has secured client agreement to a quotation; for International
  Vigilance and Post-Market Surveillance regulation clients (IVDR/MDR), she is involved
  earlier to help Sales generate the technical quote itself. She is the "technical piece" of
  the onboarding project team (alongside a Relationship Manager and a Project Coordinator),
  and identifies as an auditor rather than a Technical Documentation (TD) reviewer.
- Her scope covers: collecting application review documents from the client (including the
  Appendix ABC), submitting them to the cert body for Application Review, generating internal
  planning documents (assessment plan, sampling plan for regulation clients, Application
  Management Checklist), scheduling and personally conducting the client's first audit cycle
  as lead auditor, and writing the final audit/certification submission package. Once the
  certificate is issued, she performs a formal handoff to Operations and typically has no
  further contact with the client.
- This segment is new relative to P01-P04: it is scoped specifically to first-time client
  onboarding (a bounded lifecycle ending in handoff), not ongoing account management.
- The interviewer clarifies the scope is the new, unrelated "MACE Application" software (the
  end-to-end request-to-certification platform), not the existing "MACE Audit" tool, though
  Audit data will eventually feed into it.
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed.

sections.Theme Match:
`02_themes` contains 4 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P04):
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`, and
`Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone
document`. Every new P05 code was compared against these, plus against all standalone
preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P04.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened, confidence raised (3rd interview):** P05
  describes clients repeatedly self-assigning EAC codes (e.g. "plastics," "metals") based on a
  superficial material match rather than the code's actual manufacturing-technology scope,
  producing incorrect code sets that staff must catch and correct. This directly confirms
  [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
  for a third distinct interview (P01, P02, P05). Per the sample-relative check in
  [[Definitions]] (3 of 5 interviews processed so far = 60%, above the 25% threshold;
  repetition now at the typical 3+ level; the mechanism is described consistently and
  directly), Confidence is raised from Medium to High. P03's previously logged contradicting
  evidence (her customers already understand codes) remains recorded and does not block this
  raise, since it describes a role-based difference in exposure rather than a direct
  contradiction of the mechanism itself.
- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (4th interview):** P05's description of the
  Appendix ABC document as "the crux of this entire meeting," never filled out correctly on
  the first attempt, and the single biggest source of early back-and-forth with the customer,
  directly confirms
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  for a fourth interview (P01, P03, P04, P05). Sample-relative check: 4 of 5 interviews
  (80%), well above the 25% threshold; Confidence remains High.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/critical-supplier-definition-mismatch`,
  `#code/scope-statement-formatting-difficulty`, `#code/appendix-abc-version-branching-conflict`,
  and `#code/mace-audit-broken-findings-generation` describe mechanisms not evidenced in
  P01-P04, so they remain standalone preliminary pain points pending a second interview (see
  [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).
- **Related evidence, not merged (checked against an existing standalone pain point):**
  `#code/appendix-abc-version-branching-conflict` (independently-edited auditor and TD
  reviewer copies of Appendix ABC diverging and causing rejected submissions) was compared
  against the existing P02 standalone finding
  [[../03_pains/No shared access to the current Appendix ABC version forces staff to rely on colleagues]]
  (no one-click access point to find the current version). Both concern the absence of a
  single live Appendix ABC, but describe different root process steps — retrieval at the
  start of work versus reconciliation of two independently-maintained copies at submission —
  so they are logged as related, cross-referenced findings rather than merged, per the
  same-root-process-step merge criterion in the vault instructions.
- **Related evidence, not merged:** `#code/critical-supplier-definition-mismatch` was compared
  against [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC internal redundancy across sheets produces contradictory supplier information]]
  (P02). P02's finding is about the same supplier-relevance data being duplicated and
  contradictory across sheets within one document; P05's finding is about a definitional
  mismatch (what counts as "critical") between the customer and the certification body. These
  are different mechanisms affecting related data, so a new pain point was created instead of
  merging.
- **Candidate idea convergence (no new artifact):** P05's wish for an online, jointly
  editable Appendix ABC that both internal staff and the client can see and manipulate
  converges with the same idea already logged as unvalidated under
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (P03, P04); it is now a third interview suggesting this direction, added as an extension to
  the existing candidate idea rather than a new one. P05's detailed AI-powered
  document-extraction vision (auto-populating codes, scope statement, and critical-supplier
  list from uploaded client documents) extends the existing AI-assisted code-suggestion idea
  already logged under
  [[../03_pains/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
  (P01) and the guidance-based need for code assignment (P02); logged as an extension, not a
  new theme or need.
- **Background, out of scope for a dedicated artifact:** `#code/onboarding-role-scope-handoff`,
  `#code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation`, `#code/uci-rollout-awareness-gap`, and
  `#code/no-user-consultation-before-mandatory-tool-rollout` describe segment-defining role
  context, regional/cert-body process variation, and organizational/tool-governance
  observations about the existing MACE Audit tool. These are recorded as background in the
  Topic Coverage Inventory below rather than promoted to pain points, since they do not
  describe a workflow friction that the MACE Application software under discovery would
  directly address.
- **Positive workaround, single interview (research gap):** `#code/written-correction-trail-preference`
  and `#code/standardized-document-sharing-platform-preference` describe practices the
  participant finds effective (written correction records; standardizing on one
  document-sharing platform). Below the two-interview threshold for a positive-pattern note;
  retained as research gaps.

quotes.text: So yes, I work for SPOS, which is Special Operations and Support. ... one of our primary functions is ... to onboard new clients. ... Sales can handle ISO and MDSAP quoting themselves, however. So after a client has agreed to the initial quote, regardless of what scheme it's for, that's when they kind of get formally passed to SPOS ... a relationship manager, a project coordinator, and then SPOS themselves, which is me, is the project manager or technical expert.

And then after the audit is over ... I write the audit report. ... Submit that to the cert body ... And once all of those boxes are checked ... they issue a certificate and then I do a formal handoff to operations and then I may never see that client again.
For regulation clients, I come in a little bit earlier because I'm helping them generate the quote because IVDR quotes are a little more technically involved.

We have ISO 1345 and we have ISO 9001. ... if somebody comes to us seeking a 1345 certificate, but the products they make don't qualify as medical device, we can redirect them to 9001 ... a lot of the time they didn't even realize they were different versions and then they have to figure out which one they want because we can't make that decision for them.

We have multiple versions [of Appendix ABC] depending on what their certification is ... UCB has one for their ISO MDSAP 9001 certs, and then Munich has one for their regulation and ISO certs. And I'm pretty sure there's also a UK MDR one, but I haven't seen that one.
The client's big piece of that is the Appendix ABC document, which it sounds like you've probably seen and you know how much of a bear that thing is.
I've never had a client fill it out correctly in one go. There's always something wrong with it that I have to go back to them and ask for a correction or a clarification on.

The two things I see clients struggle with the most with this document are writing their scope statement ... We have very specific rules about how that scope must be formatted ... clients still don't seem to quite be able to pair those things. Even when I specifically pointed out ... this is what a scope statement is ... some companies do pretty well, but some are definitely a struggle.

The other big one that companies struggle with is choosing their codes. ... a lot of companies will choose the EAC 14 code for plastics because of this, even because their cartridge is made of plastic. ... those codes are only for the specific manufacturing technologies that they use and most companies don't mold their own plastic cassette housings. They buy those from a supplier. ... EAC 14 plastics is not going to be applicable to them. They're not actually manufacturing the plastic.

That's applied to plastics, that's applied to metals ... realistically, especially for IBD companies, you're probably only going to have like one to three of those applicable [but] companies will pick like 6 because they'll pick like anything that might be vaguely related to their instrument or their device.

I keep getting appendix ABC files that have wrong codes in them. ... if we're talking about moving to something more like web-based ... having more like in your face instructions for some of this stuff where like right now it's on a different tab. If they never go to that tab, they're never going to see those instructions ... have it like right in front of them when they're filling in the information would help.

Do you think codes could be automatically derived from the product information?" / "I think in some cases they could. ... ask the client to put in their intended purpose for their product and then ... the system reads it, chooses what it thinks the best codes are and asks the client to verify. ... maybe it could be separated into sort of we think these codes are highly likely and we think these codes are less likely, but maybe still a possibility.

I don't think that's the best approach [to have only Tuv Sued assign codes] just because we don't know their product. They know their product. ... we're not the expert at their product because that's kind of more the TD assessor's role. But the TD assessors don't fill out this paperwork. They're not involved with the client at this stage ... I do think we really need to rely on the customer to tell us about their product because it is their product, they're the experts on it.

There's a tab in the appendix ABC for critical suppliers ... a lot of the time we'll discover at the audit that there's a company that they left off their appendix ABC that should be considered a critical supplier ... There's a definition of critical supplier that we use internally that does not necessarily match what the client may define for themselves as critical supplier. ... sometimes there's a mismatch between what they put on the appendix ABC and what we need to see ... that can go both ways, where they've left off companies that should be there and they've put too many companies on there that we don't care about.

If on the exact screen or window ... when they're filling this out, we have a definition of what it is we're looking for. Because again, all of that is kept on a separate tab right now. ... the more of that information where we can try to define what we want on the same page as where that information is input will help, I think.

One of the biggest problems we have sort of post project initiation with the appendix ABC is multiple versions of it out there. ... maybe the one I submit at the end of the audit process ... is different from the one that TD reviewers have. So then I submit version 7 ... TD reviewer did the same. They submit their own, but it's version 6, but they're not the same ... the CRT reviewer has these two appendix ABC's for the same company that are different and then they have to issue rejects to both of us and we all kind of as a collective have to figure out which one's correct.

We have long wanted sort of an online appendix ABC that both we can see and manipulate and the client can see and manipulate ... getting rid of that would be amazing." / "Basically what we're aiming for, right? So no appendix. ... Just data sets and you get input from the client and then you do stuff with the input you got and then it goes back to the client back and forth.

It kind of depends on how much of the appendix ABC is wrong. I tend to prefer to keep it through e-mail just so that ... I would want to receive something like that written down ... I don't have to remember it and I don't have to risk maybe hearing it wrong or writing it down wrong in my own notes.

I do, as I said, always offer to have a meeting with them. ... Again, clients rarely take me up on that. But yeah, I prefer to send that stuff via e-mail just so that they have it in writing. They can always go back and refer to it.
I have never used UCI, so I don't know. That is, I don't even know what the status of the general rollout of UCI in the US is.

Kind of the other big tool that's just involved in the general certification process that I use is ID Guard, which is our internal document sharing platform. ... Some clients don't like to use ID Guard. The larger ones generally will have their own setups through like SharePoint or something or Teams. I, however, don't think those work as well as ID Guard for my purposes during an audit. So I do try to like direct my clients towards ID Guard and I kind of don't really give them a choice.

Right now, it would be that we're required to use Mace Audit going forward. ... Mace audit is awful. It is unintuitive. You have to jump around to too many screens. Things are labeled in weird ways that don't make sense. There's a ... menu on the top when you're in an audit screen that ... says start to end ... You would think that ... each of those menu items is a linear progression through the audit ... No, absolutely not. You jump around all over the place.

I found out on my most recent audit last week that there's a findings screen and you can write findings from that screen. But if you do, the system will generate them wrong. There is nothing that tells you that [and] there is nothing to prevent you from doing that. But if you generate a finding from the finding screen, it'll be wrong and your output document will be wrong. And there's no way to correct it at that point.

The thing that I hate most about Mace is how much potential it has that is going unrealized right now. This should be an amazing, helpful tool for us, but it's a disaster that actually makes our jobs harder.

I have not heard a single person who actually audits say that they were consulted in any way about this platform before it was decided that it was going to be mandatory and enforced on us. I know that ... the cert body head of UCB at the time was not consulted to make sure that MACE was actually compliant with her regulatory needs, which it wasn't.

If we're talking pipe dream worlds here ... it would have to be some form of AI powered because it would have to read the client's documents and extract and interpolate information from them. ... they can put their product IFU for all their relevant products ... enter in basic information about their own company ... maybe some basic QMS documents like their quality manual, their approved supplier list. And the system could extract enough information from these documents to build a profile for the client and auto populate a lot of this stuff ... such as the critical supplier list could be pulled from their ASL. ... It can pull from their IFU what their codes probably are. It can pull from their quality manual a draft scope statement.

Honestly, having getting that information upfront and correct the first time would probably be one of the more helpful things, especially at the beginning of an entire project, because getting the appendix ABC correct is kind of the thing we go back and forth with the most early on.

Some of these clients that have never been certified before may not even have a quality manual at this point. So I don't know if we'd want to have a workaround to get started without that ... you can upload these documents here and it'll generate all this stuff for you, or you can click here and fill it out manually yourself.

If we could build in some kind of logic as just like a sanity check for the data that gets entered. ... if the client entered a code ... but we had their IFU ... and there was something about those two where it doesn't look like this code could be applicable ... to flag that somehow. ... an address validator. ... is the address they put in valid? Is it formatted correctly?

I would say ideally I would have both the option to overwrite it. And the option to flag it for the customer to review. ... sometimes it is just faster for me ... to put the information in myself, but if I don't know the correct information ... the ability to flag it and send it back to them. ... it is probably very important that we ... always have the option to overwrite anything that has been input ... Because we have to go back to the customer for everything that's just going to slow the entire process down.

From a personal preference, I would ... probably not want them to be required to approve any changes that I make. But from a regulatory perspective, it would not at all surprise me if this system ends up requiring that. ... maybe we just have a final approval, like there are certain phase gates where we can't move on until the client has given their approval to the Appendix ABC ... maybe I can't submit app review until there's an approval of the current version ... maybe I can't submit for certification review until there's an approved final version. But along the way, I don't know that having additional approvals would be helpful.

We do work with Germany sometimes if we have like a very large client ... we'll get handed the US versions of the company. ... sometimes we'll get subcontracted from Germany if it's their client, but US site, they'll want us to do the audit. That doesn't usually happen from Asia because Asia's a little more self-contained in my experience.
