notes.body:
<!-- Write analysis prose in neutral third-person English. Keep participant quotes verbatim. -->

# Interview: P06

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- The participant ("Giacomo") is based in Italy and started six years ago as a "project
  handler," a role since renamed "customer specialist." He identifies the Customer Specialist
  role as owning the technical side of a client's certification journey end to end: collecting
  information via the Appendix ABC, building the assessment plan, and planning audits and
  assessments together with the customer.
- He currently manages roughly 15 companies across different time frames, and is also a Lead
  Auditor and TD Assessor, though he frames his answers primarily from the Customer Specialist
  perspective per the interviewer's request.
- He separately holds a "SPS" (Special Process Specialist) role coordinating competencies for a
  specific topic (risk management), preparing trainings across teams — distinct from his
  day-to-day customer-facing work.
- The interviewer clarifies the discovery focus is the new, end-to-end "MACE Application"
  software, not the existing "MACE Audit" tool, and that this interview centers on the request
  phase of the customer journey.
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "I intended always the customer specialist role as the one who take care of the technical aspects of the certification. So going in a journey with the customer to allows them to have a certification and to maintain their certification. ... We are taking the information with the appendix ABC ... and with this information, we are preparing the plan that is defining all the activities that we as a customer specialist has to do together with the customer."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "For me, the problem is not that there are some missing data. ... the real challenge ... is that the information we really need are somehow hidden within a large amount of information that are not always necessary ... this creates noise. ... there is a very small subset of information that we really need to create the plan and to be able to really interact with the customer."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty

> "Typically, I manage customers that have an appendix ABC ... with at least 1000, 1500 or something like that [device entries]. ... It's not easy to manage that with a large Excel file, probably the Excel is not the right tool. ... We just need, for example, the requested certification ... which are the sites involved ... the relevant product and technology codes applied to each site ... and then some few more key details about the sterilization, packaging, reprocessing. ... when this subset is extracted, it becomes the operational interface for our activities."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty

> "In general, we are making ... there is a lot of noise ... we have to put a lot of data entries because ... data are always the same and they are very basic data. But we are copy and paste those data in a Word file, in an Excel file, in another tool that is made for planning the assessments, and in another tool that is made for the scheduling. ... we receive a request from administration or from some other colleagues asking exactly the same information ... there is not a real tool where all the information are inside and where everyone can really take the information from there."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "Since I started six years ago ... the tools were changing ... but the information I need, if I really focus on which can be the most essential information I need, those are always the same. So if I create somehow a tool that only includes inside the very needed information, it will always stay the same. So I somehow created a tool. It's not something really ... well, it's an Excel, so I know all the limitation of having an Excel, but it worked and I always fulfill this document ... to be sure that this will not change."
Code: #code/personal-tool-preserves-stable-core-dataset

> "I know that other regions, for example, in Germany, they have a customer interface. I just realized that during the meet, I asked it a little bit ... but we don't have it in Italy. So the main mean to communicate is through emails, organizing a Teams call if needed."
Code: #code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation

> "It's true that in general there are documents that always change internally in the template. So sometimes if we are in a rush, we don't have time to understand what have been changed in the template. ... we just send them the template and wait for their answer. ... it's not correct to send them a document hoping that they will be able to understand it. ... they don't even have an example on how to fulfill some roles, some entries. And so it's ... sometimes me neither. So the CS is not instructed on how to fulfill those documents."
Code: #code/template-changes-without-staff-or-customer-guidance

> "I have an image of a very complex and not easy to assess ... document where if I made a change, it's very difficult to manage. ... Sometimes I make directly modification by myself if I feel this is the best way to proceed and then I send it back to them saying this is the last update. ... Sometimes I receive the modification on the previous version."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "There are both [modifications and missing data]. ... at the very beginning with the company, there are a lot of missing information. ... when they have to fulfill the Appendix ABC for the first time, they fear the white paper, like they don't know how to fulfill it. They don't have any example and they really are frustrated to start this job."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "Now, in these days ... it's more on the appendix ... for the supplier because it's quite complex. ... I don't even know sometimes how to manage this. And yes, this is the part where I have the back and forth now in this last period in relation to the suppliers."
Code: #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

> "I have a love and hate relationship with Excel in general. ... it's like everyone knows how to use it somehow ... it's always the first tool that I address. ... you really reach the ceiling very fast when you have to manage a large amount of data ... it's not probably the right tool with this back and forth to the customer."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty

> "You mean I receive a version [conflict]? Yes, it happened quite a lot. Sometimes I also receive this document. I think it's mine somehow, so I fix some points. ... I hope to receive the modification that they did from the last I sent them. Yes, this is a problem."
Code: #code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict

> "Yes, because it's a document inside my computer and I feel it's like one of the other Excels I have because Excel is not shared with them. It's not in a cloud, so I can only use them. ... sometimes maybe you are working and you think we are aligned, but we are not because it's not shared."
Code: #code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict

> "I would see a device list ... it is shared by both, so me and them can make modifications. ... the list can automatically suggest how to fulfill the subsequent data when one input is included ... if you start including a device that is a knee implant, mostly of the information will be always the same for every knee implant."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "I would love to have something that automatically extrapolates the small dataset that we really need in our bag. ... once having this small subset clearly established, the following plan for certification can be somehow automatically generated. ... it's ideally standardizable. ... this should be to me a real relational database software in this case."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "I always gave this feedback starting many years ago when we were in Italy creating a new platform. ... we should start with having a database with the information inside once ... and then from that obtaining the assessment plan ... and then have a tool that creates a scheduling. ... right now those informations are nowhere to me ... I have to copy and paste them inside the scheduler ... and then inside the assessment plan cloud."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "The data set, including all the devices, should allow for a modification, but keeping track somehow of this modification, like somehow freezing the previous one ... For example, ... a device that is already inside the certification path ... means nothing ... this is stored, this is recorded in a history part, but then no impact. ... then maybe there is a modification that impacts ... including a new code EA14, for example, the plastic ... you have to change the plan."
Code: #code/change-impact-auto-detection-vision

> "There is a new Article 7 in the MDR that is requesting us to share a plan with the customers ... to give them the timeline for the certification. But inside these timelines, we have only a partial responsibility. ... this timeline is really long. ... we can solve this issue if we have shared timelines with the customers saying ... you will receive this audit, you will receive this assessment ... we promise you that every round will have three months. ... but then the last part depends on you."
Code: #code/final-step-timeline-unpredictability

> "If I imagine two interfaces with the customer, one is the document list, the device list ... and then it's the timelines so that they know where they are and then the clock is stopped when they are until we will not answer. ... it will be the last point, the arrival point will be delayed if they delay the answers. This will protect us. This will a little bit protect also the reviewers."
Code: #code/shared-timeline-with-clock-stop-vision

> "I have probably more the idea of an ERP, so I would not see a chat. ... Honestly, I don't see directly a tool that I would need if the information are already there."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "My focus is more on not having too many tools or like having one real database where information are there once. Because this is a source of error because you are including information in many other fields and it's super common to have that."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "I'm assigned for risk management. So I'm coordinating with other teams for this role, not really for the customer."
Code: #code/secondary-competency-role-assignment

## Theme Match

`02_themes` contains 4 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P05):
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`, and
`Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone
document`. Every new P06 code was compared against these four themes and against all
standalone preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P05.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (5th interview):** P06 confirms
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  for a fifth interview: Appendix ABC is described as complex and difficult to manage, missing
  information is common (especially at project start), and the pain point has shifted over
  time from missing EMDN (European Medical Device Nomenclature) codes on Appendix A to
  difficulty completing the supplier information on Appendix C. Sample-relative check: 5 of 6
  interviews (83%); Confidence remains High.
- **Direct confirmation, pain point promoted to a theme (2nd confirming interview):** P06's
  description of certification review timelines depending on customer response speed, and the
  resulting need (driven by a new MDR Article 7 requirement) to share timeline expectations
  with customers while acknowledging only partial responsibility for the overall duration,
  directly confirms the mechanism in the existing P02 standalone finding
  [[../03_pains/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]:
  customers cannot reliably know when the final review step will conclude. This is promoted to
  theme
  [[../02_themes/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]
  (P02, P06; Confidence Medium, Multi-interview). Per the Severity/Confidence flag hierarchy in
  [[Definitions]] (2+ interviews, Severity High, Confidence Medium), `validation_status:
  needs-validation-before-prioritization` now applies.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty`,
  `#code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools`, `#code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict`,
  and `#code/template-changes-without-staff-or-customer-guidance` describe mechanisms not
  evidenced in P01-P05, so they remain standalone preliminary pain points pending a second
  interview (see [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).
- **Related evidence, not merged (checked against existing standalone/confirmed findings):**
  `#code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools` (the same core data copy-pasted into five
  disconnected internal tools) was compared against
  [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]. Both
  concern the absence of a single unified system, but the status-view theme is specifically
  about not knowing which stage/whose turn a project is at, while this finding is about
  duplicated manual data entry of the same underlying values across tools. These are different
  mechanisms, so a new pain point was created instead of treating this as a further
  confirmation.
  `#code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict` (staff and customer each hold their own
  unshared local copy of Appendix ABC) was compared against
  [[../03_pains/No shared access to the current Appendix ABC version forces staff to rely on colleagues]]
  (P02, retrieval friction among staff) and
  [[../03_pains/Independently-edited Appendix ABC copies between auditors and reviewers diverge, causing rejected certification submissions]]
  (P05, auditor-vs-TD-reviewer divergence at submission). All three findings share the root
  cause of Appendix ABC not being a single shared live document, but each occurs at a
  different process step and between a different pair of parties (staff retrieval; internal
  auditor/reviewer handoff; ongoing staff/customer collaboration), so this is logged as a
  related but distinct new finding rather than merged with either.
  `#code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity` (missing supplier information on Appendix C, described
  as "quite complex") was compared against
  [[../03_pains/Customers apply their own definition of critical supplier, causing omissions or over-inclusion on Appendix ABC]]
  (P05). P05's finding is a definitional mismatch about which suppliers count as "critical";
  P06's is a general completion-difficulty/complexity observation about the supplier appendix
  with no stated definitional disagreement. Logged as related evidence supporting the general
  Appendix ABC theme rather than confirming or merging with the P05 finding.
- **Candidate idea convergence (no new artifact):** P06's vision of a single, jointly-editable
  device-list database that auto-suggests field values for similar devices and automatically
  generates the assessment plan converges with the existing candidate idea already logged
  under
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (P03, P04, P05); logged as a fourth interview extending that idea, with the auto-suggestion
  and auto-generated-plan detail added as a refinement. `#code/change-impact-auto-detection-vision`
  and `#code/shared-timeline-with-clock-stop-vision` are new, more specific extensions logged
  as additional candidate ideas under the same pain point and the newly created timeline need,
  respectively.
- **Positive workaround, single interview (research gap):** `#code/personal-tool-preserves-stable-core-dataset`
  describes a personally built Excel tool that has remained useful and stable across
  successive official-system changes over six years. This is a different specific mechanism
  from the existing single-interview positive-pattern candidate logged for P04 (a personal
  planning/calendar tool for audit scheduling): P04's tool addresses scheduling visualization,
  while P06's addresses preserving a stable, minimal core dataset independent of which official
  system is currently in use. Both remain below the two-interview threshold for a
  positive-pattern note and are retained as research gaps.
- **Background, out of scope for a dedicated artifact:** `#code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation`
  (Italy lacks the customer-portal interface that Germany has) and `#code/secondary-competency-role-assignment`
  (SPS risk-management coordination role) are recorded as background in the Topic Coverage
  Inventory below.

## Topic Coverage Inventory

| Topic | Evidence / codes | Coverage decision | Artifact(s) | Gap / next check |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Customer Specialist role scope: technical journey ownership, Appendix ABC intake, assessment planning | "I intended always the customer specialist role as the one who take care of the technical aspects of the certification"; `#code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity` | Persona evidence | Logged in [[../07_personas/Proto-Segments]] | Descriptive context for the segment/persona row |
| Needed planning data is a small subset buried within a much larger volume of Appendix ABC data (signal vs. noise) | "the information we really need are somehow hidden within a large amount of information that are not always necessary"; `#code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty` | Preliminary mechanism | [[../03_pains/Certification staff must manually extract a small, essential data subset from a much larger volume of Appendix ABC information]] | Confirm with a second interview |
| Excel reaches scalability limits managing 1000+ device entries | "you really reach the ceiling very fast when you have to manage a large amount of data"; `#code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty` | Related evidence | Logged under the same pain point as supporting context | None |

| Italy lacks the customer-portal interface that Germany has; communication is by e-mail and Teams | "I know that other regions, for example, in Germany, they have a customer interface ... but we don't have it in Italy"; `#code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation` | Background only | None created | Regional workflow variation, consistent with the pattern already noted for P05 |

| Supplier appendix (Appendix C) is complex and difficult for customers to complete | "it's more on the appendix ... for the supplier because it's quite complex ... I don't even know sometimes how to manage this"; `#code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity` | Related evidence | Logged as related evidence to the P05 critical-supplier-definition-mismatch finding (distinct mechanism: general complexity, not definitional mismatch) | None |

Excel is not shared with them ... sometimes maybe you think we are aligned, but we are not"; `#code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict` | Preliminary mechanism | [[../03_pains/Customer-facing Appendix ABC version conflicts arise from unshared local copies]] | Confirm with a second interview; related to but distinct from the P02 and P05 Appendix ABC version findings |
| Vision: single jointly-editable device-list database with auto-suggested field values for similar devices, feeding an auto-generated assessment plan and scheduler | "I would see a device list ... it is shared by both ... the list can automatically suggest how to fulfill the subsequent data"; `#code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision` | Related evidence | Logged as candidate idea, extending the existing digitization vision (4th interview: P03, P04, P05, P06) | Unvalidated idea; not a recommendation |
| Vision: change-impact auto-detection distinguishing trivial edits (silently logged) from impactful edits (flagged for replanning) | "The data set ... should allow for a modification, but keeping track somehow of this modification ... this is stored ... but then no impact ... then maybe there is a modification that impacts"; `#code/change-impact-auto-detection-vision` | Related evidence | Logged as candidate idea under the Appendix ABC pain point | Unvalidated idea; not a recommendation |

| Vision: shared customer-facing timeline interface with a clock-stop mechanism while awaiting customer response | "if I imagine two interfaces with the customer ... the timelines so that they know where they are and then the clock is stopped when they are until we will not answer"; `#code/shared-timeline-with-clock-stop-vision` | Related evidence | Logged as candidate idea under the new timeline theme/need | Unvalidated idea; not a recommendation |
| Secondary Special Process Specialist (SPS) role coordinating risk-management competency training across teams | "I'm assigned for risk management. So I'm coordinating with other teams for this role"; `#code/secondary-competency-role-assignment` | Background only | None created | Role-context detail, not itself a workflow friction for the MACE Application scope |

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Steps 1-3.

> "I would see a device list ... it is shared by both, so me and them can make modifications. ... the list can automatically suggest how to fulfill the subsequent data when one input is included ... if you start including a device that is a knee implant, mostly of the information will be always the same for every knee implant."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "I would love to have something that automatically extrapolates the small dataset that we really need in our bag. ... once having this small subset clearly established, the following plan for certification can be somehow automatically generated. ... it's ideally standardizable. ... this should be to me a real relational database software in this case."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "I always gave this feedback starting many years ago when we were in Italy creating a new platform. ... we should start with having a database with the information inside once ... and then from that obtaining the assessment plan ... and then have a tool that creates a scheduling. ... right now those informations are nowhere to me ... I have to copy and paste them inside the scheduler ... and then inside the assessment plan cloud."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "The data set, including all the devices, should allow for a modification, but keeping track somehow of this modification, like somehow freezing the previous one ... For example, ... a device that is already inside the certification path ... means nothing ... this is stored, this is recorded in a history part, but then no impact. ... then maybe there is a modification that impacts ... including a new code EA14, for example, the plastic ... you have to change the plan."
Code: #code/change-impact-auto-detection-vision

> "There is a new Article 7 in the MDR that is requesting us to share a plan with the customers ... to give them the timeline for the certification. But inside these timelines, we have only a partial responsibility. ... this timeline is really long. ... we can solve this issue if we have shared timelines with the customers saying ... you will receive this audit, you will receive this assessment ... we promise you that every round will have three months. ... but then the last part depends on you."

> "If I imagine two interfaces with the customer, one is the document list, the device list ... and then it's the timelines so that they know where they are and then the clock is stopped when they are until we will not answer. ... it will be the last point, the arrival point will be delayed if they delay the answers. This will protect us. This will a little bit protect also the reviewers."

sections.Theme Match:
`02_themes` contains 4 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P05):
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`, and
`Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone
document`. Every new P06 code was compared against these four themes and against all
standalone preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P05.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (5th interview):** P06 confirms
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  for a fifth interview: Appendix ABC is described as complex and difficult to manage, missing
  information is common (especially at project start), and the pain point has shifted over
  time from missing EMDN (European Medical Device Nomenclature) codes on Appendix A to
  difficulty completing the supplier information on Appendix C. Sample-relative check: 5 of 6
  interviews (83%); Confidence remains High.
- **Direct confirmation, pain point promoted to a theme (2nd confirming interview):** P06's
  description of certification review timelines depending on customer response speed, and the
  resulting need (driven by a new MDR Article 7 requirement) to share timeline expectations
  with customers while acknowledging only partial responsibility for the overall duration,
  directly confirms the mechanism in the existing P02 standalone finding
  [[../03_pains/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]:
  customers cannot reliably know when the final review step will conclude. This is promoted to
  theme
  [[../02_themes/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]
  (P02, P06; Confidence Medium, Multi-interview). Per the Severity/Confidence flag hierarchy in
  [[Definitions]] (2+ interviews, Severity High, Confidence Medium), `validation_status:
  needs-validation-before-prioritization` now applies.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/appendix-abc-signal-extraction-difficulty`,
  `#code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools`, `#code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict`,
  and `#code/template-changes-without-staff-or-customer-guidance` describe mechanisms not
  evidenced in P01-P05, so they remain standalone preliminary pain points pending a second
  interview (see [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).
- **Related evidence, not merged (checked against existing standalone/confirmed findings):**
  `#code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools` (the same core data copy-pasted into five
  disconnected internal tools) was compared against
  [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]. Both
  concern the absence of a single unified system, but the status-view theme is specifically
  about not knowing which stage/whose turn a project is at, while this finding is about
  duplicated manual data entry of the same underlying values across tools. These are different
  mechanisms, so a new pain point was created instead of treating this as a further
  confirmation.
  `#code/customer-facing-appendix-abc-version-conflict` (staff and customer each hold their own
  unshared local copy of Appendix ABC) was compared against
  [[../03_pains/No shared access to the current Appendix ABC version forces staff to rely on colleagues]]
  (P02, retrieval friction among staff) and
  [[../03_pains/Independently-edited Appendix ABC copies between auditors and reviewers diverge, causing rejected certification submissions]]
  (P05, auditor-vs-TD-reviewer divergence at submission). All three findings share the root
  cause of Appendix ABC not being a single shared live document, but each occurs at a
  different process step and between a different pair of parties (staff retrieval; internal
  auditor/reviewer handoff; ongoing staff/customer collaboration), so this is logged as a
  related but distinct new finding rather than merged with either.
  `#code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity` (missing supplier information on Appendix C, described
  as "quite complex") was compared against
  [[../03_pains/Customers apply their own definition of critical supplier, causing omissions or over-inclusion on Appendix ABC]]
  (P05). P05's finding is a definitional mismatch about which suppliers count as "critical";
  P06's is a general completion-difficulty/complexity observation about the supplier appendix
  with no stated definitional disagreement. Logged as related evidence supporting the general
  Appendix ABC theme rather than confirming or merging with the P05 finding.
- **Candidate idea convergence (no new artifact):** P06's vision of a single, jointly-editable
  device-list database that auto-suggests field values for similar devices and automatically
  generates the assessment plan converges with the existing candidate idea already logged
  under
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (P03, P04, P05); logged as a fourth interview extending that idea, with the auto-suggestion
  and auto-generated-plan detail added as a refinement. `#code/change-impact-auto-detection-vision`
  and `#code/shared-timeline-with-clock-stop-vision` are new, more specific extensions logged
  as additional candidate ideas under the same pain point and the newly created timeline need,
  respectively.
- **Positive workaround, single interview (research gap):** `#code/personal-tool-preserves-stable-core-dataset`
  describes a personally built Excel tool that has remained useful and stable across
  successive official-system changes over six years. This is a different specific mechanism
  from the existing single-interview positive-pattern candidate logged for P04 (a personal
  planning/calendar tool for audit scheduling): P04's tool addresses scheduling visualization,
  while P06's addresses preserving a stable, minimal core dataset independent of which official
  system is currently in use. Both remain below the two-interview threshold for a
  positive-pattern note and are retained as research gaps.
- **Background, out of scope for a dedicated artifact:** `#code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation`
  (Italy lacks the customer-portal interface that Germany has) and `#code/secondary-competency-role-assignment`
  (SPS risk-management coordination role) are recorded as background in the Topic Coverage
  Inventory below.

quotes.text: I intended always the customer specialist role as the one who take care of the technical aspects of the certification. So going in a journey with the customer to allows them to have a certification and to maintain their certification. ... We are taking the information with the appendix ABC ... and with this information, we are preparing the plan that is defining all the activities that we as a customer specialist has to do together with the customer.

For me, the problem is not that there are some missing data. ... the real challenge ... is that the information we really need are somehow hidden within a large amount of information that are not always necessary ... this creates noise. ... there is a very small subset of information that we really need to create the plan and to be able to really interact with the customer.

Typically, I manage customers that have an appendix ABC ... with at least 1000, 1500 or something like that [device entries]. ... It's not easy to manage that with a large Excel file, probably the Excel is not the right tool. ... We just need, for example, the requested certification ... which are the sites involved ... the relevant product and technology codes applied to each site ... and then some few more key details about the sterilization, packaging, reprocessing. ... when this subset is extracted, it becomes the operational interface for our activities.

In general, we are making ... there is a lot of noise ... we have to put a lot of data entries because ... data are always the same and they are very basic data. But we are copy and paste those data in a Word file, in an Excel file, in another tool that is made for planning the assessments, and in another tool that is made for the scheduling. ... we receive a request from administration or from some other colleagues asking exactly the same information ... there is not a real tool where all the information are inside and where everyone can really take the information from there.

Since I started six years ago ... the tools were changing ... but the information I need, if I really focus on which can be the most essential information I need, those are always the same. So if I create somehow a tool that only includes inside the very needed information, it will always stay the same. So I somehow created a tool. It's not something really ... well, it's an Excel, so I know all the limitation of having an Excel, but it worked and I always fulfill this document ... to be sure that this will not change.

I know that other regions, for example, in Germany, they have a customer interface. I just realized that during the meet, I asked it a little bit ... but we don't have it in Italy. So the main mean to communicate is through emails, organizing a Teams call if needed.

It's true that in general there are documents that always change internally in the template. So sometimes if we are in a rush, we don't have time to understand what have been changed in the template. ... we just send them the template and wait for their answer. ... it's not correct to send them a document hoping that they will be able to understand it. ... they don't even have an example on how to fulfill some roles, some entries. And so it's ... sometimes me neither. So the CS is not instructed on how to fulfill those documents.

I have an image of a very complex and not easy to assess ... document where if I made a change, it's very difficult to manage. ... Sometimes I make directly modification by myself if I feel this is the best way to proceed and then I send it back to them saying this is the last update. ... Sometimes I receive the modification on the previous version.

There are both [modifications and missing data]. ... at the very beginning with the company, there are a lot of missing information. ... when they have to fulfill the Appendix ABC for the first time, they fear the white paper, like they don't know how to fulfill it. They don't have any example and they really are frustrated to start this job.

Now, in these days ... it's more on the appendix ... for the supplier because it's quite complex. ... I don't even know sometimes how to manage this. And yes, this is the part where I have the back and forth now in this last period in relation to the suppliers.

I have a love and hate relationship with Excel in general. ... it's like everyone knows how to use it somehow ... it's always the first tool that I address. ... you really reach the ceiling very fast when you have to manage a large amount of data ... it's not probably the right tool with this back and forth to the customer.

You mean I receive a version [conflict]? Yes, it happened quite a lot. Sometimes I also receive this document. I think it's mine somehow, so I fix some points. ... I hope to receive the modification that they did from the last I sent them. Yes, this is a problem.

Yes, because it's a document inside my computer and I feel it's like one of the other Excels I have because Excel is not shared with them. It's not in a cloud, so I can only use them. ... sometimes maybe you are working and you think we are aligned, but we are not because it's not shared.

I would see a device list ... it is shared by both, so me and them can make modifications. ... the list can automatically suggest how to fulfill the subsequent data when one input is included ... if you start including a device that is a knee implant, mostly of the information will be always the same for every knee implant.

I would love to have something that automatically extrapolates the small dataset that we really need in our bag. ... once having this small subset clearly established, the following plan for certification can be somehow automatically generated. ... it's ideally standardizable. ... this should be to me a real relational database software in this case.

I always gave this feedback starting many years ago when we were in Italy creating a new platform. ... we should start with having a database with the information inside once ... and then from that obtaining the assessment plan ... and then have a tool that creates a scheduling. ... right now those informations are nowhere to me ... I have to copy and paste them inside the scheduler ... and then inside the assessment plan cloud.

The data set, including all the devices, should allow for a modification, but keeping track somehow of this modification, like somehow freezing the previous one ... For example, ... a device that is already inside the certification path ... means nothing ... this is stored, this is recorded in a history part, but then no impact. ... then maybe there is a modification that impacts ... including a new code EA14, for example, the plastic ... you have to change the plan.

There is a new Article 7 in the MDR that is requesting us to share a plan with the customers ... to give them the timeline for the certification. But inside these timelines, we have only a partial responsibility. ... this timeline is really long. ... we can solve this issue if we have shared timelines with the customers saying ... you will receive this audit, you will receive this assessment ... we promise you that every round will have three months. ... but then the last part depends on you.

If I imagine two interfaces with the customer, one is the document list, the device list ... and then it's the timelines so that they know where they are and then the clock is stopped when they are until we will not answer. ... it will be the last point, the arrival point will be delayed if they delay the answers. This will protect us. This will a little bit protect also the reviewers.
I have probably more the idea of an ERP, so I would not see a chat. ... Honestly, I don't see directly a tool that I would need if the information are already there.

My focus is more on not having too many tools or like having one real database where information are there once. Because this is a source of error because you are including information in many other fields and it's super common to have that.
I'm assigned for risk management. So I'm coordinating with other teams for this role, not really for the customer.

frontmatter.segment: Internal certification staff - Project Coordinator (commercial/backoffice role, formally also recorded as Customer Specialist/Support Specialist; low-risk device segment: MDSub, ISO, MDD, Taiwan; ~5 years tenure; does not attend the biweekly customer calls)

notes.body:
<!-- Write analysis prose in neutral third-person English. Keep participant quotes verbatim. -->

# Interview: P07

## Context (Step 1 - before coding)
- The participant ("Angelika") holds the title Project Coordinator, though she reports also
  being formally recorded, in some form, as Customer Specialist or Support Specialist. She
  describes her own understanding of the split as: the Customer Specialist (CS) holds
  responsibility for the Appendix ABC document, and the Relationship Manager (RM) only steps
  in when difficulties arise.
- She has worked in this role for five years and started using Appendix ABC herself only in
  her third year, because she did not understand it beforehand.
- She works in the low-risk device segment (MDSub, ISO, MDD as a legacy regulation, and
  Taiwan), explicitly distinguishing this from the High Risk segment, which only carries the
  MDR (Medical Device Regulation) scheme.
- Unlike the Auditor/Customer Specialist segment interviewed previously (P03, P04, P06), she is
  not customer-call-facing in the day-to-day sense: she explicitly does not attend the
  biweekly customer calls, describing her role as commercial/backoffice ("Abwicklungsbereich").
  She has ad hoc direct customer contact only for billing questions.
- Her work centers on the commercial and administrative side of the certification lifecycle:
  creating projects in PSE (the internal project/service tool) from cycle data, generating
  cost calculations, producing quotations, routing them through a multi-party signature
  process, creating subcontracts, triggering scheduling for assessors, linking the signed
  contract to SAP (an enterprise resource planning system), and later registering audits in
  CBW (a certificate/registration system) using codes drawn from the customer's Appendix ABC
  document.
- She built and maintains a tool used to calculate audit/quotation pricing ("Audit Pricing
  Tool"), which has been formally rolled out across the Business Service Center (BSC).
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed. The interview is conducted entirely in German; all quotes below are
  German with an English translation, per the vault's language convention.

## Meaning Units and Codes

> "Wir befüllen dann PSE erstmal mit den Rumpfdaten. ... Daraufhin geht dies zum Kunden. Wir legen dann anschließend die Unteraufträge in PSE an ... Sobald ein Audit in CBW als Audit registriert wird ... diese werden ... in einem Appendix ABC zum einen vom Kunden ausgefüllt, zum anderen dann natürlich auch vom Experten, also vom CS, in eine wiederum weitere Datenbank übertragen, also in den Assessmentplan. ... Und daraufhin entnehme ich die Codes, oft aber aus dem Appendix ABC heraus, um das Audit zu registrieren. ... auch bei Zertifikaten ... überprüfen wir den Appendix ABC, ob die Codes alle so auch korrekt sind. Das ist ja eine doppelte Datenbank, die wir haben."
>
> Translation: "We first populate PSE with the base data. ... Then it goes to the customer. We then create the subcontracts in PSE ... As soon as an audit is registered as an audit in CBW ... these are filled in on one hand by the customer in an Appendix ABC, and on the other hand transferred by the expert, i.e. the CS, into yet another database, namely the assessment plan. ... And then I extract the codes, often from the Appendix ABC, to register the audit. ... also for certificates ... we check the Appendix ABC to see whether the codes are all correct. That is a duplicate database that we have."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "Das ist ja wirklich eine Datenbank beziehungsweise wird Excel hier als Datenbank missbraucht. Und wenn man sich überlegt, dass der Kunde alles manuell ausfüllen muss, ist schon wirklich großes Kino."
>
> Translation: "This is really a database, or rather Excel is being misused here as a database. And when you consider that the customer has to fill everything in manually, that's really something else."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Das sind redundante Informationen und hier ist auch die Granularität, die ich in Frage stelle. Wir haben hier immer wieder dasselbe Produkt, allerdings haben wir hier in verschiedenen Varianten. Das kann zum Beispiel eine Größe sein, aber es ist immer noch dasselbe Produkt. Aber jedes einzelne wird hier divers immer wieder hinterlegt, also als Zeile vom Kunden auszufüllen und sogar die MDN-Codes, MDS-Codes bis MDT sind eigentlich alle identisch."
>
> Translation: "These are redundant pieces of information, and this is also where I question the granularity. We have the same product again and again here, but in different variants. That could be a size, for example, but it is still the same product. Yet every single one is entered here separately, as a row for the customer to fill in, and even the MDN codes, MDS codes, up to MDT are actually all identical."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Die Codes sind bei allen Varianten selbstverständlich identisch. ... Also das muss ich mir dann auch raussuchen, ob hier Steri-Supplier und welche Steri-Methoden, die ich dann hier unter A2 mal extra herauslesen muss. Pro Zeile, ja. Also wenn es jetzt so ein paar Sachen sind, so zehn Zeilen, dann ist das nicht so schlimm. Aber bei diesem Kunden, der hat über 2000 oder 3000 Zeilen."
>
> Translation: "The codes are of course identical across all variants. ... So I also have to look up whether there is a sterilization supplier here and which sterilization methods I then have to separately read out under tab A2. Per row. If it's just a handful of rows, say ten, that's not so bad. But this customer has over 2,000 or 3,000 rows."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Ich bin mir hundertprozentig sicher, dass wir auch definitiv Fehler haben, sowohl in den Zertifikaten als auch in den Audit-Registrierungen, weil das kannst du nicht mehr menschlich abdecken. ... hier ist, wir haben Excel als Tool ... aber Excel unterstützt mich nicht, sondern ich muss das ausfüllen beziehungsweise rauslesen und der Kunde muss das ausfüllen."
>
> Translation: "I am one hundred percent certain that we definitely have errors, both in the certificates and in the audit registrations, because you can no longer cover that by hand. ... here we have Excel as a tool ... but Excel doesn't support me, I have to fill it in or read it out myself, and the customer has to fill it in."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Diese Tabs A2, A3, hier sind Sterisupplier hinterlegt mit bestimmten Sterilisationsmethoden. ... Und dies müssen wir tatsächlich anhand von Ziffern 1, 2 etc. hier herauslesen. Und das ist wirklich alles nur manuell. Hier 1, 2, 3 trifft zu, dann muss ich wieder in den anderen Tab schauen. Und was ist 1, 2, 3?"
>

## Theme Match

`02_themes` contains 5 confirmed themes at the start of this interview (after P06):
`Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification
staff`, `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff`, `EUDAMED
product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition`, `Appendix
ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document`, and
`Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step`.
Every new P07 code was compared against these five themes and against all standalone
preliminary pain points in `03_pains` from P01-P06.

- **Direct confirmation, theme strengthened (5th interview):** P07 confirms
  [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]] for a
  fifth interview: PSE (the internal project/service tool) version 2.0 is described as harder
  to keep an overview with than version 1.0, requiring a recurring biweekly team meeting to
  manually walk through all open projects, and separately splitting timeline and hours
  information into two disconnected areas that must be manually cross-referenced. Sample-relative
  check: 5 of 7 interviews (71%); Confidence remains High.
- **Direct confirmation, pain point promoted to a theme (2nd confirming interview):** P07's
  description of the one-directional interface between CBW (a certificate/registration system)
  and Appendix ABC/PSE, and of the resulting risk that a manually entered value diverges
  between the two systems once one side changes, directly confirms the mechanism in the
  existing P06 standalone finding
  [[../03_pains/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]:
  the same core data must be manually kept in sync across disconnected systems with no single
  source of truth. This is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
  (P06, P07; Confidence Medium, Multi-interview). Severity is Medium for both interviews, so
  neither Severity/Confidence flag condition in [[Definitions]] applies; `validation_status`
  and `validation_question` are removed from the linked pain point. P07's blue-sky vision of a
  single tool (built around PSE) that opens CBW, SAP, the sampling plan, and the assessment
  plan without switching systems is logged as a further converging candidate idea under the
  same pain point.
- **Direct confirmation, pain point promoted to a theme (2nd confirming interview):** P07's
  description of documents and e-mails "floating around" unassigned when a project does not
  yet exist in PSE, or when she is not copied on the initial request, directly confirms the
  mechanism in the existing P02 standalone finding
  [[../03_pains/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]:
  project-related communication is not reliably linked to a project record. This is promoted
  to theme
  [[../02_themes/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
  (P02, P07; Confidence Medium, Multi-interview). Severity is Medium for both interviews, so
  neither Severity/Confidence flag condition applies; `validation_status` and
  `validation_question` are removed from the linked pain point.
- **Candidate idea convergence (no new artifact):** P07's explicit wish for centrally managed
  master data ("diese ganzen Stammdaten ... zentral verwaltet"), for code-driven auto-suggestion
  of applicable rules/procedure packs/facilities, for in-context classification/glossary
  guidance at the point of code selection, and for easier certificate row/text editing in CBW,
  converges with the existing Appendix ABC digitization-vision candidate idea already logged
  under
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (P03, P04, P05, P06). Logged as a sixth interview extending that idea, with the auto-suggested
  rule/procedure-pack/facility detail and the certificate-editing detail as refinements.
- **No match, new standalone preliminary findings:** `#code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy`,
  `#code/informal-customer-account-assignment`, `#code/unnecessary-multi-party-signature-requirement`,
  `#code/assessor-timeline-and-ready-status-noncompliance`, and
  `#code/customer-portal-limited-to-file-exchange` describe mechanisms not evidenced in
  P01-P06, so they remain standalone preliminary pain points pending a second interview (see
  [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point Register]]).
- **Related evidence, not merged (checked against existing standalone/confirmed findings):**
  `#code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy` (per-variant and per-facility row duplication of
  identical master data within Appendix ABC) was compared against
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC internal redundancy across sheets produces contradictory supplier information]]
  (P02, duplicate/contradictory supplier-relevance fields across sheets). Both describe
  redundant data within Appendix ABC, but P02's mechanism is about the same field being
  duplicated across different sheets and becoming contradictory, while P07's is about a
  document structure that forces one row per near-identical product variant or facility with
  no normalized master-data model. These are adjacent but distinct mechanisms, so P07's
  evidence is logged as related evidence on the P02 note rather than merged or counted as a
  second confirming interview.
  `#code/informal-customer-account-assignment` (post-attrition, first-available customer
  assignment with no domain-fit criteria) was compared against
  [[../03_pains/Reactive first-come-first-serve task assignment creates workload imbalance among assessors]]
  (P02, first-come-first-served assignment of individual audit tasks among assessors). Both
  describe reactive, criteria-free allocation, but P02's mechanism operates at the level of
  individual audit tasks and causes workload imbalance, while P07's operates at the level of
  long-term customer-account ownership and causes a domain-expertise mismatch. Logged as
  related evidence on the P02 note; a new standalone pain point was created for P07's distinct
  mechanism rather than merging.
- **Positive workaround, single interview (research gap):** `#code/self-built-pricing-tool-adopted-organization-wide`
  describes a staff-built Audit Pricing Tool that simplifies fee calculation via guided
  yes/no inputs and has been formally adopted across the Business Service Center. This is a
  different specific mechanism from the existing single-interview positive-pattern candidates
  logged for P04 (a personal audit-scheduling/calendar tool) and P06 (a personal Excel tool
  preserving a stable core dataset): P07's tool addresses formalized fee/price calculation and
  was adopted organization-wide, rather than remaining a private workaround. It remains below
  the two-interview threshold for a positive-pattern note and is retained as a research gap.
- **Background, out of scope for a dedicated artifact:** `#code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation`
  (an exception permit to also view UK-cluster projects in PSE) and
  `#code/role-outside-mace-audit-scope` (the participant is not a Mace Audit stakeholder and
  has no feedback on it) are recorded as background in the Topic Coverage Inventory below.

sections.Context (Step 1 - before coding):
- The participant ("Angelika") holds the title Project Coordinator, though she reports also
  being formally recorded, in some form, as Customer Specialist or Support Specialist. She
  describes her own understanding of the split as: the Customer Specialist (CS) holds
  responsibility for the Appendix ABC document, and the Relationship Manager (RM) only steps
  in when difficulties arise.
- She has worked in this role for five years and started using Appendix ABC herself only in
  her third year, because she did not understand it beforehand.
- She works in the low-risk device segment (MDSub, ISO, MDD as a legacy regulation, and
  Taiwan), explicitly distinguishing this from the High Risk segment, which only carries the
  MDR (Medical Device Regulation) scheme.
- Unlike the Auditor/Customer Specialist segment interviewed previously (P03, P04, P06), she is
  not customer-call-facing in the day-to-day sense: she explicitly does not attend the
  biweekly customer calls, describing her role as commercial/backoffice ("Abwicklungsbereich").
  She has ad hoc direct customer contact only for billing questions.
- Her work centers on the commercial and administrative side of the certification lifecycle:
  creating projects in PSE (the internal project/service tool) from cycle data, generating
  cost calculations, producing quotations, routing them through a multi-party signature
  process, creating subcontracts, triggering scheduling for assessors, linking the signed
  contract to SAP (an enterprise resource planning system), and later registering audits in
  CBW (a certificate/registration system) using codes drawn from the customer's Appendix ABC
  document.
- She built and maintains a tool used to calculate audit/quotation pricing ("Audit Pricing
  Tool"), which has been formally rolled out across the Business Service Center (BSC).
- The exact interview date is not stated in the transcript; this field is marked `unknown`
  rather than guessed. The interview is conducted entirely in German; all quotes below are
  German with an English translation, per the vault's language convention.
sections.Meaning Units and Codes:
> "Wir befüllen dann PSE erstmal mit den Rumpfdaten. ... Daraufhin geht dies zum Kunden. Wir legen dann anschließend die Unteraufträge in PSE an ... Sobald ein Audit in CBW als Audit registriert wird ... diese werden ... in einem Appendix ABC zum einen vom Kunden ausgefüllt, zum anderen dann natürlich auch vom Experten, also vom CS, in eine wiederum weitere Datenbank übertragen, also in den Assessmentplan. ... Und daraufhin entnehme ich die Codes, oft aber aus dem Appendix ABC heraus, um das Audit zu registrieren. ... auch bei Zertifikaten ... überprüfen wir den Appendix ABC, ob die Codes alle so auch korrekt sind. Das ist ja eine doppelte Datenbank, die wir haben."
>
> Translation: "We first populate PSE with the base data. ... Then it goes to the customer. We then create the subcontracts in PSE ... As soon as an audit is registered as an audit in CBW ... these are filled in on one hand by the customer in an Appendix ABC, and on the other hand transferred by the expert, i.e. the CS, into yet another database, namely the assessment plan. ... And then I extract the codes, often from the Appendix ABC, to register the audit. ... also for certificates ... we check the Appendix ABC to see whether the codes are all correct. That is a duplicate database that we have."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "Das ist ja wirklich eine Datenbank beziehungsweise wird Excel hier als Datenbank missbraucht. Und wenn man sich überlegt, dass der Kunde alles manuell ausfüllen muss, ist schon wirklich großes Kino."
>
> Translation: "This is really a database, or rather Excel is being misused here as a database. And when you consider that the customer has to fill everything in manually, that's really something else."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Das sind redundante Informationen und hier ist auch die Granularität, die ich in Frage stelle. Wir haben hier immer wieder dasselbe Produkt, allerdings haben wir hier in verschiedenen Varianten. Das kann zum Beispiel eine Größe sein, aber es ist immer noch dasselbe Produkt. Aber jedes einzelne wird hier divers immer wieder hinterlegt, also als Zeile vom Kunden auszufüllen und sogar die MDN-Codes, MDS-Codes bis MDT sind eigentlich alle identisch."
>
> Translation: "These are redundant pieces of information, and this is also where I question the granularity. We have the same product again and again here, but in different variants. That could be a size, for example, but it is still the same product. Yet every single one is entered here separately, as a row for the customer to fill in, and even the MDN codes, MDS codes, up to MDT are actually all identical."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Die Codes sind bei allen Varianten selbstverständlich identisch. ... Also das muss ich mir dann auch raussuchen, ob hier Steri-Supplier und welche Steri-Methoden, die ich dann hier unter A2 mal extra herauslesen muss. Pro Zeile, ja. Also wenn es jetzt so ein paar Sachen sind, so zehn Zeilen, dann ist das nicht so schlimm. Aber bei diesem Kunden, der hat über 2000 oder 3000 Zeilen."
>
> Translation: "The codes are of course identical across all variants. ... So I also have to look up whether there is a sterilization supplier here and which sterilization methods I then have to separately read out under tab A2. Per row. If it's just a handful of rows, say ten, that's not so bad. But this customer has over 2,000 or 3,000 rows."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Ich bin mir hundertprozentig sicher, dass wir auch definitiv Fehler haben, sowohl in den Zertifikaten als auch in den Audit-Registrierungen, weil das kannst du nicht mehr menschlich abdecken. ... hier ist, wir haben Excel als Tool ... aber Excel unterstützt mich nicht, sondern ich muss das ausfüllen beziehungsweise rauslesen und der Kunde muss das ausfüllen."
>
> Translation: "I am one hundred percent certain that we definitely have errors, both in the certificates and in the audit registrations, because you can no longer cover that by hand. ... here we have Excel as a tool ... but Excel doesn't support me, I have to fill it in or read it out myself, and the customer has to fill it in."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Diese Tabs A2, A3, hier sind Sterisupplier hinterlegt mit bestimmten Sterilisationsmethoden. ... Und dies müssen wir tatsächlich anhand von Ziffern 1, 2 etc. hier herauslesen. Und das ist wirklich alles nur manuell. Hier 1, 2, 3 trifft zu, dann muss ich wieder in den anderen Tab schauen. Und was ist 1, 2, 3?"
>
> Translation: "These tabs A2, A3 hold sterilization suppliers along with certain sterilization methods. ... And we actually have to read this out based on digits 1, 2, etc. here. And that is really all manual. Here 1, 2, 3 applies, then I have to look at the other tab again. And what is 1, 2, 3?"
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Auch hier wieder Wiederholungseingaben, sei es einmal die CGW-Nummer, Kundeninformationen und sogar Adressen. ... Aber auch das wären Stammdaten, die eigentlich mit Eingabe der Nummer sofort auftauchen sollten ... dass ich Mehrfacheingaben machen muss. Das bleibt nicht aus, weil die Systeme nicht miteinander arbeiten."
>
> Translation: "Here again there are repeated entries, whether it's the CGW number, customer information, or even addresses. ... But that too would be master data that should actually appear immediately once the number is entered ... [meaning] I have to make duplicate entries. That's unavoidable, because the systems don't work together."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Ich habe vor fünf Jahren angefangen und ich habe erst im dritten Jahr damit gearbeitet, weil ich habe es vorher gar nicht verstanden. Die letzte Kollegin, die bei uns angefangen hat, war letztes Jahr im Januar, Februar und ich nehme mir immer noch Zeit, ihr das Dokument so zu erklären, dass es passt. ... dieses Tool macht aus der vorhandenen Komplexität also etwas, was einfach Quatsch ist."
>
> Translation: "I started five years ago and only worked with it from the third year onward, because I didn't understand it before that at all. The most recent colleague who joined us started last year in January/February, and I am still taking time to explain the document to her properly. ... this tool turns the existing complexity into something that is simply nonsensical."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy

> "Mein Hut ist ja grundsätzlich, dass man diese ganzen Stammdaten, weil das sind Stammdaten, zentral verwaltet und nur bei Neuerungen, Updates, Changes, dass man dann dies anpasst."
>
> Translation: "My general wish is that all this master data — because it is master data — be managed centrally and only adjusted when there are actual changes, updates, or amendments."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "Von so einem Tool erwarte ich tatsächlich, dass es mich unterstützt. Wähle ich etwas aus wie die 1213, wäre es doch echt schön, wenn das System mir gleich sagt: Hey, welche Rules sind da? Hey, was für Procedure Packs und hey, diese Facilities."
>
> Translation: "What I actually expect from such a tool is that it supports me. If I select something like 1213, wouldn't it be nice if the system immediately told me: hey, which rules apply here? Hey, what procedure packs, and hey, these facilities."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "Ich glaube, das mit dem Code ist tatsächlich sehr sinnvoll und das würde ich mir tatsächlich von dieser Datenbank wünschen. Wenn ich diesen Code auswähle, sollte auch gleich die Information da sein. Warum noch mal extra in ein Glossary rein? ... Classification Rules, das wäre halt auch schön, gell. Wenn ich 2a auswähle, hätte ich auch gerne die Information direkt."
>
> Translation: "I think the idea with the code is actually very sensible, and that's what I would actually wish for from this database. If I select this code, the information should be right there too. Why go into a separate glossary again? ... Classification Rules, that would be nice too. If I select 2a, I would also like the information directly."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "Ich klicke ein Zertifikat an und hier kommt dann alles, was bereits im Zertifikat drinsteht. ... Hey, wenn ich den EMDN-Code habe, wenn er noch dazukommt, brauche ich eine Code-Auswahlmöglichkeit aus diesen Codes, ohne dass ich suchen muss. ... Es ist nämlich auch ein bisschen bei CBW ein bisschen blöd ... ein Zertifikat zu bearbeiten ... Die Änderungsmöglichkeiten, Zeilen rauszunehmen, Texte anzupassen, ist extremst umständlich und nicht möglich. ... da muss man mit Tricks arbeiten."
>
> Translation: "I click on a certificate and everything that is already in the certificate appears. ... Hey, if I have the EMDN code, when a new one is added, I need a code-selection option from these codes, without having to search. ... It's also a bit annoying with CBW ... editing a certificate ... the options to remove rows, adjust text, is extremely cumbersome and not [really] possible. ... you have to work with tricks."
Code: #code/appendix-abc-digitization-vision

> "Also die Führungskräfte haben in der Regel schon bestimmte Bereiche ... Aber die Kundenverteilung, wie sie im Moment stattfindet. Letztes Jahr sind ja 35 Leute von uns gegangen und jeder, der konnte, hat Kunden genommen, ja, egal in welchem Bereich, weil einfach so viel los war. Derzeit gibt es keine signifikanten Merkmale, wie Kunden verteilt werden, sondern derjenige, der die Zeit hat, macht das."
>
> Translation: "Managers generally already have certain areas ... But how customer distribution currently happens: last year 35 people left us, and everyone who could took on customers, regardless of area, because there was simply so much going on. Currently there are no significant criteria for how customers are distributed; whoever has the time does it."
Code: #code/informal-customer-account-assignment

> "Der Kunde reicht den Antrag ein. ... Ist es nicht der Fall, existiert dieses Projekt nicht im PSE, ja, dann dümpeln die Dokumente irgendwo rum oder die E-Mails und können dann nicht mehr entsprechend zugeordnet werden. Und in der Masse, wie wir Projekte haben, ist es teils schwierig, die dann noch sauber zuzuordnen."
>
> Translation: "The customer submits the request. ... If that is not the case, if this project does not exist in PSE, then the documents or the e-mails float around somewhere and can no longer be properly assigned. And given the sheer volume of projects we have, it is sometimes difficult to assign them cleanly."
Code: #code/unanchored-cross-channel-project-communication

> "Ich muss tatsächlich sagen, mit PSE 2.0 ist es echt schwierig den Überblick zu behalten. Weil bei PSE1 war das relativ easy ... PSE 2.0 kann dies nicht. ... Ich habe auch mit allen, sie essen alle zwei Wochen ein Meeting, um alle offenen Projekte durchzugehen ... so wissen wir, ist ein Projekt verspätet dran, hat der Bewerter was verschlafen oder ist die Teilrechnung noch nicht rausgeschickt?"
>
> Translation: "I really have to say, with PSE 2.0 it is genuinely difficult to keep an overview. Because with PSE 1 that was relatively easy ... PSE 2.0 cannot do this. ... We also have, every two weeks we have a meeting to go through all open projects ... that's how we know whether a project is running late, whether the assessor overslept something, or whether the partial invoice hasn't been sent out yet."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Bitte kein neues Tool. Ich brauche ein Haupttool, das ich öffne, sehe und damit arbeiten kann. ... Ich finde es ganz schrecklich, dass hier zwei Bereiche sind, einmal mit Timeline, einmal mit Stunden. Weil wie kann ich denn sehen, wenn jetzt hier noch Stunden verfügbar ... Aber das sehe ich hier oben einfach nicht. Aber hier oben sehe ich die Timeline, also das ist totaler Quatsch."
>
> Translation: "Please, no new tool. I need one main tool that I open, see, and can work with. ... I find it really terrible that there are two separate areas here, one with the timeline, one with the hours. Because how am I supposed to see, if there are still hours available ... I simply don't see that up here. But up here I see the timeline — so that's complete nonsense."
Code: #code/project-status-tracking

> "Ich darf auch im UK-Cluster arbeiten. Und hier könnte ich zum Beispiel auch UK sehen, ja. Aber das ist eine Ausnahmegenehmigung, weil wir die jetzt unterstützt haben."
>
> Translation: "I'm also allowed to work in the UK cluster. And here I could, for example, also see UK. But that's an exception permit, because we're now supporting them."
Code: #code/regional-cert-body-workflow-variation

> "Da bin ich auch ganz stolz, weil ich dieses Tool erstellt habe und es ist auch bei uns im BSC ausgerollt worden. Das nennt sich das Audit Pricing Tool. In diesem Audit Pricing Tool ist eben ein Kalkulationsmodell, welches für als User einfach ist, weil wir nur anklicken müssen: Ja/Nein, trifft es zu? ... mit einem Copy und Inhalte einfügen ... kann Kalkulation mit Preis darzustellen."
>
> Translation: "I'm actually quite proud of this, because I created this tool and it has also been rolled out across our Business Service Center (BSC). It's called the Audit Pricing Tool. This Audit Pricing Tool contains a calculation model that is simple for users, because we only have to click: yes/no, does it apply? ... with a copy and paste-special ... it can display the calculation together with the price."
Code: #code/self-built-pricing-tool-adopted-organization-wide

> "Ich bin mir gar nicht so sicher, ob das wirklich im Kaufmännischen notwendig ist, dass das Angebot erstens doppelt unterschrieben wird. Ich bin mir auch nicht sicher, ob eine Order Confirmation mittlerweile unterschrieben werden muss ... Und das sind so Fragen, das kann sich wirklich verzögern, das verzögert, wenn jemand im Urlaub ist, nicht da ist, muss der ständig hinterherlaufen."
>
> Translation: "I'm not at all sure whether it's really necessary commercially for the quotation to be signed twice. I'm also not sure whether an order confirmation still needs to be signed at all these days ... And these are the kinds of questions [where] this can really cause delay — it causes delay when someone is on vacation, not available, you constantly have to chase them."
Code: #code/unnecessary-multi-party-signature-requirement

> "Für uns Projektkoordinatoren ist es echt ein Hinterherlaufen, weil manche Bewerter setzen ihre Unteraufträge nicht auf ready. Ich weiß nicht, ob das jetzt fällig ist oder ob da noch was offen ist. ... Kann ich erst eine Teilrechnung erstellen, wenn es gebucht ist, alles."
>
> Translation: "For us Project Coordinators it really is a constant chasing, because some assessors don't set their subcontracts to 'ready.' I don't know whether it's now due or whether something is still open. ... I can only create a partial invoice once everything has been booked."
Code: #code/assessor-timeline-and-ready-status-noncompliance

> "Bewerter halten sich nicht daran. Sie ignorieren es. Und verschieben einfach so, wie sie Lust haben. Und tatsächlich kommt auch manchmal eine E-Mail: Hey, ich bin im Urlaub, kann ich erst einen Monat später machen. ... Also das passiert schon bei jedem Projekt ein, zwei Mal, dass Timelines angepasst werden."
>
> Translation: "Assessors don't stick to it. They ignore it. And just postpone as they please. And sometimes an e-mail actually comes in: hey, I'm on vacation, can I only do it a month later. ... So this happens on every project, once or twice, that timelines get adjusted."
Code: #code/assessor-timeline-and-ready-status-noncompliance

> "UCI wird derzeit lediglich als Daten-Upload-Download-Tool verwendet. ... derzeit kann ich niemanden direkt anschreiben, sondern jeder kriegt diese Informationen. Kunden können mich auch nicht direkt anschreiben, sondern es ist halt einfach im Tool."
>
> Translation: "UCI is currently only used as a data upload/download tool. ... currently I cannot message anyone directly; instead everyone just gets these pieces of information. Customers can't message me directly either — it's just simply within the tool."
Code: #code/customer-portal-limited-to-file-exchange

> "Momentan ist es so, ich kann fehlerhaft eingestellte Dokumente nicht mehr löschen. Die bleiben für immer in diesem Tool. Das geht nicht. ... Ich kann sie lediglich verstecken, das kann nicht sein. Also so ein Tool muss schon eine Möglichkeit haben, dass man auch was löschen kann."
>
> Translation: "Right now it's the case that I can no longer delete documents that were uploaded by mistake. They stay in this tool forever. That's not acceptable. ... I can only hide them, and that shouldn't be the case. A tool like this needs to have the ability to actually delete something."
Code: #code/customer-portal-limited-to-file-exchange

> "Die Schnittstelle ist ja hier auch nur einseitig. Wenn die jetzt beidseitig wäre, ich hier zum Beispiel nachschauen kann. Ich bin hier drin, gehe unter MHS-Details rein. Das habe ich manuell eingetragen, ja. Wenn das nicht mehr stimmt, ja dann stimmt's nicht mehr. Dann ist es falsch hier, aber richtig woanders. Und wenn man hier ein Abbild haben könnte von dem, was in CBW drin steht, Pendix APC, es sollten ja die gleichen Daten sein, dann wird es schon richtig gut."
>
> Translation: "The interface here is also only one-directional. If it were now bidirectional, I could, for example, look it up here. I'm in here, I go into the MHS details. I entered that manually. If that's no longer accurate, then it's simply no longer accurate. Then it's wrong here but right somewhere else. And if one could have a mirror image here of what's in CBW, Appendix ABC — it should be the same data after all — then it would already be really good."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "Ja gut, also jetzt muss ich erstmal die ganze Komplexität abstimmen, die ja bereits da ist. ... nehmen wir mal an, das ist dieses Tool und ich habe hier die Möglichkeit: Klick, CBW öffnet sich ... Klick, ich gehe rein, ah, ich möchte eine Teilrechnung erstellen. ... Und ich muss nicht in ein anderes System wechseln. Das wäre mega. Und auch Size-Sampling-Plan, Assessment-Plan, alles. Alles in einem Tool."
>
> Translation: "Well, first I'd have to reconcile all the complexity that already exists. ... let's assume this is the tool, and I have the option here: click, CBW opens ... click, I go in, ah, I want to create a partial invoice. ... And I don't have to switch to another system. That would be amazing. And also the sampling plan, assessment plan, everything. Everything in one tool."
Code: #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

> "Ich kenne dieses Tool nicht, ich habe es noch nie gesehen. Wir dürfen nicht an ihm arbeiten, weil ... wir ja nicht die Ansprechpartner sind für Maze Audit."
>
> Translation: "I don't know this tool, I've never seen it. We're not allowed to work on it, because ... we're simply not the point of contact for Mace Audit."
Code: #code/role-outside-mace-audit-scope
