notes.body:
<!-- Use short, neutral, third-person sentences. Expand acronyms on first use in each section. -->

# Theme: Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document

## Definition
Certification staff treat the customer-maintained Appendix ABC document as the authoritative
source of truth for product/master data, even though it is also the document changed most
often and, in practice, the one most prone to being incomplete, outdated, or containing
regulatorily invalid entries at the time it is relied upon.

## Associated Codes
- #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

## Representative Quotes
> "Derzeit ist der Appendix A. B. C. die vollendete Wahrheit, die maßgeblich sein muss und deckungsgleich mit dem Assessment Plant Loud. Und auch das Dokument, das am häufigsten verändert wird, logischerweise." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Currently the Appendix ABC is the complete truth that has to be authoritative and consistent with the assessment plan. It is also, logically, the document that gets changed most often." - [P01]

> "Also einerseits dann mit den Daten, die sie dann haben ... Also immer dieser Cross-Check ... da verliere ich glaube ich am meisten Zeit ... es gibt hier in einer Basic UDI verschiedene intended users. Dürfen sie eigentlich gar nicht haben. ... dann müssen die sich erstmal fünf Wochen absprechen, dass sie irgendwie dann wieder eine neue Version schicken." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "On one hand with the data they have ... always this cross-check ... I think that's where I lose the most time ... there are different intended users on one Basic UDI here. They aren't actually allowed to have that. ... then they first have to coordinate among themselves for five weeks before sending a new version." - [P03]

> "I mean, I think that for the customer is one of the most crucial point. I mean. They are not complaining too much, but on the other side that they are making me waiting for weeks for an update." - [P04]

> "for the customer that I have more than 100 [Basic UDI/SKUs], it's critical because I have the, let's say, I'm afraid that there could be losing of data, wrong typing, from the customer ... So I always, when I receive each version, let's say, read from the ... top to the bottom." - [P04]

> "The client's big piece of that is the Appendix ABC document, which it sounds like you've probably seen and you know how much of a bear that thing is." - [P05]

> "I've never had a client fill it out correctly in one go. There's always something wrong with it that I have to go back to them and ask for a correction or a clarification on." - [P05]

> "There are both [modifications and missing data]. ... at the very beginning with the company, there are a lot of missing information. ... when they have to fulfill the Appendix ABC for the first time, they fear the white paper, like they don't know how to fulfill it. They don't have any example and they really are frustrated to start this job." - [P06]

> "Auch da, ich mein, wir haben letztlich dieselben Themen, das sind Dateninkonsistenzen, Traceability über mehrere Dokumente, die verlinkt sein sollten. ... es sind teilweise sehr Zeilen mit ... vielen Einträgen ... für die größeren Kunden ohne einen Automatismus dahinter." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "There too, I mean, we ultimately have the same issues: data inconsistencies, traceability across several documents that should be linked. ... some [sheets] have I don't even know how many entries, for the larger customers, with no automation behind it." - [P08]

## Contradicting Evidence
None identified. P01, P03, P04, P05, P06, and P08 describe the same mechanism from different
roles (account management, Audit/Customer Specialist, new-client onboarding, Customer
Specialist/Lead Auditor/TD Assessor, and Client Manager & Lead Auditor): Appendix ABC is relied
upon as authoritative while also being the most error-prone, most frequently changed document.
P06 additionally notes that the focus of missing/incomplete data has shifted over time from
Appendix A (EMDN, European Medical Device Nomenclature, codes) to Appendix C (supplier
information), indicating the mechanism persists even as its specific manifestation moves across
sections of the document. P08 independently names Appendix ABC-related issues as customers'
single biggest complaint, without being prompted for a ranking.

## Open Questions
- How often do Appendix ABC errors that reach mid-assessment (like the intended-user example)
  actually delay certificate issuance, versus being absorbed without schedule impact?
- Would structured/digitized data entry with regulatory validation rules (as P03 envisions)
  meaningfully reduce the error rate, or does the underlying customer-side classification
  complexity limit how much validation alone can help?

**Threshold check:** P01, P03, P04, P05, P06, P08 all directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). Sample-relative check: 6 of 8 interviews processed so far (75%) directly and
consistently confirm this mechanism, above the 25% threshold in [[Definitions]]; Confidence
remains High.

**Update (2026-08-14):** P08 adds a sixth confirming interview from a Client Manager & Lead
Auditor segment, reinforcing data inconsistency and cross-document traceability as the
mechanism, and separately reports that informally-used consistency-check macros remain
necessary in the absence of a digital solution. Confidence remains High (6 of 8 interviews,
75%).

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]

## Linked Insights
- [[../05_insights/Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]]

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

# Theme: Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers

## Definition
Project-related communication (e-mail, chat, and incoming documents) is not reliably linked to
a project object. Staff must manually insert a project/reference number into outgoing messages
to identify which project they concern, and incoming messages or documents that arrive before a
project record exists, or without the responsible staff member copied, can become effectively
unassignable.

## Associated Codes
- #code/unanchored-cross-channel-project-communication

## Representative Quotes
> "Momentan muss ich es, also wenn ich eine E-Mail schreibe, Team [Teams] muss man sich immer die Projektnummer, irgendeine Referenz S.A.P. Nummer oder P.S.E. Projektnummer reinschreiben, dass ich 'ne Referenz irgendeinen Anhaltspunkt habe, welches Projekt geht es quasi." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Currently I have to — so when I write an email, [or] Teams, you always have to write in the project number, some reference SAP number or PSE project number, so that I have a reference, some point of reference, [to know] which project it concerns." - [P02]

> "Ist es nicht der Fall, existiert dieses Projekt nicht im PSE, dann d\u00fcmpeln die Dokumente irgendwo rum oder die E-Mails und k\u00f6nnen dann nicht mehr entsprechend zugeordnet werden." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "If that is not the case, if this project does not exist in PSE, then the documents or the e-mails float around somewhere and can no longer be properly assigned." - [P07]

## Contradicting Evidence
None identified. P02 and P07 describe the same mechanism from different roles (TD Assessor;
Project Coordinator): communication is not anchored to a project record. P02's manifestation is
outgoing (she must manually type a reference into every message); P07's is incoming (messages
or documents that arrive before a project record exists, or without her copied, become
effectively unassignable given project volume). Both stem from the same missing capability: no
automatic link between communication and a project object.

## Open Questions
- Would linking communication to a project object at the point of sending (P02's case) also
  resolve the incoming, pre-project-creation case (P07's case), or does the latter need a
  separate intake mechanism that creates a placeholder project record?
- How often do "floating" documents/e-mails (P07) end up permanently lost versus eventually
  resolved through manual follow-up?

**Threshold check:** P02, P07 both directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview — two distinct interviews from different roles describe
the same specific mechanism (communication not linked to a project object), per
[[Definitions]].

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]

## Linked Insights
- None yet. See [[../05_insights/_status]].

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

# Theme: Communication scattered across multiple parallel channels makes project history hard to reconstruct

## Definition
Project-related communication is split across multiple parallel channels (such as email,
Teams, and UCI/PSE, an internal customer-communication portal and project/service tool) with
no single, linked record, so staff must manually reassemble the communication history from
several disconnected sources.

## Associated Codes
- #code/dual-channel-communication-friction

## Representative Quotes
> "Meistens schreibe ich mir da irgendwie noch dazu, irgendwie via Mail oder via UCI, weil das ist jetzt auch immer, dann denkt man, hey, ich bin gar keine Mail dazu. ... diese zwei Kanäle sind auch manchmal eher ein Hindernis, dass man das irgendwie nachverfolgen kann." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "Usually I also note down whether it was via email or via UCI, because otherwise you think, hey, I don't have an email about that. ... these two channels are also sometimes more of an obstacle to being able to track it." - [P03]

> "Es gibt E-Mail-Kommunikationspfad, es gibt einen Teams-Kommunikationspfad, es gibt gegebenenfalls noch zusätzlichen Pfad über UCI beziehungsweise PSE[M] und Kunden. Diese Informationen nach zwei Wochen Urlaub wieder zusammenzusuchen, katastrophal." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "There's an email communication path, there's a Teams communication path, there is possibly an additional path via UCI or PSE and customers. Reassembling this information after two weeks of vacation — catastrophic." - [P08]

## Contradicting Evidence
None identified. P03 (two channels: email, UCI) and P08 (three channels: email, Teams,
UCI/PSE) describe the same channel-fragmentation mechanism at different scales.

## Open Questions
Whether a single-tool, in-context chat/communication feature (see P08's Candidate Solution
Ideas on the linked pain point) would meaningfully reduce reassembly effort, or whether staff
would still default to email/Teams for reasons outside tooling (e.g. habit, external-party
constraints).

**Threshold check:** P03, P08 both directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview — two distinct interviews (P03, P08) directly evidence
the same specific mechanism (project communication scattered across multiple parallel, unlinked
channels), per [[Definitions]]. This is distinct from
[[../02_themes/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
(P02, P07), which concerns communication missing a project-object/reference-number anchor
rather than channel fragmentation.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/Communication scattered across multiple parallel channels makes project history hard to reconstruct]]

## Linked Insights
- 

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

notes.body:
<!-- Use short, neutral, third-person sentences. Expand acronyms on first use in each section. -->

# Theme: Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step

## Definition
Unlike earlier service-model phases, which have defined day counts (e.g. 40 working days for
the first round, 20 for the second), the final certification-body review step has no
comparably predictable timeline. The final duration also depends heavily on how quickly the
customer responds to requests, so the certification body holds only partial responsibility for
the overall outcome, even though a new MDR (Medical Device Regulation) Article 7 requirement
now obliges it to share timeline expectations with the customer.

## Associated Codes
- #code/final-step-timeline-unpredictability

## Representative Quotes
> "Ich denk, der größte Pain Point für Kunden ist, wenn die Timeline nicht eingehalten werden, weil der Kunde zuverlässig wissen muss, wann eine Bewertung fertig ist, wann er einen Reporter bekommt, wann er ein Zertifikat bekommt. ... da kommt es oft zu Rückfragen, dann verschiebt sich oder verlängert sich der Slot." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "I think the biggest pain point for customers is when the timeline is not met, because the customer needs to reliably know when an assessment will be finished, when they'll get a report, when they'll get a certificate. ... there are often follow-up questions, and then the slot shifts or extends." - [P02]

> "There is a new Article 7 in the MDR that is requesting us to share a plan with the customers ... to give them the timeline for the certification. But inside these timelines, we have only a partial responsibility. ... this timeline is really long. ... we can solve this issue if we have shared timelines with the customers saying ... you will receive this audit, you will receive this assessment ... we promise you that every round will have three months. ... but then the last part depends on you." - [P06]

## Contradicting Evidence
None identified. P02 and P06 describe the same mechanism from different angles:
customer-facing frustration with unpredictable final-review timing (P02), and the regulatory
and shared-responsibility framing of the same unpredictability under MDR Article 7 (P06).

## Open Questions
- Would a shared, customer-facing timeline interface with a "clock-stop" mechanism while
  awaiting the customer's response (P06's vision) meaningfully reduce customer dissatisfaction,
  or does the underlying uncertainty in the final review step's duration limit how much a
  timeline display alone can help?
- Do other regions besides Italy and Germany (P02, P06's segments) report the same
  final-review unpredictability, or is it specific to certain certification bodies/schemes?

**Threshold check:** P02 and P06 both directly evidence the same mechanism (2 of 6 interviews
processed so far).
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview — the mechanism is confirmed by two distinct interviews,
below the typical 3+ repetition needed for Confidence High per [[Definitions]].

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]

## Linked Insights
None yet. Logged in [[../05_insights/_status]] as not yet enough connected evidence for an
insight (only one supporting theme).

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

# Theme: Customers frequently fill in standard request forms incorrectly, requiring staff to return them for correction

## Definition
Customers submitting a formal service request frequently fill in the standard request form
incorrectly or inconsistently, requiring staff to catch the error manually and, in some cases,
return the form for correction.

## Associated Codes
- #code/customers-frequently-fill-in-request-forms-incorrectly

## Representative Quotes

<!-- Use short, neutral, third-person sentences. Expand acronyms on first use in each section. -->

# Theme: Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff

## Definition
When customers self-assign regulatory codes to their products during a certification
request, they frequently guess or misjudge which codes apply, so certification staff must
identify and correct the errors before assessor qualification and assessment planning can
proceed correctly.

## Associated Codes
- #code/customer-code-misassignment

## Representative Quotes
> "Bei den Codes weiß der Kunde immer, was das Richtige ist oder?" / "Natürlich nicht. Kann er nicht oder verbockt er manchmal einfach? Beides." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "With the codes, does the customer always know what's correct?" / "Of course not. Can't he, or does he sometimes just get it wrong? Both." - [P01]

> "Manchmal ist auch nicht so ganz klar, ist der Code jetzt relevant für das Produkt oder nicht. ... es kann schon zu Fehlern kommen und zurückfragen, und dann ... das kann viel Zeit kosten." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Sometimes it's also not entirely clear whether a code is relevant for the product or not. ... errors and follow-up questions can occur, and then ... that can cost a lot of time." - [P02]

> "A lot of companies will choose the EAC 14 code for plastics because of this, even because their cartridge is made of plastic. ... those codes are only for the specific manufacturing technologies that they use and most companies don't mold their own plastic cassette housings. They buy those from a supplier. ... They're not actually manufacturing the plastic." - [P05]

> "Realistically, especially for IBD companies, you're probably only going to have like one to three of those applicable [but] companies will pick like 6 because they'll pick like anything that might be vaguely related to their instrument or their device." - [P05]

## Contradicting Evidence
P03 reports that, in her experience, her customers — large or small — already understand and
can work with regulatory codes (EMDN/MDA/MDN), in some tension with the mechanism P01 and P02
describe. Interview count is not increased on this basis, since P03 does not directly report
customers guessing codes incorrectly; a plausible explanation is a role-based difference in
exposure, as P03 is less involved in Application-stage code review than P01/P02. This is
recorded as an open tension rather than smoothed over.

## Open Questions
- How often does a wrong code actually change assessor assignment or audit scope, versus
  being caught and corrected without downstream effect?
- Would example/guidance material measurably reduce the error rate, or is the underlying
  classification logic too complex for self-service guidance to fix?
- Does code-misassignment frequency vary by role/exposure (e.g. Application-stage reviewers
  vs. Audit/Customer Specialists), which could explain P03's contrasting experience?

**Threshold check:** P01, P02, P05 all directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). Sample-relative check: 3 of 5 interviews processed so far (60%) directly and
consistently confirm this mechanism, above the 25% threshold in [[Definitions]], and
repetition is now at the typical 3+ level, so Confidence is raised from Medium to High. P03's
contradicting evidence (recorded above) remains documented and does not block this raise,
since it reflects a role-based difference in exposure rather than a direct contradiction of
the mechanism.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]

## Linked Insights
- [[../05_insights/Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]]

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

# Theme: EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition

## Definition
Customer product and certificate data held in EUDAMED (European Database on Medical Devices)
is not yet reliable or complete enough for certification staff to use as a primary
verification source, because the platform is still in a transition period and richer data
types have only recently started to become available.

## Associated Codes
- #code/data-source-of-truth-ambiguity

## Representative Quotes
> "Würdest du sagen, dass deine Kunden ihre Daten in EUDAMED zu 100 Prozent gepflegt haben?" / "Nee. Mindestens dadurch, dass es einen Humanfehler gibt und Leute sich verklicken." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Would you say your customers maintain their data in EUDAMED 100 percent [accurately]?" / "No. At the very least because there is human error and people misclick." - [P01]

> "Es hat halt große Verzögerung gehabt, das Tool. ... was momentan wirklich bisher nur für Herstellerdaten, Adresse gut war, und die ganzen Sachen mit Zertifikaten, Produktdaten, die kommen jetzt erst zu langsam, müssen wir im Detail testen." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "The tool has had major delays. ... what has really only been good so far for manufacturer data and address, and all the things with certificates and product data are only now slowly coming online; we still need to test them in detail." - [P02]

## Contradicting Evidence
None identified. Both participants describe EUDAMED data as currently insufficient, for
different but compatible reasons: P01 points to uncorrected human error in customer-entered
data, and P02 points to the platform itself only recently beginning to expose
certificate/product data at all.

## Open Questions
- Once EUDAMED's product/certificate data matures, would certification staff adopt it as a
  cross-check against Appendix ABC, or does the human-error concern (P01) persist regardless
  of platform maturity?
- Is there a known target timeline for EUDAMED's transition that would inform when to revisit
  this?

**Threshold check:** P01, P02 both directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Multi-interview — 2 of 2 interviews processed so far, described
consistently by both participants.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition]]
- [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]] (related: original bundled finding, now narrowed to the Appendix ABC-only mechanism)

## Linked Insights
- [[../05_insights/Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]]

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

# Theme: No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff

## Definition
Certification staff lack a reliable, consolidated view of where a project or application
currently stands in the certification process. Existing tools only provide an accurate
overview when everyone maintains data consistently, which does not happen systematically,
especially on internationally-coordinated projects.

## Associated Codes
- #code/project-status-tracking

## Representative Quotes
> "Tracking von Projektstatus ist mit Sicherheit eine wichtige Sache. wenn man das hier einbauen könnte wie bei einem DHL Paket, in welchem Status wir uns befinden, wo das Paket sich gerade befindet." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Tracking the project status is certainly an important thing, if one could build this in like a DHL package, [showing] what status we are in, where the package currently is." - [P01]

> "Wenn das so gehandhabt wird [Tasks nur zum Buchen angelegt], dann habe ich eigentlich keinerlei Übersicht mehr." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "If it's handled that way [tasks only created for booking hours], then I actually have no overview at all anymore." - [P02]

> "Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "What I would actually want ... is something that really depicts this workflow ... whose turn it is, so to speak." - [P03]

> "Surely for what regard the changes and assessment, I think there is a, there is a, let's say, void or lack in following planning. ... I have no tool proposed by to suit the tool. I need to let's say rely on my own, let's say scheduling for following the project." - [P04]

> "You may, I mean, if you don't have something that supports you, you may, I mean, lose the overall picture of how you are going." - [P04]

> "Ich muss tatsächlich sagen, mit PSE 2.0 ist es echt schwierig den Überblick zu behalten. ... Ich habe auch mit allen, sie essen alle zwei Wochen ein Meeting, um alle offenen Projekte durchzugehen." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I really have to say, with PSE 2.0 it is genuinely difficult to keep an overview. ... We also have, every two weeks, a meeting to go through all open projects." - [P07]

> "Ich finde es ganz schrecklich, dass hier zwei Bereiche sind, einmal mit Timeline, einmal mit Stunden. ... das sehe ich hier oben einfach nicht." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I find it really terrible that there are two separate areas here, one with the timeline, one with the hours. ... I simply don't see that up here." - [P07]

> "Darüber hinaus, was schön wäre, wenn ich alles in UCI direkt hätte ... Ich hätte gern mein [Gantt]-Diagramm, wo ich mein einzelnes Projekt sehe." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Beyond that, it would be nice if I had everything directly in UCI ... I'd like my Gantt chart, where I see my individual project." - [P08]

## Contradicting Evidence
P02 qualifies the mechanism: when the existing PSE 2.0 tool is well-maintained, it can
provide a good overview, so the gap is inconsistent data-entry discipline (especially on
internationally-coordinated tasks) rather than a complete absence of any status feature. This
narrows, but does not contradict, P01's observation that no reliable consolidated view exists
in practice today.

## Open Questions
- Is the inconsistency concentrated in specific regions/teams (e.g. internationally-managed
  tasks), or general across the project portfolio?
- Would a status view independent of manual timeline maintenance resolve this, or does the
  underlying data-entry gap need to be fixed regardless of the viewing tool?

**Threshold check:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P07, P08 all directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). Sample-relative check: 6 of 8 interviews processed so far (75%) directly and
consistently confirm this mechanism, above the 25% threshold in [[Definitions]]; Confidence
remains High.

**Update (2026-08-13):** P07 adds a fifth confirming interview from a Project Coordinator
(commercial/backoffice) segment: PSE (the internal project/service tool) version 2.0 is
described as harder to keep an overview with than version 1.0, requiring a recurring biweekly
team meeting to manually walk through all open projects as a workaround, and separately
splitting timeline and hours/booking-status information into two disconnected areas that must
be manually cross-referenced. Confidence remains High (5 of 7 interviews, 71%).

**Update (2026-08-14):** P08 adds a sixth confirming interview from a Client Manager & Lead
Auditor segment: two separate, personally-built filters are needed (a time filter in BSE for
personal to-dos; a project-manager filter in PSE for team oversight), an upcoming PSE
master-data reduction is a specific concern because it would remove status detail currently
relied upon, and a single graphical (Gantt-style) status view within UCI is wished for.
Confidence remains High (6 of 8 interviews, 75%).

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]

## Linked Insights
- (none yet — see [[../05_insights/_status]])

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

described as harder to keep an overview with than version 1.0, requiring a recurring biweekly

Auditor segment: two separate, personally-built filters are needed (a time filter in BSE for

master-data reduction is a specific concern because it would remove status detail currently
relied upon, and a single graphical (Gantt-style) status view within UCI is wished for.
Confidence remains High (6 of 8 interviews, 75%).

notes.body:
<!-- Use short, neutral, third-person sentences. Expand acronyms on first use in each section. -->

# Theme: The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools

## Definition
The same core, largely static certification data (e.g. requested certification, sites, codes,
customer/facility details) must be manually kept in sync across several disconnected internal
tools and documents, because no single tool or interface holds the information once for
everyone to draw from. This is distinct from
[[No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]], which concerns not
knowing which stage/whose turn a project is at, rather than duplicated manual entry of the same
underlying values.

## Associated Codes
- #code/redundant-manual-data-reentry-across-tools

## Representative Quotes
> "In general, we are making ... there is a lot of noise ... we have to put a lot of data entries because ... data are always the same and they are very basic data. But we are copy and paste those data in a Word file, in an Excel file, in another tool that is made for planning the assessments, and in another tool that is made for the scheduling. ... we receive a request from administration or from some other colleagues asking exactly the same information ... there is not a real tool where all the information are inside and where everyone can really take the information from there." - [P06]

> "My focus is more on not having too many tools or like having one real database where information are there once. Because this is a source of error because you are including information in many other fields and it's super common to have that." - [P06]

> "Das ist ja eine doppelte Datenbank, die wir haben." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "That is a duplicate database that we have." - [P07]

> "Die Schnittstelle ist ja hier auch nur einseitig. ... Ich bin hier drin, gehe unter MHS-Details rein. Das habe ich manuell eingetragen. Wenn das nicht mehr stimmt, dann stimmt's nicht mehr. Dann ist es falsch hier, aber richtig woanders." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "The interface here is also only one-directional. ... I'm in here, I go into the MHS details. I entered that manually. If that's no longer accurate, then it's simply no longer accurate. Then it's wrong here but right somewhere else." - [P07]

> "Ich habe hier die M\u00f6glichkeit: Klick, CBW \u00f6ffnet sich ... Und ich muss nicht in ein anderes System wechseln. Das w\u00e4re mega." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I have the option here: click, CBW opens ... And I don't have to switch to another system. That would be amazing." - [P07]

> "Ihr kennt wahrscheinlich die Geschichte, dass wir eine Application Identification oder irgendein sonstiges Kürzel brauchen das wirklich über alle Dokumente identifiziert. ... Das liegt einfach an den händischen Einträgen. Und es muss zeichengenau, glaube ich, gehen dementsprechend." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "You probably know the story that we need an Application Identification, or some other short code, that really identifies [the case] across all documents. ... That's simply because of the manual entries. And it has to match character-for-character, I believe." - [P08]

> "Was wir intern dann machen müssen ist, dass wir diese Daten, die vom Kunden verfügbar sind, nochmal übertragen in unsere internen Dokumente. Also wenn ich eine Change Notification von Kunden zum Beispiel bekomme, dann fülle ich ein Decision of Significant Change Dokument aus, wo mehr oder weniger Copy-Paste die Justification vom Kunden für diese Änderung noch mal drinsteht." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "What we then have to do internally is transfer this data, which is already available from the customer, once again into our internal documents. So if I receive a Change Notification from a customer, for example, I fill out a Decision of Significant Change document, where the customer's justification for that change is more or less copy-pasted in again." - [P08]

## Contradicting Evidence
None identified. P06, P07, and P08 describe the same mechanism from different roles
(Customer Specialist/Lead Auditor/TD Assessor; Project Coordinator; Client Manager & Lead
Auditor): the same core data exists in more than one system or document with no automatic
synchronization, and staff bear the risk of the copies diverging. P06 frames this around
planning tools (Word, Excel, the assessment-planning tool, the scheduling tool); P07 frames it
around the one-directional interface between CBW (a certificate/registration system) and
Appendix ABC/PSE; P08 frames it around an Application Identification code that must match
character-for-character across all application documents, and around copy-pasting a
customer-supplied Change Notification justification into a separate internal Decision of
Significant Change document. P08 additionally reports that on long-running projects (beyond
about three months), accumulated customer-side changes render previously-entered references
outdated, requiring extensive manual rework, which is the same underlying mechanism
manifesting over time rather than across tools.

## Open Questions
- Does the divergence risk materialize more often for master/facility data (P07's example) or
  for planning/schedule data (P06's example), or equally for both?
- Would a single shared database eliminate the need for the specific tools named by P06 and
  P07, or would some (e.g. the scheduler) still need to remain separate for other reasons?

**Threshold check:** P06, P07, P08 all directly evidence the same mechanism.
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). Sample-relative check: 3 of 8 interviews processed so far (37.5%), above the 25%
threshold in [[Definitions]], and repetition has reached the typical 3+ level; Confidence is
raised from Medium to High.

## Linked Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]

## Linked Insights
- None yet. See [[../05_insights/_status]].

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for confidence criteria and [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] for the full process.

# Pain Point Register

Last consolidated: 2026-08-12 (after P03, 3 interviews processed). Full pass over all rows
performed per SOP-Analysis-Process.md D3; no pairs describing the same underlying mechanism
were found to merge. Appendix ABC-related rows (single source of truth despite errors,
internal redundancy across sheets, no shared access to current version) remain distinct —
each describes a different specific mechanism, not the same root process step.

P04 processed (4 interviews total); not yet due for the next ~3-5 interview consolidation
pass. New P04 rows checked individually against all existing rows at creation time; no
duplicates found.

P05 processed (5 interviews total; 2 interviews since the last full consolidation pass after
P03) — still not yet due for the next full pass. New P05 rows checked individually against
all existing rows at creation time: `critical-supplier-definition-mismatch` and
`appendix-abc-version-branching-conflict` were each explicitly compared against the existing
Appendix ABC-related rows and judged to describe distinct root process steps (see the Theme
Match section in [[../01_interviews/P05]]); no duplicates found.

P06 processed (6 interviews total; 3 interviews since the last full consolidation pass after
P03 — due for the next full pass). Full pass performed per SOP-Analysis-Process.md D3: all
rows were re-scanned for mergeable pairs, with particular attention to the now eight
Appendix-ABC/document-related rows (single source of truth despite errors; internal
redundancy across sheets; no shared access to current version; independently-edited copies
diverge between auditor and reviewer; customer-facing version conflicts from unshared local
copies; signal-extraction difficulty; redundant manual data re-entry across tools; template
changes without guidance). Each was confirmed to describe a distinct root mechanism or
process step (authority-despite-errors; within-document sheet duplication; staff-to-staff
retrieval friction; auditor-vs-reviewer divergence at submission; staff-to-customer sync gap;
data-volume/extraction difficulty; cross-tool re-entry; template-guidance gap). No merges were
made. `Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step`
was promoted from a standalone finding to a theme-linked pain point (2nd confirming
interview, P02 and P06).

P07 processed (7 interviews total; 1 interview since the last full consolidation pass after
P06) — not yet due for the next full pass. New P07 rows checked individually against all
existing rows at creation time: `appendix-abc-master-data-redundancy` was compared against
`Appendix ABC internal redundancy across sheets produces contradictory supplier information`
and judged to describe a distinct root mechanism (per-variant/per-facility row duplication vs.
cross-sheet contradictory duplication); `informal-customer-account-assignment` was compared
against `Reactive first-come-first-serve task assignment creates workload imbalance among
assessors` and judged distinct (account-level assignment vs. task-level assignment). Both
comparisons are logged as Related Evidence on the existing rows, not merges. Two standalone
findings (`The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple
disconnected tools`, P06; `Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to
manually reference project numbers`, P02) were promoted to theme-linked pain points (2nd
confirming interview, both with P07).

P08 processed (8 interviews total; 2 interviews since the last full consolidation pass after
P06) — not yet due for the next full pass. New P08 rows checked individually against all
existing rows at creation time (see the Theme Match and Topic Coverage Inventory sections in
[[../01_interviews/P08]]); no duplicates found beyond the merges/promotions listed below.
`Customers frequently fill in standard request forms incorrectly, requiring staff to return
them for correction` (P03) was promoted to a theme-linked pain point (2nd confirming
interview, P08). A new theme-linked pain point, `Communication scattered across multiple
parallel channels makes project history hard to reconstruct`, was created directly with two
confirming interviews (P03, P08) by promoting P03's previously related-evidence-only
dual-channel observation. `The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across
multiple disconnected tools` was confirmed a third time (P08), raising Confidence from Medium
to High. `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` and `Appendix
ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document` were
each confirmed a sixth time (P08).

Priority Tier is looked up from the Severity x Confidence matrix in [[Definitions]] ("Priority
Tier (pain points)"), not multiplied. Interview Count is a tie-breaker only, not part of the
tier calculation.

frontmatter.name: Appendix ABC glossary lags behind evolving regulatory guidance
frontmatter.validation_question: Do other staff also encounter cases where the Appendix ABC glossary or classification filters no longer match current regulatory guidance (e.g. new MDCG papers), and do they rely on the outdated glossary/filters without being able to re-check every device?

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Appendix ABC glossary lags behind evolving regulatory guidance

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** The Appendix ABC glossary and its classification filters can fall out of step
with evolving regulatory guidance (e.g. a new MDCG — Medical Device Coordination Group — paper
on Well-Established Technologies, or a device-classification distinction such as Exempted Class
2B). When this happens, staff cannot re-check every device against the updated guidance and
must rely on the outdated glossary/filter as-is.
**Trigger:** New regulatory guidance is published (e.g. an MDCG paper) that changes a
definition or classification the Appendix ABC glossary or filters are built around.
**Impact:** The participant states that in such cases "our Appendix ABC is no longer current
and the regulation runs ahead of it," and that staff cannot re-check every device against a
new filter for large customer lists, so they "rely on it" despite the known gap. This carries a
regulatory/compliance risk, since staff are consciously relying on a document that may no
longer match current guidance.
**Workaround:** None described beyond continuing to rely on the outdated glossary/filter for
new entries.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes a specific,
concrete recent instance (the MDCG paper on Well-Established Technologies) and a general,
recurring pattern (relying on filters that cannot be manually re-verified device-by-device),
not a one-off anecdote.

**Severity/Confidence flag:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (single interview) triggers
the flag in [[Definitions]] "Severity/Confidence flag," rule 1. This finding carries a
Severity/Confidence risk: an outdated glossary or classification filter creates a regulatory
compliance risk if left unaddressed, but is based on one interview and requires
cross-interview validation before being prioritized as a confirmed, high-severity mechanism.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Wir haben zwar ein ausführliches Glossary, aber dieses Glossary widerspricht ... teilweise der Regularien oder den Definitionen in der Regularien ... Das kam jetzt im M.D.C.G.Paper raus, dass sogenannten Web Devices, also die Well-Established Technologies zum Beispiel angeht. Das heißt, in dem Moment ist unser Appendix ABC nicht mehr aktuell und die Regularia läuft dann sozusagen voraus. ... Da setzen wir Filter in dieser Liste an und wir können nach diesem Filter nicht nochmal jedes Device prüfen, ob das auch korrekt wirklich in diese Liste fällt. Dementsprechend verlassen wir uns darauf." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "We do have a detailed glossary, but this glossary sometimes contradicts the regulations or the definitions in the regulations ... This came out now in the MDCG paper, concerning so-called WET devices, i.e. Well-Established Technologies for example. That means, at that moment our Appendix ABC is no longer current and the regulation runs ahead of it, so to speak. ... We set filters on this list, and after that filter we can't re-check every single device to see whether it really correctly falls into this list. So we rely on it." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A mechanism to flag Appendix ABC glossary entries or classification filters as
  potentially outdated when new regulatory guidance is published, rather than relying on
  manual awareness and unable-to-verify filters (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other staff also encounter cases where the Appendix ABC glossary
or classification filters no longer match current regulatory guidance (e.g. new MDCG papers),
and do they rely on the outdated glossary/filters without being able to re-check every device?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Appendix ABC internal redundancy across sheets produces contradictory supplier information

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Within a single customer's Appendix ABC document, the same information (for
example, which suppliers are relevant to a given product) is captured redundantly in more than
one sheet. These duplicate entries are often contradictory, since they can be filled in at
different times with different levels of detail, and it is not always clear whether a
discrepancy reflects a customer error or a misunderstanding.
**Trigger:** A reviewer cross-checks supplier or product information across different sheets
within the same Appendix ABC document.
**Impact:** Contradictions raise follow-up questions and require the reviewer to determine
which entry is correct and why, adding review effort.
**Workaround:** None described beyond raising the discrepancy as a follow-up question.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant gives a specific,
concrete example (duplicated supplier-relevance columns) of the redundancy mechanism.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Es gibt so ein paar Redundanzen, also im Sheet 1 zum Beispiel, wo die Produkte aufgeführt werden, ... gibt es da auch 'ne Spalte in Excel, die dann sagt, welche Supplier quasi für das Produkt relevant sind. Die gleiche Information ... habe ich aber dann noch mal in diesen Sheets dahinter, ... und die sind oft widersprüchlich." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "There are a few redundancies — in Sheet 1, for example, where the products are listed, there is also a column in Excel that says which suppliers are relevant for the product. I have the same or similar information again in the sheets behind that, ... and they are often contradictory." - [P02]

> "Da kommt schon mal zu fragen, ja, war das jetzt 'n Fehler vom Kunden oder 'n Missverständnis, warum hat er es am Anfang allgemein quasi nicht genannt, dass der Supplier relevant ist, aber erst später im Detail ... genannt, dass der Supplier relevant ist." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "That raises questions — was that a mistake by the customer or a misunderstanding, why didn't they mention initially, in general, that the supplier was relevant, but only mentioned it later, in detail." - [P02]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Removing duplicate supplier-relevance fields from Appendix ABC in favor of a single
  authoritative entry (P02, mentioned later regarding digitizing Appendix ABC). Explicitly
  unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other assessors also find contradictory information (e.g. supplier
relevance) duplicated across different sheets within the same customer's Appendix ABC?

**Related Evidence (2026-08-13):** P07 separately describes a distinct redundancy mechanism
within Appendix ABC: the document forces one row per near-identical product variant or
facility even though the underlying codes are identical across them, at volumes of
2,000-3,000 rows for one customer. This is an adjacent but distinct mechanism (per-row
variant/facility duplication of identical master data vs. cross-sheet duplication that becomes
contradictory) and is logged here as related evidence only; it does not increase this pain
point's interview count or confidence. See
[[Appendix ABC's row structure forces redundant master-data re-entry and manual cross-tab decoding]].

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document

**Update (2026-08-11):** Scope narrowed. This note originally bundled two topics: (a) Appendix
ABC being treated as authoritative despite being the most frequently changed/error-prone
document, and (b) EUDAMED product/certificate data reliability. P02 confirms only topic (b) as
a cross-interview mechanism, and separately describes Appendix ABC itself as a good, important
document — not as authoritative-despite-being-error-prone. Topic (b) has therefore been split
out into its own theme and pain point:
[[../02_themes/EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition]] /
[[../03_pains/EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition]].
This note now covers topic (a) only, remained a single-interview (P01) standalone finding at
that time, and was otherwise unchanged (severity, confidence, validation status).

**Update (2026-08-12):** P03 directly confirms the same mechanism (Appendix ABC frequently not
submitted or updated with the Application; data-quality errors, such as invalid multiple
intended-user entries, discovered only mid-assessment; ~5-week customer correction round-trips)
from a different segment (Auditor / Customer Specialist). Per [[Definitions]] "Theme
threshold," this note is promoted to theme
[[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
with Confidence Basis Single-interview strong evidence → Multi-interview (2 of 3 interviews
processed so far; Confidence remains Medium since repetition is below the typical 3+ needed
for High). With 2 interviews and Severity Medium, neither condition in [[Definitions]]
"Severity/Confidence flag" applies, so `validation_status` and `validation_question` are
removed from the frontmatter.

**Update (2026-08-12, same day):** P04 adds a third, independent confirmation of the same
mechanism (Appendix ABC described as the most critical customer document; review burden scales
sharply with Basic UDI/SKU count; every new version requires full manual re-verification
because of risk of customer data loss, typos, or overwriting; customer corrections take
"weeks"). Per [[Definitions]] "Sample-relative check," 3 of 4 interviews processed so far
(75%) directly and consistently confirm this mechanism, and repetition is now at the typical
3+ level, so Confidence is raised from Medium to High. Priority Tier recalculated from P2 to
P1 (Severity Medium x Confidence High) in `03_pains/_register.md`.

**Update (2026-08-12, later):** P05 adds a fourth confirming interview, from a new-client
onboarding segment: Appendix ABC is described as "the crux of this entire meeting" and is
never filled out correctly on the first attempt, making it the single biggest source of
back-and-forth with the customer early in a project. Per [[Definitions]] "Sample-relative
check," 4 of 5 interviews processed so far (80%) directly and consistently confirm this
mechanism; Confidence remains High.

**Update (2026-08-13):** P06 adds a fifth confirming interview, from a Customer
Specialist/Lead Auditor/TD Assessor segment: Appendix ABC is described as complex, difficult
to manage, and never complete at the start of a customer relationship, with the specific
missing-data focus having shifted over time from Appendix A (EMDN codes) to Appendix C
(supplier information). Per [[Definitions]] "Sample-relative check," 5 of 6 interviews
processed so far (83%) directly and consistently confirm this mechanism; Confidence remains
High. P06 also extends the existing digitization-vision candidate idea (see below) and adds a
new change-impact auto-detection candidate idea.

**Theme:** [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
**Description:** The internal data collection document ("Appendix ABC") is currently treated as
the authoritative, complete source of truth that must match the assessment plan, even though
it is also the document changed most often and, per P03, the source of the largest single
time cost before assessment (data-quality cross-checks against regulatory rules).
**Trigger:** The interviewer asks where the "single source of truth" for customer master data
lies (P01); P03 raises it unprompted when asked what costs her the most time.
**Impact:** Certification staff and reviewers rely on a document acknowledged to be the most
frequently corrected and error-prone one as their working source of truth. P03 reports that
errors not caught at intake — such as multiple intended users listed against a single Basic
UDI (Unique Device Identification), which is not regulatorily permitted — are sometimes only
discovered mid-assessment, after which the customer needs about five weeks to coordinate and
resubmit a corrected version. P04 reports that review burden scales sharply with the number of
Basic UDIs/SKUs on a customer's Appendix ABC (manageable under about 10, "critical" above
about 100), requiring a full top-to-bottom manual re-verification of every new version because
of the risk of customer data loss, typing errors, or accidental overwriting; customers can also
make staff wait "weeks" for an updated version, delaying internal work. P05 reports never
having had a client fill out Appendix ABC correctly on the first attempt, always requiring at
least one correction or clarification round-trip, and separately describes independently-edited
internal copies of Appendix ABC diverging between the auditor and the Technical Documentation
(TD) reviewer (see the related, separately logged finding
[[Independently-edited Appendix ABC copies between auditors and reviewers diverge, causing rejected certification submissions]]).
**Workaround:** None described beyond treating Appendix ABC as authoritative by convention;
P03 performs a manual cross-check against regulatory rules before assessment can proceed. P04
manually re-reads each new Appendix ABC version from top to bottom to catch customer data
errors before relying on it. P05 tempers client expectations in advance and always offers a
line-by-line review call, though clients rarely take this offer up before at least one
rejected attempt.
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). For traceability: 6 of 8 interviews processed so far (P01, P03, P04, P05, P06, P08)
directly and consistently evidence the same mechanism, satisfying both the repetition and
sample-relative checks in [[Definitions]].

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 11
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P01, P03, P04, P05, P06, P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Derzeit ist der Appendix A. B. C. die vollendete Wahrheit, die maßgeblich sein muss und deckungsgleich mit dem Assessment Plant Loud. Und auch das Dokument, das am häufigsten verändert wird, logischerweise." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Currently the Appendix ABC is the complete truth that has to be authoritative and consistent with the assessment plan. It is also, logically, the document that gets changed most often." - [P01]

> "Ob das jetzt die Single Source of Truth ist, würde ich noch mal in den Raum stellen, einfach nur, was manuelle Prozesse sind." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Whether that is really the single source of truth, I would still question, simply because of what manual processes are." - [P01]

> "Sagen wir mal zu 90 Prozent muss zu dieser Application gehört auch dieser Appendix ABC dazu. ... das ist meistens nicht so, dass sie da überhaupt den Appendix ABC mitschicken, geschweige denn da schon die Änderung irgendwie drin haben." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "About 90 percent of the time, this Appendix ABC has to be part of the Application. ... it's usually not the case that they even send the Appendix ABC along, let alone already have the change reflected in it." - [P03]

> "Also einerseits dann mit den Daten, die sie dann haben ... Also immer dieser Cross-Check ... da verliere ich glaube ich am meisten Zeit ... es gibt hier in einer Basic UDI verschiedene intended users. Dürfen sie eigentlich gar nicht haben. ... dann müssen die sich erstmal fünf Wochen absprechen, dass sie irgendwie dann wieder eine neue Version schicken." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "On one hand with the data they have ... always this cross-check ... I think that's where I lose the most time ... there are different intended users on one Basic UDI here. They aren't actually allowed to have that. ... then they first have to coordinate among themselves for five weeks before sending a new version." - [P03]

> "I mean, I think that for the customer is one of the most crucial point. I mean. They are not complaining too much, but on the other side that they are making me waiting for weeks for an update." - [P04]

> "for the customer that have, let's say, until 10 basic QDI, there is not, let's say it's fine having this ABC because you can quite, let's say, rapidly scroll the SKUs, not much a problem. Let's say for the customer that I have more than 100, it's critical because I have the, let's say, I'm afraid that there could be losing of data, wrong typing, from the customer, I mean, overwriting. So I always, when I receive each version, let's say, read from the ... top to the bottom." - [P04]

> "The client's big piece of that is the Appendix ABC document, which it sounds like you've probably seen and you know how much of a bear that thing is." - [P05]

> "I've never had a client fill it out correctly in one go. There's always something wrong with it that I have to go back to them and ask for a correction or a clarification on." - [P05]

> "Honestly, having getting that information upfront and correct the first time would probably be one of the more helpful things, especially at the beginning of an entire project, because getting the appendix ABC correct is kind of the thing we go back and forth with the most early on." - [P05]

> "at the very beginning with the company, there are a lot of missing information. ... when they have to fulfill the Appendix ABC for the first time, they fear the white paper, like they don't know how to fulfill it. They don't have any example and they really are frustrated to start this job." - [P06]

> "Auch da, ich mein, wir haben letztlich dieselben Themen, das sind Dateninkonsistenzen, Traceability über mehrere Dokumente, die verlinkt sein sollten." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "There too, I mean, we ultimately have the same issues: data inconsistencies, traceability across several documents that should be linked." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Digitizing Appendix ABC as structured data instead of Excel, enabling automatic cross-checks
  and blocking regulatorily invalid entries (such as multiple intended users on one Basic UDI)
  at data-entry time (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A live or bulk-upload interface between the customer's own systems (e.g. SAP) and Appendix
  ABC to reduce manual re-entry for large customers (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A customer-facing portal with a live, database-like document tracking modifications, acting
  as a single container/retrieval point for all customer changes, with direct links to change
  forms (P04, converging with P03's structured-data idea). Explicitly unvalidated.
- An online Appendix ABC that both internal staff and the client can jointly see and
  manipulate, replacing the current siloed Excel copies and eliminating internal version
  branching (P05, a third interview converging on the same live-document direction as P03 and
  P04). Explicitly unvalidated.
- An AI-powered capability that extracts information from client-uploaded documents (e.g.
  Instructions for Use, quality manual, approved supplier list) to auto-populate Appendix ABC
  fields such as codes, scope statement drafts, and the critical supplier list, with a manual
  fallback for clients who lack some of these documents (P05). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A sanity-check/validation layer that flags likely mismatches (e.g. a code that looks
  inconsistent with the stated intended purpose) or invalid entries (e.g. malformed
  addresses), combined with both an override option (for staff to correct directly) and a
  flag-to-customer option, with formal customer approval required only at defined phase gates
  rather than on every edit (P05). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A single, jointly-editable device-list database (shared by staff and the customer) that
  auto-suggests field values for similar device types (e.g. pre-filling likely values when a
  new knee implant is added, based on other knee implants already listed), with the
  assessment plan and audit scheduling automatically generated from this shared dataset
  (P06, a fourth interview converging on the same live-document/digitization direction as P03,
  P04, and P05, with the auto-suggestion and auto-generated-plan detail as a new refinement).
  Explicitly unvalidated.
- A change-tracking mechanism that freezes prior states of the device dataset and
  automatically distinguishes edits with no downstream planning impact (recorded silently)
  from edits that require replanning (e.g. adding a new required code), surfacing only the
  latter for staff attention instead of treating every edit the same (P06). Explicitly
  unvalidated.
- Centrally managed master data (rather than re-entered per row/variant), with code-driven
  auto-suggestion of applicable rules, procedure packs, and facilities at the point of code
  selection, in-context classification/glossary guidance instead of a separate glossary
  lookup, and easier certificate row/text editing in CBW (a certificate/registration system)
  (P07, a sixth interview converging on the same live-document/digitization direction as P03,
  P04, P05, and P06, with the auto-suggested rule/procedure-pack/facility detail and the
  certificate-editing detail as further refinements). This is a converging candidate idea
  only; P07 does not directly confirm the core mechanism (Appendix ABC treated as
  authoritative despite being error-prone) and is not counted toward this pain point's
  interview count. Explicitly unvalidated.
- Automated consistency checks/macros that search Appendix ABC for expected wordings or
  patterns (an informal version of which already exists, built by colleagues, per P08) should
  be a built-in, digital-solution feature rather than a personal workaround, since manual
  checking is infeasible for large customers' row volumes (P08, a sixth interview converging
  on the same automated-validation direction as P03, P05, and P06). Explicitly unvalidated.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Appendix ABC's row structure forces redundant master-data re-entry and manual cross-tab decoding

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Appendix ABC (a customer-facing document, misused as a database in Excel)
requires one row per product variant or per facility, even when the underlying codes (e.g.
MDN/MDS/MDT classification codes) are identical across all of those rows. The participant must
also manually decode cross-referenced fields, such as sterilization supplier and method,
represented only as numeric shorthand in separate tabs (A2, A3), by looking them up row by row.
At volume (over 2,000-3,000 rows for one customer), the participant states this cannot be
reliably covered by hand and is confident it produces errors in certificates and audit
registrations.
**Trigger:** A Customer Specialist or Project Coordinator processes a customer's Appendix ABC
to extract codes for certificate or audit registration, or a customer fills in the document
for a product line with many near-identical variants or facilities.
**Impact:** The participant states she is "one hundred percent certain" that errors exist in
both certificates and audit registrations as a result, because the redundant, per-row
structure cannot be fully and correctly cross-checked by hand at the volumes involved (an
example customer had over 2,000-3,000 rows). New hires take about two to three years to become
proficient with the document because of its complexity.
**Workaround:** None beyond manual, row-by-row cross-referencing between tabs; Excel does not
support or validate the entries, and the customer must also fill in the redundant fields
manually.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant raises this
repeatedly, unprompted, with specific concrete examples (variant/facility duplication, the
A2/A3 sterilization-method lookup, and a 2,000-3,000-row customer) and an explicit, confident
statement that errors result.

**Severity/Confidence flag:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (single interview) triggers
`validation_status: needs-cross-interview-validation` per [[Definitions]]
"Severity/Confidence flag." This is a single-interview finding at High severity and should not
be treated as validated for prioritization until confirmed by a second interview.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 6
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Das ist ja wirklich eine Datenbank beziehungsweise wird Excel hier als Datenbank missbraucht. Und wenn man sich überlegt, dass der Kunde alles manuell ausfüllen muss, ist schon wirklich großes Kino." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "This is really a database, or rather Excel is being misused here as a database. And when you consider that the customer has to fill everything in manually, that's really something else." - [P07]

> "Das sind redundante Informationen und hier ist auch die Granularität, die ich in Frage stelle. Wir haben hier immer wieder dasselbe Produkt, allerdings haben wir hier in verschiedenen Varianten. ... Aber jedes einzelne wird hier divers immer wieder hinterlegt, also als Zeile vom Kunden auszufüllen und sogar die MDN-Codes, MDS-Codes bis MDT sind eigentlich alle identisch." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "These are redundant pieces of information, and this is also where I question the granularity. We have the same product again and again here, but in different variants. ... Yet every single one is entered here separately, as a row for the customer to fill in, and even the MDN codes, MDS codes, up to MDT are actually all identical." - [P07]

> "Die Codes sind bei allen Varianten selbstverständlich identisch. ... Pro Zeile, ja. Also wenn es jetzt so ein paar Sachen sind, so zehn Zeilen, dann ist das nicht so schlimm. Aber bei diesem Kunden, der hat über 2000 oder 3000 Zeilen." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "The codes are of course identical across all variants. ... Per row. If it's just a handful of rows, say ten, that's not so bad. But this customer has over 2,000 or 3,000 rows." - [P07]

> "Ich bin mir hundertprozentig sicher, dass wir auch definitiv Fehler haben, sowohl in den Zertifikaten als auch in den Audit-Registrierungen, weil das kannst du nicht mehr menschlich abdecken." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I am one hundred percent certain that we definitely have errors, both in the certificates and in the audit registrations, because you can no longer cover that by hand." - [P07]

> "Diese Tabs A2, A3, hier sind Sterisupplier hinterlegt mit bestimmten Sterilisationsmethoden. ... Hier 1, 2, 3 trifft zu, dann muss ich wieder in den anderen Tab schauen. Und was ist 1, 2, 3?" - [P07]
>
> Translation: "These tabs A2, A3 hold sterilization suppliers along with certain sterilization methods. ... Here 1, 2, 3 applies, then I have to look at the other tab again. And what is 1, 2, 3?" - [P07]

> "Ich habe vor fünf Jahren angefangen und ich habe erst im dritten Jahr damit gearbeitet, weil ich habe es vorher gar nicht verstanden. ... dieses Tool macht aus der vorhandenen Komplexität also etwas, was einfach Quatsch ist." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I started five years ago and only worked with it from the third year onward, because I didn't understand it before that at all. ... this tool turns the existing complexity into something that is simply nonsensical." - [P07]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Normalize Appendix ABC's data model so identical master data (e.g. codes shared across
  variants of the same product) is captured once rather than repeated per row, converging with
  the broader digitization vision logged under
  [[Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]].
  Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other Customer Specialists/Project Coordinators also report that
Appendix ABC's per-variant, per-facility row structure forces redundant re-entry of identical
master data and manual cross-tab decoding, and do they independently suspect resulting errors
in certificates or audit registrations?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Archival processing is deprioritized and often left incomplete, complicating customer handovers between staff

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Archival/handover processing (referred to as "PSC") is treated as the lowest
priority among a Customer Specialist's activities and is often left incomplete. When a
customer or project is reassigned to another staff member (due to turnover, leave, or
reorganization), the successor must reconstruct the customer's status from multiple systems
because the archival record is incomplete.
**Trigger:** The interviewer asks about archival/handover experiences and what would help.
**Impact:** Incomplete archival records make it harder for a successor to quickly understand a
customer's status when a handover happens, which the participant estimates occurs at least
once a year (e.g. due to staff turnover, maternity leave, or reorganization). This is
particularly difficult for assessments left in progress, since most of the work has already
been done by the departing colleague and is hard to pick up without context.
**Workaround:** Successors reconstruct customer status by checking multiple separate systems
(a CRM-like tool referred to as "CBW", Appendix ABC, and a project system referred to as
"Medici"), and, where possible, request a handover call with the departing colleague.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes a specific,
recurring mechanism (deprioritized archival work causing reconstruction effort at handover)
with a stated frequency (at least once a year) and concrete detail about which systems are
involved.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 4
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P04

**Representative Quotes:**
> "One thing that I challenge a little bit because it is one thing that I leave as the last things in my activities as customer specialist is archival processing PSC. That is, I mean, really crucial. But I mean, to the my priorities, I mean the least because I tried to, let's say, close the project and then set up the archival." - [P04]

> "So maybe I just received a customer from another colleague's customer specialist. I just jumped on a PSC and the archivation is not complete. So a support would be good, especially when you need to, let's say, move project or customer to other customer specialist or RM." - [P04]

> "I would say in a year, let's say it happens at least once, probably surely once every year. In some cases, even more, but it is, let's say, not time triggered, but even triggered. For example, something is somebody's leaving or maternity leave or everything. There is a reorganization. So you need to be, let's say, rapid in taking the customer and knowing how you can retrieve all their information to start immediately." - [P04]

> "For this assessment is quite, let's say, as let's say, for example, assessor, it happens to me that I a colleague was in maternity leave and I pick up the assessment. That is quite complicated. ... Probably, yes, most critical could be assessment left behind because they are most difficult to be, let's say, taken by the assessor because most part of the assessment have been done. ... probably the best would be yes a call, a call just I mean the quickest way would be a call just to show how to where to link how the process it is." - [P04]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Built-in archival/handover support that consolidates customer status across systems (e.g.
  CBW, Appendix ABC, Medici) so a successor does not need to manually reconstruct it (P04).
  Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other Customer Specialists also deprioritize archival/handover
processing (e.g. PSC) relative to other tasks, and does this recur at a similar frequency (at
least once a year) when customers or projects are reassigned?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Assessors do not reliably mark subcontracts ready or follow committed timelines

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Some assessors do not reliably set their subcontracts to "ready" once
finished, and separately do not reliably keep to committed timelines, instead postponing as
they see fit (including last-minute vacation notices). Because partial invoicing depends on a
subcontract being marked ready/booked, the Project Coordinator cannot tell whether a task is
actually due or still open, and must manually follow up.
**Trigger:** A Project Coordinator needs to confirm whether an assessor's subcontract is
complete in order to create a partial invoice, or needs to track whether a committed timeline
will be met.
**Impact:** The participant describes this as "a constant chasing" for Project Coordinators.
Partial invoices cannot be created until everything is booked, so non-compliance directly
delays billing. The participant states that timeline adjustments happen on every project, once
or twice.
**Workaround:** Manually following up with assessors to check status and confirm bookings
before invoicing.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes this as a
routine, repeated, unprompted observation with a specific example (last-minute vacation
notices) and a stated frequency ("once or twice" per project).

**Severity/Confidence flag:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (single interview) triggers
`validation_status: needs-cross-interview-validation` per [[Definitions]]
"Severity/Confidence flag." This is a single-interview finding at High severity and should not
be treated as validated for prioritization until confirmed by a second interview.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Für uns Projektkoordinatoren ist es echt ein Hinterherlaufen, weil manche Bewerter setzen ihre Unteraufträge nicht auf ready. Ich weiß nicht, ob das jetzt fällig ist oder ob da noch was offen ist. ... Kann ich erst eine Teilrechnung erstellen, wenn es gebucht ist, alles." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "For us Project Coordinators it really is a constant chasing, because some assessors don't set their subcontracts to 'ready.' I don't know whether it's now due or whether something is still open. ... I can only create a partial invoice once everything has been booked." - [P07]

> "Bewerter halten sich nicht daran. Sie ignorieren es. Und verschieben einfach so, wie sie Lust haben. Und tatsächlich kommt auch manchmal eine E-Mail: Hey, ich bin im Urlaub, kann ich erst einen Monat später machen. ... Also das passiert schon bei jedem Projekt ein, zwei Mal, dass Timelines angepasst werden." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "Assessors don't stick to it. They ignore it. And just postpone as they please. And sometimes an e-mail actually comes in: hey, I'm on vacation, can I only do it a month later. ... So this happens on every project, once or twice, that timelines get adjusted." - [P07]
