notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Mace Audit generates incorrect finding documents from certain screens with no way to correct them

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Mace Audit, the existing internal audit tool now mandatory for all auditors,
has non-linear, unintuitive navigation that makes some functions hard to locate. On top of
this, writing a finding from the tool's findings screen generates an incorrect output
document, with no warning beforehand and no way to correct the document afterward.

**Severity/Confidence flag:** This finding is rated Severity Critical (it produces a corrupted
official audit output document with no correction path, meeting the Definitions.md Critical
criterion "causes data loss/errors") but is supported by only one interview, giving Confidence
Medium (Single-interview strong evidence). Per the Severity/Confidence flag hierarchy in
[[Definitions]], single-interview support takes precedence regardless of severity, so
`validation_status: needs-cross-interview-validation` is set. This combination (Critical
severity, non-High confidence) still carries elevated prioritization risk and should not be
deprioritized purely because `validation_status` reads as a single-interview flag; it should
be treated as a candidate for urgent cross-interview validation given the potential impact of
corrupted audit outputs.

**Trigger:** The auditor writes an audit finding using the tool's findings screen during or
after an audit.
**Impact:** The generated finding document is incorrect, and the tool provides no indication
this will happen and no mechanism to correct the output once generated. The participant
discovered this only after the fact, on her most recent audit. She separately notes that
non-linear navigation ("you jump around all over the place") makes the tool generally hard to
use, independent of this specific defect. She also reports that auditors, including the cert
body stakeholder responsible for a specific scheme's regulatory compliance, were not consulted
before the tool was made mandatory, and that the tool did not meet that stakeholder's
regulatory requirements at the time of mandate.
**Workaround:** None described; the participant now avoids generating findings from that
specific screen, but only because she happened to discover the defect.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes the defect,
how she discovered it, and its irreversibility directly and specifically.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 3
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P05

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Mace audit is awful. It is unintuitive. You have to jump around to too many screens. Things are labeled in weird ways that don't make sense. There's a ... menu on the top when you're in an audit screen that ... says start to end ... You would think that ... each of those menu items is a linear progression through the audit ... No, absolutely not. You jump around all over the place." - [P05]

> "I found out on my most recent audit last week that there's a findings screen and you can write findings from that screen. But if you do, the system will generate them wrong. There is nothing that tells you that [and] there is nothing to prevent you from doing that. But if you generate a finding from the finding screen, it'll be wrong and your output document will be wrong. And there's no way to correct it at that point." - [P05]

> "The thing that I hate most about Mace is how much potential it has that is going unrealized right now. This should be an amazing, helpful tool for us, but it's a disaster that actually makes our jobs harder." - [P05]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
[None logged; the participant did not propose a specific fix beyond wanting the tool's
existing potential to be realized.]

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: New-customer requests proceed without an upfront technical feasibility review

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** When a new customer is acquired, Sales can promise a scope or timeline
without a technical feasibility review taking place first. The technical side of the request
can be under-assessed at intake, especially when Sales has a financial incentive to close the
deal.
**Trigger:** A new customer is acquired, sometimes via outsourcing or corporate restructuring
(e.g. a large company outsourcing part of its business), and Sales commits to a scope before a
technical review of feasibility occurs.
**Impact:** The participant reports this can involve financial magnitudes not visible at
intake, and that problems "can become quite problematic" later in the project, including for
customer satisfaction. This has not personally happened to the participant, but is described
as a known risk pattern.
**Workaround:** None described; the gap is structural (Sales-led intake without a mandatory
technical feasibility gate).
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes this as a
known, recurring risk pattern in new-customer acquisition, not a one-off anecdote.

**Severity/Confidence flag:** Severity High with Confidence Medium (single interview) triggers
the flag in [[Definitions]] "Severity/Confidence flag," rule 1. This finding carries a
Severity/Confidence risk: the downstream cost and customer-satisfaction impact described could
be significant, but is based on one interview and requires cross-interview validation before
being prioritized as a confirmed, high-severity mechanism rather than an occasional edge case.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Es ist mir persönlich nicht passiert, aber ja, es geht teilweise wirklich um finanzielle Größenordnungen, die man nicht auf dem Schirm hat, zum Beispiel Konzernumstrukturierung, wenn da was outgesourced wird ... die natürlich erstmal die Aufgabe haben und auch eine gewisse Initiative finanziell natürlich sehen ... aber dann fällt das Fachliche vielleicht ein bisschen runter. ... im Nachgang kann es ziemlich problematisch werden und auch für die Kundenzufriedenheit natürlich." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "It hasn't happened to me personally, but yes, it partly really does concern financial magnitudes you don't have on your radar — for example corporate restructuring, if something gets outsourced ... if Sales promises something, since they naturally have that objective and also see a certain financial incentive ... but then the technical side maybe falls by the wayside a bit. ... afterward it can become quite problematic, also for customer satisfaction." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)

[None currently logged.]

technical feasibility check, leading to problems later in the project?

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: No automated reminder prompts customers to respond to deficiency reports within the expected timeframe

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** After a deficiency report is issued, no tool automatically tracks or reminds
the customer to respond within the expected timeframe (e.g. 60 days). Certification staff
track this manually.
**Trigger:** The interviewer asks what would be useful to support planning and tracking of
assessments; the participant raises the difficulty of standardizing customer response times to
deficiency reports.
**Impact:** Certification staff must personally track and chase overdue deficiency-report
responses, an activity the participant identifies as one of the most difficult parts of the
Customer Specialist role. Offsite assessment milestones are effectively defined by deficiency
report issuance and response, so the lack of tracking support affects overall assessment
planning.
**Workaround:** The participant manually sets personal Outlook reminders to prompt herself to
follow up with the customer.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes a specific,
concrete, and recurring mechanism (manual Outlook reminders compensating for the absence of any
tool support) tied directly to a named difficulty of the role, rather than a general or
speculative complaint.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 3
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P04

**Representative Quotes:**
> "I think that one of the difficulties, I mean, the challenges that, let's say, customer specialist probably ever is that I mean also standardize the time to receive the responses from deficiency report. It's it's difficult." - [P04]

> "I don't know if it is worth, let's say, that once it is scheduled ... I'm doing manually now, let's say putting a sort of in outlook some reminder to to ask the customer, let's say responses of the deficiency reports. So I mean would be good something that let's say or remind us as customer specialist to. Or for example, something that directly and independently remind the customer that they need to ... we said that the responses should be provided in the 60 days." - [P04]

> "Because I mean relevant, let's say in offsite assessment, I mean I can consider that milestone for assessment is the deficiency report points and responses. So once you have something that, let's say, pop out, for example, deficiency report directly, or let's say a reminder would be good." - [P04]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- An automated reminder sent directly and independently to the customer once the expected
  response window (e.g. 60 days) is approaching or has elapsed, rather than relying on staff
  to chase manually (P04). Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other Customer Specialists / TD assessors also rely on manual,
personal reminders (e.g. Outlook) to chase customer responses to deficiency reports, and would
an automated reminder directly to the customer be seen as useful across accounts?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff

**Update (2026-08-11):** Confidence Basis Single-interview → Multi-interview; theme link added
(Standalone preliminary finding → confirmed theme); P02 quotes and interview ID added;
`validation_status` changed from `needs-cross-interview-validation` to
`needs-validation-before-prioritization` per the 2+ interview Severity High / Confidence
Medium flag rule ([[Definitions]] "Severity/Confidence flag," rule 2).

**Update (2026-08-12):** P03 adds a third, independent confirmation of the same mechanism (a
self-maintained Excel status list compensating for the lack of a built-in view, and an explicit
wish to see "whose turn it is" without manually chasing colleagues). Per [[Definitions]]
"Sample-relative check," 3 of 3 interviews processed so far directly and consistently confirm
this mechanism (ratio 100%, well above the 25% threshold), so Confidence is raised from Medium
to High. With Confidence now High, neither condition in [[Definitions]]
"Severity/Confidence flag" applies, so `validation_status` and `validation_question` are
removed from the frontmatter. Priority Tier recalculated to P0 (Severity High x Confidence
High) in `03_pains/_register.md`.

**Update (2026-08-12, same day):** P04 adds a fourth confirming interview: no company-provided
tool exists to track Technical Documentation (TD) assessment or Change Notification progress
(only a personal, regional planning tool used for audits); the existing Assessment Plan Cloud
(APC) tool is described as static, not showing live deficiency-report status. Confidence
remains High (4 of 4 interviews, 100%).

**Update (2026-08-13):** P07 adds a fifth confirming interview, from a Project Coordinator
(commercial/backoffice) segment: PSE version 2.0 is described as harder to keep an overview
with than PSE 1.0, requiring a recurring biweekly team meeting to manually walk through all
open projects, plus a personal, informally-used "Aktionen" (actions/notes) feature as a
workaround; timeline and hours/booking-status information are additionally split into two
disconnected PSE areas that must be manually cross-referenced. Per [[Definitions]]
"Sample-relative check," 5 of 7 interviews processed so far (71%) directly and consistently
confirm this mechanism; Confidence remains High.

**Update (2026-08-14):** P08 adds a sixth confirming interview, from a Client Manager & Lead
Auditor segment: two separate, personally-built filters are required to track status (a
personal time filter in BSE for individual to-dos, and a project-manager filter in PSE for
oversight across a team of experts); an upcoming PSE master-data reduction is a specific,
named concern because it would remove status detail the participant currently relies on for
oversight, forcing more internal communication as a substitute; and a wish is expressed for a
single graphical (Gantt-style) status view directly in UCI (an internal customer portal). Per
[[Definitions]] "Sample-relative check," 6 of 8 interviews processed so far (75%) directly and
consistently confirm this mechanism; Confidence remains High.

**Theme:** [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]
**Description:** There is no consolidated view showing where a project or application
currently stands in the certification process (comparable to a package-tracking view). P01
currently learns about status changes only through informal channels ("experts"), and only
for projects self-selected or specialist-selected as critical, not systematically. P02
confirms the same mechanism from the assessor side: an existing tool (PSE 2.0) can show status
only when tasks are consistently maintained and timelines kept up to date; when this discipline
is absent (worse for internationally-coordinated tasks routed through BSC/Global BSC), the
participant has no overview at all.
**Trigger:** Staff want to know the current status of a certification request or project,
especially for high-priority or internationally-coordinated accounts.
**Impact:** P01 states this costs significant time for many people, with status awareness
limited to a subset of projects flagged informally as critical. P02 states that without
consistent maintenance, project overview is lost entirely, which particularly affects
international projects. P03 maintains a personal, manually-updated Excel list (inherited from
her predecessor) tracking project number, module-level timelines, communication channel used,
and task ownership, specifically to avoid losing track of the last status. P04 relies on a
personal, regional planning tool for audits, but has no company-provided tool at all for TD
assessment or Change Notification tracking, and reports risking loss of "the overall picture"
on assessments that run in parallel for six to nine months. P07 reports that PSE 2.0 is
genuinely harder to keep an overview with than PSE 1.0, relies on a recurring biweekly team
meeting to walk through all open projects together with a colleague, and separately describes
the split between the timeline area and the hours/booking-status area as forcing constant
manual back-and-forth between the two. P08 relies on two separate, personally-built filters (a
time filter in BSE for personal to-dos; a project-manager filter in PSE for team oversight)
and is concerned that an upcoming reduction in PSE master data will remove status detail
currently relied upon, requiring more internal communication as a substitute.
**Workaround:** P01 relies on the assigned Customer Specialist or other experts to flag and
report status on selected "critical" projects; no systematic tracking otherwise. P02 relies on
whichever staff happen to keep PSE 2.0 tasks and timelines current. P03 relies on a
self-maintained Excel list built up over time rather than any built-in tool. P04 relies on a
personal, regionally-built planning tool for audits and has no equivalent support for TD
assessment or Change Notification tracking. P07 relies on a recurring biweekly team meeting
and an informally-used "Aktionen" note feature within PSE, which she describes as inconvenient
to use for quick notes. P08 relies on two separately-built filters across two tools (BSE and
PSE) rather than a single consolidated view.
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). For traceability: 6 of 8 interviews processed so far (P01, P02, P03, P04, P07, P08)
directly and consistently evidence the same mechanism, satisfying both the repetition and
sample-relative checks in [[Definitions]].

**Severity/Confidence flag:** Not applicable. Severity High with Confidence High does not meet
either condition in [[Definitions]] "Severity/Confidence flag"; no `validation_status` is set.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 13
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P01, P02, P03, P04, P07, P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Tracking von Projektstatus ist mit Sicherheit eine wichtige Sache. wenn man das hier einbauen könnte wie bei einem DHL Paket, in welchem Status wir uns befinden, wo das Paket sich gerade befindet." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Tracking the project status is certainly an important thing, if one could build this in like a DHL package, [showing] what status we are in, where the package currently is." - [P01]

> "Über die Experten für die kritischen Projekte, ich will sie ja gar nicht für alle mitkriegen." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Through the experts, for the critical projects, I don't want to be informed about all of them anyway." - [P01]

> "Ich denke, die Zahlen zu erfassen, sage ich mal so, also für Traceability auf jeden Fall gut. ... Also Monitoring von den Daten würde ich auf jeden Fall sinnvoll halten." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "I think capturing the numbers is, let's say, definitely good for traceability. ... So I would definitely consider monitoring the data useful." - [P02]

> "Wenn das so gehandhabt wird [Tasks nur zum Buchen angelegt], dann habe ich eigentlich keinerlei Übersicht mehr. Aber wenn es aber gepflegt wird und auch die Timelines angepasst werden, dann kann ich sehr gut nutzen, um Übersicht zu haben." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "If it's handled that way [tasks only created for booking hours], then I actually have no overview at all anymore. But if it is maintained and the timelines are also adjusted, then I can use it very well to have an overview." - [P02]

> "Das wär tatsächlich ganz cool, ehrlich gesagt. Ich habe das nicht. ... das wäre schon tatsächlich cool, wenn das irgendwie übersichtlicher dargestellt werden könnte." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "That would actually be pretty cool, honestly. I don't have that. ... it would actually be cool if that could be displayed in a clearer way." - [P03]

> "Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet, dass ich irgendwie sehe, was ist gerade meine Aufgabe ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "What I would actually want ... is something that really depicts this workflow, so I can see what my current task is ... whose turn it is, so to speak." - [P03]

> "Surely for what regard the changes and assessment, I think there is a, there is a, let's say, void or lack in following planning. ... I have no tool proposed by to suit the tool. I need to let's say rely on my own, let's say scheduling for following the project." - [P04]

> "You may, I mean, if you don't have something that supports you, you may, I mean, lose the overall picture of how you are going." - [P04]

> "I think in the APC you can upload the sampling plan, but it's, let's say, not rolling, it's a static... you don't know if you have a deficiency report ongoing when you expect from the customer to, let's say, to push." - [P04]

> "Ich muss tatsächlich sagen, mit PSE 2.0 ist es echt schwierig den Überblick zu behalten. Weil bei PSE1 war das relativ easy ... Ich habe auch mit allen, sie essen alle zwei Wochen ein Meeting, um alle offenen Projekte durchzugehen." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I really have to say, with PSE 2.0 it is genuinely difficult to keep an overview. Because with PSE 1 that was relatively easy ... We also have, every two weeks, a meeting to go through all open projects." - [P07]

> "Ich finde es ganz schrecklich, dass hier zwei Bereiche sind, einmal mit Timeline, einmal mit Stunden. ... das sehe ich hier oben einfach nicht. Aber hier oben sehe ich die Timeline, also das ist totaler Quatsch." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I find it really terrible that there are two separate areas here, one with the timeline, one with the hours. ... I simply don't see that up here. But up here I see the timeline — so that's complete nonsense." - [P07]

> "Darüber hinaus, was schön wäre, wenn ich alles in UCI direkt hätte, weil UCI einfach die Möglichkeit hat, das Ganze grafisch noch mal so ein bisschen abzubilden. Ich hätte gern mein [Gantt]-Diagramm, wo ich mein einzelnes Projekt sehe und genau weiß, darunter ist es." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Beyond that, it would be nice if I had everything directly in UCI, because UCI simply has the option of depicting the whole thing graphically a bit better. I'd like my Gantt chart, where I see my individual project and know exactly [where it stands]." - [P08]

> "Als Projektmanager sehe ich das tatsächlich kritisch, weil ich dann Informationen verliere. ... Wenn es weniger Informationen werden, muss ich mehr intern kommunizieren." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "As a project manager I actually see that critically, because then I lose information. ... If there's less information, I have to communicate more internally." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A priority/escalation button (deliberately avoiding the word "escalation") tied into a
  request-to-decision time metric, to raise disputes or decisions that need resolution.
  Explicitly unvalidated.
- Exposing status tracking to customers as an optional, separately licensed module was
  mentioned but flagged by the participant as ethically ambiguous ("fishy"). Explicitly
  unvalidated.
- Phase-level time traceability/monitoring independent of manual timeline maintenance (P02).
  Explicitly unvalidated.
- An end-to-end workflow view showing whose turn it is to act, so staff do not have to
  manually chase colleagues for the next step (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A single main working area combining timeline and hours/booking status in one view, rather
  than requiring staff to switch between two disconnected PSE areas; the participant
  explicitly prefers improving the existing tool over introducing a new one (P07). Explicitly
  unvalidated.

> "Tracking von Projektstatus ist mit Sicherheit eine wichtige Sache. wenn man das hier einbauen könnte wie bei einem DHL Paket, in welchem Status wir uns befinden, wo das Paket sich gerade befindet." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Tracking the project status is certainly an important thing, if one could build this in like a DHL package, [showing] what status we are in, where the package currently is." - [P01]

> "Über die Experten für die kritischen Projekte, ich will sie ja gar nicht für alle mitkriegen." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Through the experts, for the critical projects, I don't want to be informed about all of them anyway." - [P01]

> "Ich denke, die Zahlen zu erfassen, sage ich mal so, also für Traceability auf jeden Fall gut. ... Also Monitoring von den Daten würde ich auf jeden Fall sinnvoll halten." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "I think capturing the numbers is, let's say, definitely good for traceability. ... So I would definitely consider monitoring the data useful." - [P02]

> "Wenn das so gehandhabt wird [Tasks nur zum Buchen angelegt], dann habe ich eigentlich keinerlei Übersicht mehr. Aber wenn es aber gepflegt wird und auch die Timelines angepasst werden, dann kann ich sehr gut nutzen, um Übersicht zu haben." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "If it's handled that way [tasks only created for booking hours], then I actually have no overview at all anymore. But if it is maintained and the timelines are also adjusted, then I can use it very well to have an overview." - [P02]

> "Das wär tatsächlich ganz cool, ehrlich gesagt. Ich habe das nicht. ... das wäre schon tatsächlich cool, wenn das irgendwie übersichtlicher dargestellt werden könnte." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "That would actually be pretty cool, honestly. I don't have that. ... it would actually be cool if that could be displayed in a clearer way." - [P03]

> "Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet, dass ich irgendwie sehe, was ist gerade meine Aufgabe ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "What I would actually want ... is something that really depicts this workflow, so I can see what my current task is ... whose turn it is, so to speak." - [P03]

> "Surely for what regard the changes and assessment, I think there is a, there is a, let's say, void or lack in following planning. ... I have no tool proposed by to suit the tool. I need to let's say rely on my own, let's say scheduling for following the project." - [P04]

> "You may, I mean, if you don't have something that supports you, you may, I mean, lose the overall picture of how you are going." - [P04]

> "I think in the APC you can upload the sampling plan, but it's, let's say, not rolling, it's a static... you don't know if you have a deficiency report ongoing when you expect from the customer to, let's say, to push." - [P04]

>
> Translation: "I really have to say, with PSE 2.0 it is genuinely difficult to keep an overview. Because with PSE 1 that was relatively easy ... We also have, every two weeks, a meeting to go through all open projects." - [P07]

> "Ich finde es ganz schrecklich, dass hier zwei Bereiche sind, einmal mit Timeline, einmal mit Stunden. ... das sehe ich hier oben einfach nicht. Aber hier oben sehe ich die Timeline, also das ist totaler Quatsch." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I find it really terrible that there are two separate areas here, one with the timeline, one with the hours. ... I simply don't see that up here. But up here I see the timeline — so that's complete nonsense." - [P07]

> "Darüber hinaus, was schön wäre, wenn ich alles in UCI direkt hätte, weil UCI einfach die Möglichkeit hat, das Ganze grafisch noch mal so ein bisschen abzubilden. Ich hätte gern mein [Gantt]-Diagramm, wo ich mein einzelnes Projekt sehe und genau weiß, darunter ist es." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Beyond that, it would be nice if I had everything directly in UCI, because UCI simply has the option of depicting the whole thing graphically a bit better. I'd like my Gantt chart, where I see my individual project and know exactly [where it stands]." - [P08]

> "Als Projektmanager sehe ich das tatsächlich kritisch, weil ich dann Informationen verliere. ... Wenn es weniger Informationen werden, muss ich mehr intern kommunizieren." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "As a project manager I actually see that critically, because then I lose information. ... If there's less information, I have to communicate more internally." - [P08]

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: No official cost calculation template exists for several service types, forcing reliance on informal tools

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** TD (technical documentation) Assessment has an official cost-calculation tool
("PPS") and Audit has an official "Effort Calculation" tool, but Supplier Audit and Change
Notification cost/hour calculation are not covered by any official template. Staff instead use
an unofficial Wiki-based template that is not part of the official Working Instructions or
ROXPA (the process documentation system).
**Trigger:** The participant needs to calculate cost/hours for a Supplier Audit or a Change
Notification.
**Impact:** The calculation is done informally ("aus dem Daumen geschüttelt" — improvised),
without an official, validated basis, for two service types.
**Workaround:** Using an unofficial Wiki template not covered by ROXPA or the Working
Instructions.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes this
directly and unprompted, naming the specific service types affected and the specific
unofficial tool used.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Bei mir ist es auch oft so, dass ich irgendwie Supplier Audit kalkuliere, da kann ich mir wieder anscheinend alles aus dem Daumen schütteln ... Genauso ist es tatsächlich bei Change Notifications, da gibt es nicht so eine richtig offizielle Vorlage. ... das ist nichts, was in ROXPA ist und so ein bisschen inoffiziell läuft." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "For me it's often the case that I sort of calculate a Supplier Audit out of thin air ... it's the same for Change Notifications, there isn't really an official template. ... it's not in ROXPA [the official process documentation system] and runs a bit unofficially." - [P03]

> "Fände tatsächlich eigentlich ganz cool, wenn es für alle Situationen irgendwie was offizielles gibt." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "I would actually find it pretty nice if there were something official for all situations." - [P03]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Publishing an official cost/hour calculation template for Supplier Audits and Change
  Notifications, integrated into ROXPA/the Working Instructions like the existing PPS and
  Effort Calculation tools (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other staff who calculate costs for Supplier Audits or Change
Notifications also lack an official template and rely on informal, unofficial tools?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: No shared access to the current Appendix ABC version forces staff to rely on colleagues

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** There is no single, shared point of access where staff can retrieve a
customer's current Appendix ABC version directly. Instead, the participant currently asks the
Customer Specialist or Relationship Manager, who usually knows where the latest version is.
This works in practice, but depends on that person's availability.
**Trigger:** An assessor needs the current version of a customer's Appendix ABC to begin or
continue an assessment.
**Impact:** Retrieving the current document depends on a specific colleague's availability;
the participant notes this costs time when that person is, for example, on vacation.
**Workaround:** Asking the Customer Specialist or Relationship Manager directly, who usually
knows the current location/version.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes both the
current workaround and its dependency cost directly.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Wenn der Appendix ABC in der aktuellen Version für alle zugänglich wäre oder aufrufbar wäre. Also ich weiß, mit einem Klick, da finde ich von dem Kunden den aktuellen Appendix ABC, dass ich den schon mal hätte." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "If the current version of the Appendix ABC were accessible or retrievable for everyone. So I mean, with one click, I could find the customer's current Appendix ABC, so I'd already have it." - [P02]

> "Momentan frag ich auch immer den Customer Specialist oder Relationship Manager, weil der weiß meistens, wo ist die aktuellste Version von Appendix ABC. Das funktioniert gut, würde ich sagen, aber kostet natürlich auch ein bisschen, wenn der gerade im Urlaub ist." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Currently I always ask the Customer Specialist or Relationship Manager, because they usually know where the most current version of Appendix ABC is. That works well, I'd say, but of course it also costs a bit of time if that person happens to be on vacation." - [P02]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A one-click, single point of access to a customer's current Appendix ABC version (P02).
  Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other assessors also lack a single point of access to a customer's
current Appendix ABC version and rely on asking colleagues instead?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: No single accountable point of contact for cross-department cost estimation input

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** When calculating a project's cost, the participant must call multiple people
(five to seven) across departments to gather input, since no single accountable point of
contact exists per department. The people reached do not always share the same view within
their own team and do not always have decision authority, even when working on the project.
**Trigger:** A cost calculation for a project requires input from multiple departments.
**Impact:** The participant describes this as inefficient: repeated calls to several people per
calculation, inconsistent views within a team, and contacts who lack decision authority despite
working on the project.
**Workaround:** Calling several people per department each time and reconciling their answers
manually.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes this as the
standard, recurring current practice ("every time, right now") rather than a one-off event.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Jedes Mal, also im Moment, so ich kalkuliere das und rufe dann fünf, sechs, sieben Leute an, die auch nicht in ihren Teams unbedingt immer dieselbe Ansicht haben, gegebenenfalls auch nicht die Entscheidungsgewalt mit sich bringen, obwohl sie das Projekt bearbeiten. Auch das ist ineffizient. Wenn da eine Person in jeder Abteilung sitzt, die das macht und auch entsprechend die Verantwortung dafür übernehmen darf, wäre für mich wesentlich effizient." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Every time, so right now I calculate this and then call five, six, seven people, who also don't necessarily always have the same view within their teams, and sometimes don't carry decision authority even though they're working on the project. That's also inefficient. If one person sat in every department who does this and is also allowed to take responsibility for it accordingly, that would be much more efficient for me." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Designating a single accountable point of contact per department for cost-estimation input,
  with the authority to answer or decide directly, instead of the participant needing to call
  several people per department (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other staff calculating project costs also need to call multiple
people across departments due to the lack of a single accountable point of contact per
department?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

# Pain Point: Project Coordinator and customer communication effort is not reflected in commercial cost calculation

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Project hours mainly grow with customer-facing communication, since internal
communication cannot be billed and is treated as irrelevant from a cost standpoint. However,
the effort Project Coordinators (PCs) spend — including on internal coordination — and detailed
customer communication are both not captured in the commercial cost calculation.
**Trigger:** A project involves substantial PC coordination effort or detailed customer
communication that goes beyond what the cost calculation model accounts for.
**Impact:** The participant states this effort "is still not captured," meaning PC time and
detailed customer communication effort are not reflected in what is billed, though the
downstream financial or workload impact is not further quantified in this interview.
**Workaround:** None described.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant states this as a
current, ongoing gap in the cost-calculation model ("nach wie vor nicht abgebildet" / "still
not captured"), not a one-off event.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Die Projekte explodieren von den Stunden her nur, wir viel Kommunikation zwischen Kunden und uns haben. Die internen Sachen können wir eh nicht verrechnen, deswegen sollten die von der Informationsseite eigentlich irrelevant sein. ... Was nach wie vor nicht abgebildet ist, sind natürlich die Sachen, die die PCs aufwenden, die gegebenenfalls auch intern an Kommunikation und so weiter angehen. Und auch die Kundenkommunikation ist nicht detailliert abgebildet." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Projects only explode in hours when we have a lot of communication between the customer and us. We can't bill the internal things anyway, so from an information standpoint they should actually be irrelevant. ... What is still not captured, of course, is the effort the PCs spend, which sometimes also concerns internal communication and so on. And the customer communication also isn't captured in detail." - [P08]

frontmatter.name: Reactive first-come-first-serve task assignment creates workload imbalance among assessors
frontmatter.validation_question: Do other assessors also experience uneven workload because tasks are assigned strictly first-come-first-served without capacity balancing?

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Reactive first-come-first-serve task assignment creates workload imbalance among assessors

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** New work items are assigned strictly first-come-first-served, typically by
email or tool notification, without any capacity or workload balancing. An assessor who is
occupied on another project when a task is posted, and who therefore does not respond within
the first few minutes, effectively loses the opportunity to take it, regardless of their
actual availability afterward.
**Trigger:** A new task/project is posted for assignment while the assessor is occupied
elsewhere and cannot respond within the first few minutes.
**Impact:** Workload becomes unevenly distributed across assessors over time, independent of
actual capacity.
**Workaround:** None described; the participant checks for new tasks the next time they are
free, by which point available tasks are usually already taken.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant identifies this
mechanism directly and unprompted as a likely cause of workload imbalance.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P02

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Weil meistens komme ich erst, wenn ich am Projekt sitz, sag ich mal, am Ende des Tages dazu, da reinzuschauen am nächsten Tag, und dann merkt man eigentlich, dass, wenn man nicht in den ersten ein, zwei, drei oder fünf Minuten klickt, ist es eigentlich schon weg. Ja, das ich denke, das könnte auch schon mal ein Punkt sein, der zu einer Ungleichverteilung von der Arbeitslast führt." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Because usually I only get to look at it the next day, at the end of the day when I'm sitting on a project, and then you notice that if you don't click within the first one, two, three, or five minutes, it's basically already gone. Yes, I think that could also be a point that leads to an uneven distribution of workload." - [P02]

> "Ich denke auf jeden Fall besser als First Come for Serve schon mal 'n Zeitfenster, wir haben meinten meine erste Idee, sag ich mal, 24 Stunden, und dann sieht man, wer klickt, und dann müssen es vielleicht Experten entscheiden ... wer da wirklich am wenigsten Auslastung von den Leuten, die dann zugesagt haben." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "I think a time window would definitely be better than first-come-first-serve — my first idea would be 24 hours — and then you see who clicks, and then maybe experts need to decide ... who among those who accepted really has the least workload." - [P02]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Replace immediate first-come-first-serve claiming with a fixed response window (e.g. 24
  hours), after which assignment is decided based on relative workload among those who
  responded. Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other assessors also experience uneven workload because tasks are
assigned strictly first-come-first-served without capacity balancing?

**Related Evidence (2026-08-13):** P07 separately describes a distinct, adjacent allocation
mechanism at the customer-account level rather than the individual audit-task level:
customer accounts are currently assigned informally, on a first-available basis, without
domain-fit criteria, particularly following a period of high staff attrition. This is logged
here as related evidence only; it does not increase this pain point's interview count or
confidence. See
[[Customer accounts are assigned informally without domain-fit criteria following staff attrition]].

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.title: Rigid step-by-step process sequencing blocks parallel work on priority projects

frontmatter.name: Rigid step-by-step process sequencing blocks parallel work on priority projects
frontmatter.validation_question: Do other staff handling priority/expedited projects also need to work process steps in parallel rather than strictly sequentially, and would a digital tool need to support that flexibility?

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Rigid step-by-step process sequencing blocks parallel work on priority projects

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** The standard certification process requires steps to be completed strictly in
sequence (e.g. not starting work without complete application documents and a purchase order).
For priority projects, staff need to work several steps in parallel to meet urgency, which the
current process/tooling does not accommodate, and which is currently only supported through a
separately-priced "Dedicated Service."
**Trigger:** A priority project needs faster turnaround than the standard step-by-step process
allows; a Change Notification needs the same downstream steps re-run in full even when only a
small change is involved.
**Impact:** Working strictly step-by-step exposes the company (no purchase order in hand yet),
so priority projects require a paid Dedicated Service costing double to quadruple the standard
cost to informally allow parallel work. For change notifications, the participant wants a
shortened, "Fast-Track Change History" version of the same steps rather than repeating the full
project strand.
**Workaround:** Using the paid Dedicated Service for priority projects; no workaround described
for the change-notification case beyond repeating the full step sequence.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes this as a
structural, recurring constraint of the current process (not a one-off event), with a
named paid workaround (Dedicated Service) as evidence of its systemic nature.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Ich würde warten bis zu dem Punkt ... ich fange nicht an zu arbeiten, wenn ich keine vollständigen Antragsunterlagen vorliegen habe. Damit machen wir uns angreifbar, wir haben keine PO zu dem Zeitpunkt vorliegen. ... Für Prio-Projekte ist es aber tatsächlich so ... darf ich eben nicht Step by Step, sondern versuche die Schritte irgendwie parallel schon zu überarbeiten, soweit es möglich ist. Wir bieten hier auch einen Dedicated Service an, der dann das Doppelte an Kosten oder das Vierfache an Kosten ... mit sich bringt." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "I wait until that point ... I don't start working if I don't have the complete application documents. That makes us vulnerable, we don't have a purchase order at that point. ... For priority projects it's actually the case ... that I'm not allowed to go step by step, so I try to work on the steps somewhat in parallel where possible. We also offer a Dedicated Service here, which then comes with double or quadruple the cost, depending." - [P08]

> "Auch da sollte es eventuell eine Möglichkeit geben, dass man vielleicht nicht denselben Projektstrang nutzen muss, sondern quasi dieselben Schritte durchläuft, aber eben nicht in voll, sondern in irgendeiner abgekürzten Version, die wirklich nur diese Änderungen betrifft. ... eine Art von ... Fast-Track Change History." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "There too, there should possibly be a way that you don't have to use the same project strand, but rather go through the same steps, just not in full, but in some abbreviated version that only concerns these changes. ... a kind of ... Fast-Track Change History." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A digital process representation that allows steps to be worked in parallel with built-in
  flexibility for priority projects, instead of requiring strict step 1-before-step 2
  sequencing (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A "Fast-Track Change History" mode that runs a change notification through an abbreviated
  version of the same steps, scoped only to what changed, instead of the full project strand
  (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other staff handling priority/expedited projects also need to work
process steps in parallel rather than strictly sequentially, and would a digital tool need to
support that flexibility?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Rules for which certification body fee applies to a given service scenario are unclear even to staff responsible for them

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** It is unclear, even to staff responsible for applying it, which fee type (a
"Multiplied Body Review Fee" or a "Certification Review Fee") applies to which scenario,
especially for Change Notifications, Supplier Audits, or Special Audits. Decisions are made ad
hoc, without documented, clear rules.
**Trigger:** A service scenario (e.g. a Change Notification or Supplier Audit) requires a fee
to be assigned.
**Impact:** Colleagues responsible for applying the fee often do not know themselves which fee
type is correct and decide ad hoc. No customer complaints have been reported specifically
about fee type so far, though customers do sometimes question the number of hours billed.
**Workaround:** Deciding ad hoc, without a documented, agreed rule set.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant describes this
directly and unprompted, including that colleagues responsible for the decision are themselves
unsure.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 3
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P03

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Also brauche ich eine Multiplied Body Review Fee, brauche ich eine Certification Review Fee oder in welchen Fällen ... muss da was berechnet werden ... dann merke ich einfach auch oft, das wissen beide einfach selber nicht und dann entscheiden sie einfach irgendwas." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "Do I need a Multiplied Body Review Fee, do I need a Certification Review Fee, or in which cases ... does something need to be calculated ... I often notice that neither of them actually knows themselves, and then they just decide something." - [P03]

> "Ich vermute, irgendjemand hat sich ja das mal ausgedacht mit dieser Fee ... aber es ist wirklich nicht so, dass die Regeln klar sind." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "I assume someone came up with this fee at some point ... but it's really not the case that the rules are clear." - [P03]

> "Aber tatsächlich haben die sich noch nie auf diese Fees gestürzt. ... Wo sie dann irgendwie nachhaken, ist dann wie viele, also ist das gerechtfertigt, dass so und so viele Stunden dafür veranschlagt sind." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "But they've actually never pounced on these fees. ... Where they do sometimes push back is on how many hours are being budgeted for it." - [P03]

[None currently logged.]

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools

**Update (2026-08-13):** P07 directly confirms the same mechanism from a Project Coordinator
(commercial/backoffice) segment: the one-directional interface between CBW (a
certificate/registration system) and Appendix ABC/PSE means a manually entered value (e.g.
under "MHS-Details") can diverge from the same value elsewhere once one side changes, with no
automatic reconciliation. Per [[Definitions]] "Theme threshold," this note is promoted to
theme
[[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
with Confidence Basis Single-interview strong evidence → Multi-interview (2 of 7 interviews
processed so far; Confidence remains Medium since repetition is below the typical 3+ needed
for High). With 2 interviews and Severity Medium, neither condition in [[Definitions]]
"Severity/Confidence flag" applies, so `validation_status` and `validation_question` are
removed from the frontmatter. P07 also extends the candidate solution ideas with a blue-sky
vision of a single tool (built around PSE) that opens CBW, SAP, the sampling plan, and the
assessment plan without switching systems.

**Update (2026-08-14):** P08 adds a third confirming interview, from a Client Manager & Lead
Auditor segment: an Application Identification code must be entered character-for-character
identically across all application documents, with high error potential from manual entry;
a Change Notification's customer-supplied Justification is copy-pasted a second time into an
internal Decision of Significant Change document; and on long-running projects, references to
customer documents become outdated after about three months as the customer's data changes,
requiring extensive manual rework (an estimated 50% reduction in this extra effort if
references were maintained automatically). Per [[Definitions]] "Sample-relative check," 3 of 8
interviews processed so far (37.5%) directly confirm this mechanism, and repetition has
reached the typical 3+ level, so Confidence is raised from Medium to High. Priority Tier
recalculated from P2 to P1 (Severity Medium x Confidence High) in `03_pains/_register.md`.

**Theme:** [[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
**Description:** The same core, largely static certification data (e.g. requested
certification, sites, codes) must be manually copy-pasted into several disconnected internal
tools and documents — a Word file, an Excel file, a separate assessment-planning tool, and a
separate scheduling tool — with colleagues sometimes separately requesting the same
information again by e-mail. No single tool holds all the information for everyone to draw
from. P07 confirms the same mechanism from a different pair of systems: the interface between
CBW and Appendix ABC/PSE is one-directional, so a value entered manually on one side can
diverge from the same value elsewhere without warning. P08 confirms the same mechanism at the
application-document level: an Application Identification code must match
character-for-character across all documents in an application, and a customer's Change
Notification justification must be manually copy-pasted into a separate internal document.
This is distinct from the existing
theme
[[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]], which
concerns not knowing which stage/whose turn a project is at, rather than duplicated manual data
entry of the same underlying values.
**Trigger:** A Customer Specialist builds the assessment plan and schedule for a customer after
intake, and colleagues separately request the same customer data for other purposes (P06); a
Project Coordinator enters or checks master data (e.g. MHS details) that also exists in CBW and
Appendix ABC (P07); a customer submits an application or a Change Notification, requiring the
same identifying code or justification to be manually re-entered across multiple documents
(P08).
**Impact:** P06 explicitly describes this redundant re-entry as "a source of error," since the
same values are typed into multiple fields across multiple systems with no single point of
truth. P07 describes the risk concretely: a value can be "wrong here but right somewhere
else" once one side changes and the other is not updated. P08 reports high error potential on
both the customer and internal sides due to manual, character-exact entry requirements, and
reports that accumulated customer-side changes on long-running projects render prior
references outdated, adding significant rework.
**Workaround:** None described beyond manually copy-pasting between tools (P06), manually
checking both systems (P07), or manually re-entering and periodically refreshing references
(P08).
**Confidence Basis:** Not required at Confidence High (Confidence Basis only applies to
Medium). For traceability: 3 of 8 interviews processed so far (P06, P07, P08) directly and
consistently evidence the same mechanism, satisfying both the repetition and sample-relative
checks in [[Definitions]].

**Severity/Confidence flag:** Not applicable. Severity Medium with Confidence High does not
meet either condition in [[Definitions]] "Severity/Confidence flag"; no `validation_status` is
set.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 7
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P06, P07, P08

**Representative Quotes:**
> "In general, we are making ... there is a lot of noise ... we have to put a lot of data entries because ... data are always the same and they are very basic data. But we are copy and paste those data in a Word file, in an Excel file, in another tool that is made for planning the assessments, and in another tool that is made for the scheduling. ... we receive a request from administration or from some other colleagues asking exactly the same information ... there is not a real tool where all the information are inside and where everyone can really take the information from there." - [P06]

> "I always gave this feedback starting many years ago when we were in Italy creating a new platform. ... we should start with having a database with the information inside once ... and then from that obtaining the assessment plan ... and then have a tool that creates a scheduling. ... right now those informations are nowhere to me ... I have to copy and paste them inside the scheduler ... and then inside the assessment plan cloud." - [P06]

> "My focus is more on not having too many tools or like having one real database where information are there once. Because this is a source of error because you are including information in many other fields and it's super common to have that." - [P06]

> "Das ist ja eine doppelte Datenbank, die wir haben." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "That is a duplicate database that we have." - [P07]

> "Die Schnittstelle ist ja hier auch nur einseitig. ... Ich bin hier drin, gehe unter MHS-Details rein. Das habe ich manuell eingetragen. Wenn das nicht mehr stimmt, dann stimmt's nicht mehr. Dann ist es falsch hier, aber richtig woanders." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "The interface here is also only one-directional. ... I'm in here, I go into the MHS details. I entered that manually. If that's no longer accurate, then it's simply no longer accurate. Then it's wrong here but right somewhere else." - [P07]

> "Ihr kennt wahrscheinlich die Geschichte, dass wir eine Application Identification oder irgendein sonstiges Kürzel brauchen das wirklich über alle Dokumente identifiziert. ... Das liegt einfach an den händischen Einträgen. Und es muss zeichengenau, glaube ich, gehen." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "You probably know the story that we need an Application Identification, or some other short code, that really identifies [the case] across all documents. ... That's simply because of the manual entries. And it has to match character-for-character, I believe." - [P08]

> "Wenn ich einmal über diesen Dreimonatszeitraum drüber bin, dann hat sich beim Kunden so viel an der Supplyliste und den Dokumenten ... geändert, dass alle meine Referenzen outdated sind." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Once I'm past this three-month period, so much has changed on the customer's side regarding the supply list and the documents ... that all my references are outdated." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A single database holding core certification data once, from which the assessment plan and
  the audit/assessment schedule are both automatically generated, eliminating repeated manual
  re-entry (P06), converging with the broader Appendix ABC digitization vision logged under
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]].
  Explicitly unvalidated.
- A bidirectional interface between CBW and Appendix ABC/PSE so that a mirrored value in one
  system is automatically reflected in the other, instead of the current one-directional,
  manually-maintained link (P07). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A blue-sky single tool (built around PSE) that opens CBW, SAP, the sampling plan, and the
  assessment plan in place, without requiring staff to switch to another system (P07,
  converging with P06's "one real database"/ERP framing). Explicitly unvalidated.
- Automatically linking application documents that share the same Application Identification
  code, and automatically refreshing references on long-running projects as customer-side data
  changes, rather than requiring staff to re-enter the identifier on every document or
  manually track staleness (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: UCI customer portal is limited to one-way file exchange

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** UCI, an internal customer/communication portal, is currently used only as a
file upload/download tool. It has no direct-messaging capability between staff and customers;
information is instead simply placed in the tool for whoever accesses it. Separately, documents
uploaded by mistake cannot be deleted, only hidden, so incorrect files remain in the tool
permanently.
**Trigger:** A staff member or customer needs to exchange a message tied to a specific
document or upload, or needs to remove a document uploaded in error.
**Impact:** Neither staff nor customers can message each other directly through the tool,
limiting it to passive file exchange. Documents that were uploaded incorrectly persist
indefinitely, since only hiding (not deletion) is possible.
**Workaround:** None described for direct communication; incorrect documents are hidden rather
than removed.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant identifies two
distinct, concrete tool limitations (no direct messaging; no deletion, only hiding) as direct,
unprompted observations.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 2
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "UCI wird derzeit lediglich als Daten-Upload-Download-Tool verwendet. ... derzeit kann ich niemanden direkt anschreiben, sondern jeder kriegt diese Informationen. Kunden können mich auch nicht direkt anschreiben, sondern es ist halt einfach im Tool." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "UCI is currently only used as a data upload/download tool. ... currently I cannot message anyone directly; instead everyone just gets these pieces of information. Customers can't message me directly either — it's just simply within the tool." - [P07]

> "Momentan ist es so, ich kann fehlerhaft eingestellte Dokumente nicht mehr löschen. Die bleiben für immer in diesem Tool. Das geht nicht. ... Ich kann sie lediglich verstecken, das kann nicht sein. Also so ein Tool muss schon eine Möglichkeit haben, dass man auch was löschen kann." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "Right now it's the case that I can no longer delete documents that were uploaded by mistake. They stay in this tool forever. That's not acceptable. ... I can only hide them, and that shouldn't be the case. A tool like this needs to have the ability to actually delete something." - [P07]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Add direct messaging tied to uploaded documents/projects within UCI. Explicitly unvalidated.
- Add a genuine delete capability for incorrectly uploaded documents, rather than hide-only.
  Explicitly unvalidated.

**Validation question:** Do other staff also report that UCI (the customer portal) only
supports file upload/download without direct messaging, and that uploaded documents cannot be
deleted, only hidden?

## Reference
See [[Definitions]] for severity and confidence criteria.

notes.body:
<!-- Describe observations in plain, third-person language. Keep validation and inference separate. -->

# Pain Point: Unnecessary multi-party signature requirement delays quotation and order confirmation

**Theme:** `Standalone preliminary finding`
**Description:** Quotations currently require being signed twice, and order confirmations may
also require a signature, though the participant is not convinced either requirement is still
commercially necessary. When a required signatory is unavailable (e.g. on vacation), the
process is delayed and must be actively chased.
**Trigger:** A quotation or order confirmation reaches the point where it requires signature
before it can be issued or confirmed.
**Impact:** The participant states this "can really cause delay," particularly when a
signatory is on vacation or otherwise unavailable, requiring the Project Coordinator to
repeatedly follow up.
**Workaround:** Manually chasing signatories until the signature is obtained.
**Confidence Basis:** Single-interview strong evidence — the participant raises this as a
specific, concrete process question with a direct example of the resulting delay.

## Evidence
**Quotes Logged:** 1
<!-- Citation count for traceability, not corroboration. Many quotes from one interview_id is NOT multiple confirmations; see Definitions.md "Quote Count vs. Interview Count". -->
**Interview IDs:** P07

**Representative Quotes:**
> "Ich bin mir gar nicht so sicher, ob das wirklich im Kaufmännischen notwendig ist, dass das Angebot erstens doppelt unterschrieben wird. Ich bin mir auch nicht sicher, ob eine Order Confirmation mittlerweile unterschrieben werden muss ... Und das sind so Fragen, das kann sich wirklich verzögern, das verzögert, wenn jemand im Urlaub ist, nicht da ist, muss der ständig hinterherlaufen." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I'm not at all sure whether it's really necessary commercially for the quotation to be signed twice. notes.body:
<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff and customers need shared visibility into final certification review timeline expectations

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff and customers need a shared, realistic understanding of
the final certification review step's expected duration, including which portion of that
duration is the certification body's responsibility and which portion depends on the
customer's own response speed. P02 identifies unmet timeline expectations at this step as the
single biggest customer pain point. P06 confirms the same mechanism and adds that a new MDR
(Medical Device Regulation) Article 7 requirement now obliges certification bodies to share a
timeline with customers, even though the certification body holds only partial responsibility
for the final duration.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence Medium (direct evidence from P02 and P06).

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**
> "Ich denk, der größte Pain Point für Kunden ist, wenn die Timeline nicht eingehalten werden, weil der Kunde zuverlässig wissen muss, wann eine Bewertung fertig ist, wann er einen Reporter bekommt, wann er ein Zertifikat bekommt. ... da kommt es oft zu Rückfragen, dann verschiebt sich oder verlängert sich der Slot." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "I think the biggest pain point for customers is when the timeline is not met, because the customer needs to reliably know when an assessment will be finished, when they'll get a report, when they'll get a certificate. ... there are often follow-up questions, and then the slot shifts or extends." - [P02]

> "There is a new Article 7 in the MDR that is requesting us to share a plan with the customers ... to give them the timeline for the certification. But inside these timelines, we have only a partial responsibility. ... but then the last part depends on you." - [P06]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A shared, customer-facing timeline interface showing expected certification milestones,
  which pauses ("stops the clock") while awaiting the customer's response, so that delays
  attributable to the customer are visibly separated from delays attributable to the
  certification body (P06). Explicitly unvalidated.

notes.body:
<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff need a consolidated, reliable project status view independent of manual data-entry discipline

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need a consolidated view of where a project or
application currently stands in the certification process, comparable to a package-tracking
view. P01 has no such view today and relies on informal expert channels for a subset of
projects flagged as critical. P02 confirms the same underlying gap and adds that existing
tooling can approximate a status view, but only when task and timeline data are consistently
maintained — a condition that is not reliably met, particularly for internationally-coordinated
projects. P03 confirms the same gap from a third role and describes maintaining a personal,
manually-updated Excel list as a substitute, alongside a wish for a workflow view that shows
whose turn it currently is. P04 confirms the same gap a fourth time, specifically for
Technical Documentation (TD) assessment and Change Notification tracking, where no
company-provided tool exists at all and the Assessment Plan Cloud (APC) tool is static rather
than showing live deficiency-report status. P07 confirms the same gap a fifth time, from a
Project Coordinator (commercial/backoffice) segment: PSE version 2.0 is harder to keep an
overview with than PSE 1.0, requiring a recurring biweekly team meeting as a workaround, with
timeline and hours/booking-status information additionally split into two disconnected areas.
P08 confirms the same gap a sixth time, from a Client Manager & Lead Auditor segment: two
separate, personally-built filters are needed across two tools (BSE and PSE) to approximate an
overview, an upcoming PSE master-data reduction threatens to remove status detail currently
relied upon, and a single graphical (Gantt-style) status view directly within UCI is wished
for.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence High (direct evidence from P01, P02, P03,
P04, P07, and P08).

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**
> "Tracking von Projektstatus ist mit Sicherheit eine wichtige Sache. wenn man das hier einbauen könnte wie bei einem DHL Paket, in welchem Status wir uns befinden, wo das Paket sich gerade befindet." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Tracking the project status is certainly an important thing, if one could build this in like a DHL package, [showing] what status we are in, where the package currently is." - [P01]

> "Wenn das so gehandhabt wird [Tasks nur zum Buchen angelegt], dann habe ich eigentlich keinerlei Übersicht mehr." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "If it's handled that way [tasks only created for booking hours], then I actually have no overview at all anymore." - [P02]

> "Also, ich hätte tatsächlich eigentlich ... dass man irgendwie was hat, was diesen Workflow tatsächlich irgendwie abbildet, dass ich irgendwie sehe, was ist gerade meine Aufgabe ... bei wem liegt gerade der Ball in dem Sinne." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "What I would actually want ... is something that really depicts this workflow, so I can see what my current task is ... whose turn it is, so to speak." - [P03]

> "Surely for what regard the changes and assessment, I think there is a, there is a, let's say, void or lack in following planning. ... I have no tool proposed by to suit the tool. I need to let's say rely on my own, let's say scheduling for following the project." - [P04]

> "I think in the APC you can upload the sampling plan, but it's, let's say, not rolling, it's a static... you don't know if you have a deficiency report ongoing when you expect from the customer to, let's say, to push." - [P04]

> "Ich muss tatsächlich sagen, mit PSE 2.0 ist es echt schwierig den Überblick zu behalten." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "I really have to say, with PSE 2.0 it is genuinely difficult to keep an overview." - [P07]

> "Darüber hinaus, was schön wäre, wenn ich alles in UCI direkt hätte ... Ich hätte gern mein [Gantt]-Diagramm, wo ich mein einzelnes Projekt sehe." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "Beyond that, it would be nice if I had everything directly in UCI ... I'd like my Gantt chart, where I see my individual project." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Phase-level time traceability/monitoring that does not depend on manual timeline
  maintenance (P02). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A priority/escalation mechanism tied to a request-to-decision time metric (P01). Explicitly
  unvalidated.
- An end-to-end workflow view showing whose turn it is to act (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A single main working area combining timeline and hours/booking status, rather than two
  disconnected areas (P07). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A single graphical (Gantt-style) status view within UCI with filter functions, preserving
  current status/master-data detail rather than reducing it (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.

notes.body:
<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff need application forms that validate entries before submission to prevent inconsistent customer data

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need the standard request/application form to catch
customer entry errors before submission, rather than discovering them only after the fact. P03
describes customers frequently getting checkboxes or fields wrong, requiring staff to return
the form for correction. P08 confirms the same mechanism from the form-design side: dropdowns
do not dynamically filter out logically mutually-exclusive combinations, so inconsistent data
is frequently submitted and accepted uncaught, and customers are often unclear which
form/information is even required.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/Customers frequently fill in standard request forms incorrectly, requiring staff to return them for correction]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence Medium (direct evidence from P03 and P08).

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**
> "Ja, also gerade bei den Formblättern, stellen die sich manchmal schlauer und mal dümmer an, da irgendwie die Häkchen richtig zu machen oder das auszufüllen ... das gibt es schon öfter mal dass ich das wieder zurückschicke." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "Yes, especially with the forms, they sometimes manage better and sometimes worse to get the checkboxes right or fill it in correctly ... it happens fairly often that I send it back." - [P03]

> "Das heißt entweder bestimmte Dropdowns, die dann verschwinden, wenn bestimmte Auswahlmöglichkeiten oben das nicht unterstützen, weil wir haben sehr oft die Inkonsistenz von Daten in diesen Formblättern. ... Aber es gibt viele Fälle, die sich einfach logisch ausschließen, die aber nach wie vor oft eingereicht werden können und nicht zu Fehlern kommen." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "So either certain dropdowns disappear when certain selections above don't support them, because we very often have data inconsistency in these forms. ... But there are many cases that are simply logically mutually exclusive, that can nevertheless still often be submitted and are not caught." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A guided intake flow with dynamic follow-up questions that routes the customer to the
  correct form and pre-fills known data (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- Dynamic dropdowns that filter out logically mutually-exclusive combinations at entry time,
  while preserving free-text/comment fields (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.
