notes.body:
<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff need core certification data held once in a shared system instead of re-entered across disconnected tools

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need the same core, largely static certification data
(e.g. requested certification, sites, codes, customer/facility details) to exist once in a
shared system, rather than being manually copy-pasted or re-entered across several
disconnected tools and documents. P06 describes copy-pasting the same basic data into a Word
file, an Excel file, an assessment-planning tool, and a scheduling tool, calling the resulting
duplication "a source of error." P07 confirms the same mechanism from a different pair of
systems: the interface between CBW (a certificate/registration system) and Appendix ABC/PSE
(the internal project/service tool) is one-directional, so a manually entered value can
diverge from the same value elsewhere without warning. P08 confirms the same mechanism a third
time, at the application-document level: an Application Identification code must match
character-for-character across all documents in an application, and a customer's Change
Notification justification must be manually copy-pasted into a separate internal document,
with accumulated customer-side changes making prior references outdated on long-running
projects.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence High (direct evidence from P06, P07, and
P08).

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**

> "My focus is more on not having too many tools or like having one real database where information are there once. Because this is a source of error because you are including information in many other fields and it's super common to have that." - [P06]

> "Die Schnittstelle ist ja hier auch nur einseitig. ... Ich bin hier drin, gehe unter MHS-Details rein. Das habe ich manuell eingetragen. Wenn das nicht mehr stimmt, dann stimmt's nicht mehr. Dann ist es falsch hier, aber richtig woanders." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "The interface here is also only one-directional. ... I'm in here, I go into the MHS details. I entered that manually. If that's no longer accurate, then it's simply no longer accurate. Then it's wrong here but right somewhere else." - [P07]

> "Ihr kennt wahrscheinlich die Geschichte, dass wir eine Application Identification oder irgendein sonstiges Kürzel brauchen das wirklich über alle Dokumente identifiziert. ... Das liegt einfach an den händischen Einträgen. Und es muss zeichengenau, glaube ich, gehen." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "You probably know the story that we need an Application Identification, or some other short code, that really identifies [the case] across all documents. ... That's simply because of the manual entries. And it has to match character-for-character, I believe." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)

<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff need guided, example-based support so customers self-assign correct regulatory codes

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need a way to reduce the volume of incorrect regulatory
codes that customers propose, so that fewer corrections and follow-up questions are required
before assessor qualification and assessment planning can proceed. All three interviews
describe customers guessing at code relevance and staff having to catch and correct the
result; P02 and P05 also independently raise example- or guidance-based support, and P05 adds
a first-pass, AI-derived code suggestion with client verification, as ways to help customers
assign codes more accurately at the point of submission.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence High (direct evidence from P01, P02, and
P05; see the theme note for the sample-relative confidence check).

**Update (2026-08-12):** P05 adds a third confirming interview and a new quote; evidence
threshold updated from Confirmed theme (Medium) to Confirmed theme, Confidence High.

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**
> "Bei den Codes weiß der Kunde immer, was das Richtige ist oder?" / "Natürlich nicht. Kann er nicht oder verbockt er manchmal einfach? Beides." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "With the codes, does the customer always know what's correct?" / "Of course not. Can't he, or does he sometimes just get it wrong? Both." - [P01]

> "Beispiele sind generell immer gut. ... Ich denke, wenn man da den Kunden noch weiter unterstützen kann in die Richtung ... vielleicht mit so einem, wie nennt man das, Info oder Beispiele anzeigt, das könnte schon helfen." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Examples are generally always good. ... I think if customers could be supported further in that direction ... maybe by showing some kind of info or examples, that could already help." - [P02]

> "A lot of companies will choose the EAC 14 code for plastics because of this, even because their cartridge is made of plastic. ... those codes are only for the specific manufacturing technologies that they use and most companies don't mold their own plastic cassette housings. They buy those from a supplier. ... They're not actually manufacturing the plastic." - [P05]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- In-workflow examples or guidance information shown at the point where a customer selects a
  regulatory code (P02); P05 converges on the same direction, describing instructions
  currently living on a separate tab that customers never see. Explicitly unvalidated.
- An AI-assisted code-suggestion tool (P01); P05 extends this with a specific mechanism —
  deriving a first-pass code suggestion from the client's entered intended-purpose statement,
  shown as likely/possible tiers, with the client verifying the final selection, and cautions
  that certification staff should not assign codes unilaterally since the customer, not staff,
  is the expert on their own product. Explicitly unvalidated.

<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff need project communication consolidated into a single, traceable channel

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need project-related communication consolidated so it can
be reconstructed without manually checking multiple separate channels. P03 must manually note
which channel (email or UCI) was used for a given update to avoid losing track. P08 confirms
the same mechanism across three channels (email, Teams, and UCI/PSE), describing reassembly of
scattered communication after time away as very difficult, and separately reports that an
internal escalation process spanning multiple communication paths is itself
communication-intensive.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/Communication scattered across multiple parallel channels makes project history hard to reconstruct]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence Medium (direct evidence from P03 and P08).

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**
> "Meistens schreibe ich mir da irgendwie noch dazu, irgendwie via Mail oder via UCI, weil das ist jetzt auch immer, dann denkt man, hey, ich bin gar keine Mail dazu. ... diese zwei Kanäle sind auch manchmal eher ein Hindernis, dass man das irgendwie nachverfolgen kann." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "Usually I also note down whether it was via email or via UCI, because otherwise you think, hey, I don't have an email about that. ... these two channels are also sometimes more of an obstacle to being able to track it." - [P03]

> "Es gibt E-Mail-Kommunikationspfad, es gibt einen Teams-Kommunikationspfad, es gibt gegebenenfalls noch zusätzlichen Pfad über UCI beziehungsweise PSE[M] und Kunden. Diese Informationen nach zwei Wochen Urlaub wieder zusammenzusuchen, katastrophal." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "There's an email communication path, there's a Teams communication path, there is possibly an additional path via UCI or PSE and customers. Reassembling this information after two weeks of vacation — catastrophic." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- A single tool with an in-tool chat/communication feature tied to the project object, so
  history does not need to be reassembled from separate channels (P08). Explicitly
  unvalidated.
- A single-click forwarding/escalation action within the tool, replacing ad hoc phone calls
  and a multi-channel escalation process (P08). Explicitly unvalidated.

notes.body:
<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Certification staff need reliable, complete Appendix ABC data before assessment can proceed efficiently

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need the Appendix ABC master-data document to be
complete, current, and free of regulatorily invalid entries before assessment can proceed
efficiently. P01 describes it as authoritative despite being the most frequently changed,
most error-prone document. P03 confirms the same mechanism from a different role and adds
that data-quality cross-checking is her single biggest time cost before assessment, with
errors sometimes discovered only mid-assessment and corrected only after a roughly five-week
customer round-trip. P04 confirms the same mechanism a third time: review burden scales
sharply with the number of Basic UDIs/SKUs on a customer's Appendix ABC, and every new version
requires a full manual re-verification because of the risk of customer data loss, typing
errors, or accidental overwriting. P05 confirms the same mechanism a fourth time from a
new-client onboarding role: no client has ever filled out Appendix ABC correctly on the first
attempt, and getting the document correct upfront is the single largest source of early
back-and-forth with the customer. P06 confirms the same mechanism a fifth time from a Customer
Specialist/Lead Auditor/TD Assessor role: the document is never complete at the start of a
customer relationship, with the specific missing-data focus having shifted over time from
Appendix A (EMDN codes) to Appendix C (supplier information). P08 confirms the same mechanism
a sixth time from a Client Manager & Lead Auditor role: the same data-inconsistency and
cross-document traceability issues persist, informally-used consistency-check macros remain
necessary in the absence of a digital solution since manual checking is infeasible for large
customers' row volumes, and Appendix ABC-related issues are independently named as customers'
single biggest complaint.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence High (direct evidence from P01, P03, P04,
P05, P06, and P08).

**Update (2026-08-12):** P05 adds a fourth confirming interview and a new quote; three new
candidate ideas added (AI-powered document extraction, an online jointly-editable Appendix
ABC, and an override-vs-flag validation preference).

**Update (2026-08-13):** P06 adds a fifth confirming interview and a new quote; two new
candidate ideas added (a jointly-editable device-list database with auto-suggested field
values, and a change-impact auto-detection mechanism).

**Update (2026-08-13, later):** P07 adds a converging candidate idea only (centrally managed
master data, code-driven auto-suggestion, in-context glossary/classification guidance, and
easier certificate editing); P07 does not directly confirm the underlying theme mechanism, so
the evidence threshold and Confidence remain based on P01, P03, P04, P05, P06 (High).

**Update (2026-08-14):** P08 adds a sixth confirming interview and a new quote; a candidate
idea is added for built-in, automated consistency checks/macros as a digital-solution feature.

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**
> "Derzeit ist der Appendix A. B. C. die vollendete Wahrheit, die maßgeblich sein muss und deckungsgleich mit dem Assessment Plant Loud. Und auch das Dokument, das am häufigsten verändert wird, logischerweise." - [P01]
>
> Translation: "Currently the Appendix ABC is the complete truth that has to be authoritative and consistent with the assessment plan. It is also, logically, the document that gets changed most often." - [P01]

> "Also einerseits dann mit den Daten, die sie dann haben ... da verliere ich glaube ich am meisten Zeit ... es gibt hier in einer Basic UDI verschiedene intended users. Dürfen sie eigentlich gar nicht haben. ... dann müssen die sich erstmal fünf Wochen absprechen, dass sie irgendwie dann wieder eine neue Version schicken." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "On one hand with the data they have ... I think that's where I lose the most time ... there are different intended users on one Basic UDI here. They aren't actually allowed to have that. ... then they first have to coordinate among themselves for five weeks before sending a new version." - [P03]

> "for the customer that I have more than 100 [Basic UDI/SKUs], it's critical because I have the, let's say, I'm afraid that there could be losing of data, wrong typing, from the customer ... So I always, when I receive each version, let's say, read from the ... top to the bottom." - [P04]

> "I've never had a client fill it out correctly in one go. There's always something wrong with it that I have to go back to them and ask for a correction or a clarification on." - [P05]

> "at the very beginning with the company, there are a lot of missing information. ... when they have to fulfill the Appendix ABC for the first time, they fear the white paper, like they don't know how to fulfill it. They don't have any example and they really are frustrated to start this job." - [P06]

> "Auch da, ich mein, wir haben letztlich dieselben Themen, das sind Dateninkonsistenzen, Traceability über mehrere Dokumente, die verlinkt sein sollten." - [P08]
>
> Translation: "There too, I mean, we ultimately have the same issues: data inconsistencies, traceability across several documents that should be linked." - [P08]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)
<!-- Optional, non-binding ideas only. These are NOT recommendations. A validated recommendation lives inside its anchor insight, never here. -->
- Digitizing Appendix ABC as structured data with automatic cross-checks and regulatory
  validation at entry time, instead of Excel (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A live or bulk-upload interface between customer systems (e.g. SAP) and Appendix ABC to
  reduce manual re-entry for large customers (P03). Explicitly unvalidated.
- An online Appendix ABC that both staff and the client can jointly see and manipulate,
  replacing siloed Excel copies (P03, P04, P05 — a third interview converging on this
  direction). Explicitly unvalidated.
- An AI-powered capability that extracts data from client-uploaded documents (Instructions for
  Use, quality manual, approved supplier list) to auto-populate Appendix ABC fields, with a
  manual fallback for clients who lack some documents (P05). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A validation layer with both an override option (staff correct directly) and a
  flag-to-customer option, with formal customer approval required only at defined phase gates
  rather than on every edit (P05). Explicitly unvalidated.
- A single, jointly-editable device-list database (shared by staff and the customer) that
  auto-suggests field values for similar device types and automatically generates the
  assessment plan and audit schedule (P06, a fourth interview converging on the joint-editing
  direction, with auto-suggestion and auto-generated planning as new refinements). Explicitly
  unvalidated.
- A change-tracking mechanism that freezes prior states and automatically distinguishes edits
  with no downstream planning impact from edits that require replanning, surfacing only the
  latter for staff attention (P06). Explicitly unvalidated.
- Centrally managed master data with code-driven auto-suggestion of applicable rules,
  procedure packs, and facilities, in-context classification/glossary guidance at the point of
  code selection, and easier certificate row/text editing (P07, converging with the same
  live-document/digitization direction as P03, P04, P05, and P06). Explicitly unvalidated.
- Automated consistency checks/macros searching for expected wordings or patterns, built into
  the digital solution rather than kept as an informal personal workaround (P08). Explicitly
  unvalidated.

<!-- Use neutral third-person prose. Mark latent needs as inferences, not direct observations. -->

# Need: Project-related communication needs to be automatically linked to its project record

**Category:** Functional
**Description:** Certification staff need project-related communication (e-mail, chat, and
incoming documents) to be automatically linked to its project record, instead of relying on
staff to manually insert a project/reference number, or on a project record already existing
at the time communication arrives. P02 must manually include a reference (e.g. an SAP or PSE
project number) in every outgoing message to identify which project it concerns. P07 confirms
the same missing link from the receiving side: incoming e-mails or documents that arrive
before a project exists in PSE, or without her copied, "float around" and can become
effectively unassignable given project volume.
**Related Theme:** [[../02_themes/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
**Evidence threshold:** Confirmed theme, Confidence Medium (direct evidence from P02 and P07).

## Evidence
**Representative Quotes:**

> "Momentan muss ich es, also wenn ich eine E-Mail schreibe, Team [Teams] muss man sich immer die Projektnummer, irgendeine Referenz S.A.P. Nummer oder P.S.E. Projektnummer reinschreiben, dass ich 'ne Referenz irgendeinen Anhaltspunkt habe, welches Projekt geht es quasi." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Currently I have to — so when I write an email, [or] Teams, you always have to write in the project number, some reference SAP number or PSE project number, so that I have a reference, some point of reference, [to know] which project it concerns." - [P02]

> "Ist es nicht der Fall, existiert dieses Projekt nicht im PSE, dann dümpeln die Dokumente irgendwo rum oder die E-Mails und können dann nicht mehr entsprechend zugeordnet werden." - [P07]
>
> Translation: "If that is not the case, if this project does not exist in PSE, then the documents or the e-mails float around somewhere and can no longer be properly assigned." - [P07]

## Candidate Solution Ideas (unvalidated)

# Insights Status

Track, per confirmed theme, whether evidence is sufficient to justify an insight. Log
`Theme X: not yet enough connected evidence` for themes that exist but don't yet warrant an
insight. See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] Step 8/F.

## After P01 (first processed interview)

`02_themes` contains no confirmed themes yet (creating a theme requires direct evidence from
at least two distinct interviews; see [[Definitions]] "Theme threshold"). All findings from P01
are standalone preliminary pain points instead (see [[../03_pains/_register|Pain Point
Register]]). No insight is created at this stage, since an insight requires multiple supporting
themes and none exist yet.

## After P02 (second processed interview)

Three themes now exist, each confirmed by direct evidence from P01 and P02:
[[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]],
[[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]], and
[[../02_themes/EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition]]
(the last split out of a P01 pain point that originally bundled it with an unrelated Appendix
ABC finding; see [[../01_interviews/P02]] "Theme Match").

One insight has been created:
[[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
connecting the code-misassignment theme and the EUDAMED theme, since both describe the same
underlying mechanism (externally-sourced data requiring manual staff verification) across two
different data types. It carries one recommendation, logged in
[[_recommendations-register]].

`No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` is not yet connected to
an insight: it does not currently share a clear common mechanism with either of the other two
themes (it concerns internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than externally-sourced data
requiring verification), and only one theme is not enough to justify an insight on its own.
This is recorded as `Theme: No consolidated project status view exists for certification
staff — not yet enough connected evidence` pending a theme that shares its mechanism.

## After P03 (third processed interview)

P03 directly confirms two existing themes and promotes one existing standalone pain point to a
new theme:
- `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` gains a third
  confirming interview; Confidence raised Medium → High per the sample-relative check in
  [[Definitions]]. It still concerns internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than
  externally-sourced data requiring verification, so it remains `not yet enough connected
  evidence` for an insight on its own.
- The P01 standalone pain point [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (P01, P03; Confidence Medium). This theme shares the same underlying mechanism as the
  existing insight — externally-sourced (customer-maintained) data being relied upon without
  adequate verification — for a third data type (Appendix ABC master data, alongside
  regulatory codes and EUDAMED records). It has therefore been added as a third supporting
  theme to
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]].
  Insight confidence remains Medium (weakest-link rule; all three supporting themes are
  Medium). The existing recommendation was extended to include Appendix ABC entry-time
  validation; no new recommendation/insight was created.
- P03 also surfaces contradicting evidence on `Customers propose regulatory codes by best
  guess, requiring correction by certification staff` (her customers reportedly already
  understand codes) and related-but-distinct evidence on the P02 communication pain point
  (dual-channel tracking friction); neither changes the theme's confidence or triggers a new
  theme, per [[../01_interviews/P03]] "Theme Match".

## After P04 (fourth processed interview)

P04 directly confirms two existing themes; no new theme or insight was created:
- `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` gains a fourth
  confirming interview (TD assessment/Change Notification tracking has no company tool at all;
  the Assessment Plan Cloud tool is static). Confidence remains High (4 of 4 interviews, 100%).
  It still concerns internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than externally-sourced data
  requiring verification, so it remains `not yet enough connected evidence` for an insight on
  its own.
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a third confirming interview (Appendix ABC review burden scales sharply with SKU/Basic
  UDI count; every new version requires full manual re-verification). Per the sample-relative
  check in [[Definitions]], Confidence is raised from Medium to High (3 of 4 interviews, 75%).
  Since this theme supports
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
  the insight's own confidence was reassessed: per the weakest-link rule, it cannot exceed the
  weakest supporting theme. The other two supporting themes (regulatory code assignment;
  EUDAMED data completeness) remain Confidence Medium and were not reassessed this turn, so the
  insight's confidence stays Medium overall.
- Three new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P04 evidence (deficiency
  report reminders; auditor/assessor conflict-of-interest verification; archival/handover
  incompleteness); none share a mechanism with an existing theme, so none were connected to an
  insight at this stage.
- Two P04 topics (`#code/customer-service-awareness-gap`,
  `#code/objectivity-perception-external`) were evaluated and found out of scope for the MACE
  Application workflow-digitization focus; recorded as background only in
  [[../01_interviews/P04]], not promoted to any artifact.

## After P05 (fifth processed interview)

P05 directly confirms two existing themes; no new theme was created, and the existing insight
was enriched but its overall confidence did not change:
- [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
  gains a third confirming interview (customers self-assigning EAC codes by superficial
  material match rather than manufacturing-technology scope). Per the sample-relative check in
  [[Definitions]] (3 of 5 interviews, 60%), Confidence is raised from Medium to High.
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a fourth confirming interview (no client has ever filled out Appendix ABC correctly on
  the first attempt). Sample-relative check: 4 of 5 interviews (80%); Confidence remains High.
- Since both themes support
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
  the insight's own confidence was reassessed: per the weakest-link rule, it cannot exceed the
  weakest supporting theme. The EUDAMED supporting theme remains Confidence Medium and was not
  reassessed this turn, so the insight's confidence stays Medium overall despite two of its
  three supporting themes now being High.
- Four new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P05 evidence (critical-supplier
  definition mismatch; scope-statement formatting difficulty; independently-edited Appendix
  ABC copies diverging between auditor and reviewer; Mace Audit's broken findings-generation
  defect). None share a mechanism with an existing insight-supporting theme, so none were
  connected to an insight at this stage.
- P05's segment (new-client onboarding, SPOC/SPOS role) is background-only for insight
  purposes; logged in [[../07_personas/Proto-Segments]] as a first row in a new, not-yet-
  clustered segment (below the 3-interview persona threshold).
- Several P05 topics (onboarding role-scope context, regional/cert-body workflow variation,
  UCI rollout awareness gap, lack of user consultation before Mace Audit's mandatory rollout)
  were evaluated and found out of scope for a dedicated artifact; recorded as background only
  in [[../01_interviews/P05]].

## After P06 (sixth processed interview)

P06 directly confirms one existing theme, confirms and promotes one standalone pain point to a
new theme, and creates four new standalone pain points; no new insight was created:
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a fifth confirming interview (Appendix ABC never complete at the start of a customer
  relationship; missing-data focus has shifted over time from Appendix A to Appendix C).
  Sample-relative check: 5 of 6 interviews (83%); Confidence remains High. Since this theme
  supports
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
  the insight was re-checked per the weakest-link rule: the EUDAMED supporting theme remains
  Confidence Medium and was not reassessed this turn, so the insight's confidence stays Medium
  overall.
- The P02 standalone pain point
  [[../03_pains/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]
  is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]
  (P02, P06; Confidence Medium). This theme concerns final-review timeline unpredictability and
  shared responsibility for delays, not externally-sourced data requiring verification. It does
  not currently share a clear common mechanism with any existing insight-supporting theme, and
  only one theme is not enough to justify an insight on its own. This is recorded as `Theme:
  Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step — not
  yet enough connected evidence` pending a second theme that shares its mechanism.
- Four new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P06 evidence
  (Appendix-ABC signal-extraction difficulty; redundant manual data re-entry across
  disconnected tools; customer-facing Appendix ABC version conflicts from unshared local
  copies; internal document templates changing without staff or customer guidance). None share
  a mechanism with an existing insight-supporting theme, so none were connected to an insight
  at this stage.
- P06's segment (Customer Specialist / Lead Auditor / TD Assessor, Italy) is the third
  interview clustering with the existing Auditor/Customer Specialist proto-segment (P03, P04);
  see [[../07_personas/Proto-Segments]] and the new persona note created this turn.
- P06's secondary competency-coordination role (SPS, risk management) and the regional
  workflow variation (no customer portal in Italy) were evaluated and found out of scope for a
  dedicated artifact; recorded as background only in [[../01_interviews/P06]].

## After P07 (seventh processed interview)

P07 directly confirms one existing theme, promotes two standalone pain points to new themes,
and creates five new standalone pain points; no new insight was created:
- `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` gains a fifth
  confirming interview (PSE 2.0 harder to keep an overview with than PSE 1.0, requiring a
  recurring biweekly team meeting; timeline and hours/booking status split into two
  disconnected areas). Sample-relative check: 5 of 7 interviews (71%); Confidence remains High.
  It still concerns internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than externally-sourced data
  requiring verification, so it remains `not yet enough connected evidence` for an insight on
  its own.
- The P06 standalone pain point
  [[../03_pains/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
  is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
  (P06, P07; Confidence Medium). This theme concerns duplicated manual data entry across
  disconnected tools, not externally-sourced data requiring verification. It does not
  currently share a clear common mechanism with any existing insight-supporting theme, and
  only one theme is not enough to justify an insight on its own. This is recorded as `Theme:
  The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected
  tools — not yet enough connected evidence` pending a second theme that shares its mechanism.
- The P02 standalone pain point
  [[../03_pains/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
  is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
  (P02, P07; Confidence Medium). This theme concerns communication not being anchored to a
  project record. It was explicitly compared against the newly promoted redundant-re-entry
  theme above: the two are adjacent fragmentation mechanisms (duplicated core data vs.
  unanchored communication) but are distinct — one concerns data values, the other concerns
  message/document routing — so they were not combined into a single insight. Neither theme
  currently shares a clear common mechanism with any other existing theme, so both are
  recorded as `not yet enough connected evidence` pending a second theme that shares either
  specific mechanism.
- Five new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P07 evidence (Appendix ABC
  row-structure redundancy and cross-tab decoding; informal customer-account assignment;
  unnecessary multi-party signature requirement; assessor ready-status/timeline
  non-compliance; UCI customer-portal one-way file exchange). None share a mechanism with an
  existing insight-supporting theme, so none were connected to an insight at this stage.
- P07's converging candidate idea (centrally managed master data, code-driven auto-suggestion,
  in-context glossary/classification guidance, easier certificate editing) was logged as a
  sixth interview extending the existing digitization-vision candidate idea under
  [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  and its linked need; it does not confirm that theme's core mechanism directly, so it was not
  counted toward that theme's interview count or confidence.
- P07's segment (Project Coordinator, commercial/backoffice, non-customer-call-facing) is
  background-only for insight purposes; logged in [[../07_personas/Proto-Segments]] as the
  first row in a new, not-yet-clustered segment (below the 3-interview persona threshold).
- P07's self-built Audit Pricing Tool (single-interview positive pattern, below the
  two-interview threshold), UK-cluster access exception, and stated non-involvement with Mace
  Audit were evaluated and found out of scope for a dedicated artifact; recorded as background
  only in [[../01_interviews/P07]].

## After P08 (eighth processed interview)

P08 directly confirms three existing themes, promotes two standalone pain points (one to an
existing new theme, one directly into a new theme with two interviews), and creates seven new
standalone pain points; no new insight was created:
- `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` gains a sixth
  confirming interview (two separately-built filters across BSE and PSE; concern over an
  upcoming PSE master-data reduction; a wish for a single graphical UCI status view).
  Sample-relative check: 6 of 8 interviews (75%); Confidence remains High. It still concerns
  internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than externally-sourced data requiring
  verification, so it remains `not yet enough connected evidence` for an insight on its own.
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a sixth confirming interview (data inconsistency and cross-document traceability
  issues persist; informal consistency-check macros remain necessary pending digitization).
  Sample-relative check: 6 of 8 interviews (75%); Confidence remains High. Since this theme
  supports
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
  the insight was re-checked per the weakest-link rule: the EUDAMED supporting theme remains
  Confidence Medium and was not reassessed this turn, so the insight's confidence stays Medium
  overall.
- [[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
  gains a third confirming interview (Application Identification code must match
  character-for-character across documents; Change Notification justification copy-pasted into
  a separate internal document; long-running-project references going stale). Per the
  sample-relative check in [[Definitions]] (3 of 8 interviews, 37.5%, reaching the typical 3+
  repetition level), Confidence is raised from Medium to High. This theme concerns duplicated
  manual data entry across disconnected tools, not externally-sourced data requiring
  verification, and does not currently share a clear common mechanism with any
  insight-supporting theme, so it remains `not yet enough connected evidence`.
- The P03 standalone pain point
  [[../03_pains/Customers frequently fill in standard request forms incorrectly, requiring staff to return them for correction]]
  is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/Customers frequently fill in standard request forms incorrectly, requiring staff to return them for correction]]
  (P03, P08; Confidence Medium). This theme concerns customer-submitted form correctness, not
  externally-sourced data requiring assessment-time verification, and does not currently share
  a clear common mechanism with any insight-supporting theme. Recorded as `not yet enough
  connected evidence`.
- P03's previously related-evidence-only dual-channel communication observation is directly
  confirmed by P08 from a third-channel angle (email, Teams, UCI/PSE), and is promoted into a
  new theme created directly with two confirming interviews:
  [[../02_themes/Communication scattered across multiple parallel channels makes project history hard to reconstruct]]
  (P03, P08; Confidence Medium). This theme was explicitly compared against
  [[../02_themes/Communication is not linked to a project object, requiring staff to manually reference project numbers]]
  (P02, P07): the two are adjacent but distinct (channel fragmentation vs. missing
  reference-number linking), so they were not combined. Neither theme currently shares a clear
  common mechanism with any other existing theme; both remain `not yet enough connected
  evidence`.
- Seven new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P08 evidence (new-customer
  technical feasibility review gap; rigid step-by-step process sequencing blocking parallel
  work; inefficient ad hoc handoff communication between Auditor and Project Coordinator;
  Appendix ABC glossary lagging behind regulatory guidance; no single accountable point of
  contact for cross-department cost estimation; Project Coordinator/customer communication
  effort not reflected in commercial cost calculation; incomplete application document
  submission). None share a mechanism with an existing insight-supporting theme, so none were
  connected to an insight at this stage.
- P08's converging candidate idea (a single daily-use project overview with automatic
  per-project team assignment, in-tool phase-scoped chat, and a digital Appendix
  ABC-correction email template) was logged as a seventh/second interview extending the
  existing Appendix ABC digitization-vision candidate idea and the new communication-scattered
  pain point respectively; it does not confirm either theme's core mechanism on its own, so it
  was not counted toward interview count or confidence for either.
- P08's segment (Client Manager & Lead Auditor, blending Audit with account-level Client
  Management and project-manager-style oversight) does not cluster with the existing
  Auditor/Customer Specialist segment (P03, P04, P06) per the explicit comparison in
  [[../01_interviews/P08]] Context; it is background-only for insight purposes and logged in
  [[../07_personas/Proto-Segments]] as the first row in a new, not-yet-clustered segment (below
  the 3-interview persona threshold).

## Reference

  confirming interview; Confidence raised Medium → High per the sample-relative check in
  [[Definitions]]. It still concerns internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than
  externally-sourced data requiring verification, so it remains `not yet enough connected
  evidence` for an insight on its own.
- The P01 standalone pain point [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  is promoted to theme
  [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  (P01, P03; Confidence Medium). This theme shares the same underlying mechanism as the
  existing insight — externally-sourced (customer-maintained) data being relied upon without
  adequate verification — for a third data type (Appendix ABC master data, alongside
  regulatory codes and EUDAMED records). It has therefore been added as a third supporting
  theme to
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]].
  Insight confidence remains Medium (weakest-link rule; all three supporting themes are
  Medium). The existing recommendation was extended to include Appendix ABC entry-time
  validation; no new recommendation/insight was created.
- P03 also surfaces contradicting evidence on `Customers propose regulatory codes by best
  guess, requiring correction by certification staff` (her customers reportedly already
  understand codes) and related-but-distinct evidence on the P02 communication pain point
  (dual-channel tracking friction); neither changes the theme's confidence or triggers a new
  theme, per [[../01_interviews/P03]] "Theme Match".
sections.After P04 (fourth processed interview):
P04 directly confirms two existing themes; no new theme or insight was created:
- `No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff` gains a fourth
  confirming interview (TD assessment/Change Notification tracking has no company tool at all;
  the Assessment Plan Cloud tool is static). Confidence remains High (4 of 4 interviews, 100%).
  It still concerns internal tooling/data-entry discipline rather than externally-sourced data
  requiring verification, so it remains `not yet enough connected evidence` for an insight on
  its own.
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a third confirming interview (Appendix ABC review burden scales sharply with SKU/Basic
  UDI count; every new version requires full manual re-verification). Per the sample-relative
  check in [[Definitions]], Confidence is raised from Medium to High (3 of 4 interviews, 75%).
  Since this theme supports
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
  the insight's own confidence was reassessed: per the weakest-link rule, it cannot exceed the
  weakest supporting theme. The other two supporting themes (regulatory code assignment;
  EUDAMED data completeness) remain Confidence Medium and were not reassessed this turn, so the
  insight's confidence stays Medium overall.
- Three new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P04 evidence (deficiency
  report reminders; auditor/assessor conflict-of-interest verification; archival/handover
  incompleteness); none share a mechanism with an existing theme, so none were connected to an
  insight at this stage.
- Two P04 topics (`#code/customer-service-awareness-gap`,
  `#code/objectivity-perception-external`) were evaluated and found out of scope for the MACE
  Application workflow-digitization focus; recorded as background only in
  [[../01_interviews/P04]], not promoted to any artifact.
sections.After P05 (fifth processed interview):
P05 directly confirms two existing themes; no new theme was created, and the existing insight
was enriched but its overall confidence did not change:
- [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
  gains a third confirming interview (customers self-assigning EAC codes by superficial
  material match rather than manufacturing-technology scope). Per the sample-relative check in
  [[Definitions]] (3 of 5 interviews, 60%), Confidence is raised from Medium to High.
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a fourth confirming interview (no client has ever filled out Appendix ABC correctly on

- Since both themes support
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],

  three supporting themes now being High.
- Four new standalone preliminary pain points were created from P05 evidence (critical-supplier

  ABC copies diverging between auditor and reviewer; Mace Audit's broken findings-generation

sections.After P06 (sixth processed interview):

new theme, and creates four new standalone pain points; no new insight was created:
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
  gains a fifth confirming interview (Appendix ABC never complete at the start of a customer
  relationship; missing-data focus has shifted over time from Appendix A to Appendix C).
  Sample-relative check: 5 of 6 interviews (83%); Confidence remains High. Since this theme
  supports
  [[Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably]],
  the insight was re-checked per the weakest-link rule: the EUDAMED supporting theme remains
  Confidence Medium and was not reassessed this turn, so the insight's confidence stays Medium

  [[../02_themes/Customers cannot reliably predict the duration of the final certification review step]]

  shared responsibility for delays, not externally-sourced data requiring verification. It does

  yet enough connected evidence` pending a second theme that shares its mechanism.

  (Appendix-ABC signal-extraction difficulty; redundant manual data re-entry across
  disconnected tools; customer-facing Appendix ABC version conflicts from unshared local
  copies; internal document templates changing without staff or customer guidance). None share
  a mechanism with an existing insight-supporting theme, so none were connected to an insight
  at this stage.

  interview clustering with the existing Auditor/Customer Specialist proto-segment (P03, P04);

  its own.

  [[../03_pains/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]

  [[../02_themes/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]

  disconnected tools, not externally-sourced data requiring verification. It does not
  currently share a clear common mechanism with any existing insight-supporting theme, and
  only one theme is not enough to justify an insight on its own. This is recorded as `Theme:

  tools — not yet enough connected evidence` pending a second theme that shares its mechanism.

  sample-relative check in [[Definitions]] (3 of 8 interviews, 37.5%, reaching the typical 3+

  manual data entry across disconnected tools, not externally-sourced data requiring
  verification, and does not currently share a clear common mechanism with any
  insight-supporting theme, so it remains `not yet enough connected evidence`.

  common mechanism with any other existing theme; both remain `not yet enough connected
  evidence`.

notes.body:
<!-- State the synthesis directly in short, neutral sentences. Do not prescribe a solution here. -->

# Insight: Certification staff spend recurring, unplanned effort verifying externally-sourced data before assessment can proceed reliably

**Insight:** Certification staff cannot rely on customer-provided or platform-sourced data
without manual verification. This applies across at least three distinct data types —
customer-assigned regulatory codes, EUDAMED (European Database on Medical Devices)
product/certificate records, and the customer-maintained Appendix ABC master-data document —
and creates recurring correction overhead before assessment planning can proceed with
confidence.
**Supporting Themes:** [[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]], [[../02_themes/EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition]], [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]

**Update (2026-08-12):** Added the newly promoted theme
[[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
(P01, P03) as a third supporting theme; it describes the same underlying mechanism —
externally-sourced (customer-maintained) data being relied upon without adequate
verification — for a third data type. Confidence remains Medium: the weakest-link rule
applies, and all three supporting themes are currently Medium.

**Update (2026-08-12, same day):** P04 adds a third confirming interview to the Appendix ABC
supporting theme, raising that theme's own confidence from Medium to High (see
[[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]).
Per the weakest-link rule in [[Definitions]] "Inference Chain," this insight's confidence
cannot exceed the confidence of its weakest supporting theme. The other two supporting themes
(regulatory code assignment; EUDAMED data completeness) remain Confidence Medium and were not
reassessed this turn, so this insight's confidence stays Medium overall.

**Update (2026-08-12, later):** P05 confirms both the regulatory-code-assignment theme (3rd
interview, raising its confidence to High) and the Appendix ABC theme (4th interview, staying
High) — see
[[../02_themes/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]]
and
[[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]].
Two of the three supporting themes are now Confidence High. The weakest-link rule still
applies: the EUDAMED supporting theme remains Confidence Medium and was not reassessed this
turn, so this insight's overall confidence stays Medium, and Priority stays P2 (Severity
Medium x Confidence Medium).

**Update (2026-08-13):** P06 adds a fifth confirming interview to the Appendix ABC supporting
theme (see
[[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]);
Confidence remains High (5 of 6 interviews). The EUDAMED supporting theme remains Confidence
Medium and was not reassessed this turn, so this insight's overall confidence stays Medium and
Priority stays P2.

## Evidence
**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Manchmal ist auch nicht so ganz klar, ist der Code jetzt relevant für das Produkt oder nicht. ... es kann schon zu Fehlern kommen und zurückfragen, und dann ... das kann viel Zeit kosten." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "Sometimes it's also not entirely clear whether a code is relevant for the product or not. ... errors and follow-up questions can occur, and then ... that can cost a lot of time." - [P02]

> "Es hat halt große Verzögerung gehabt, das Tool. ... was momentan wirklich bisher nur für Herstellerdaten, Adresse gut war, und die ganzen Sachen mit Zertifikaten, Produktdaten, die kommen jetzt erst zu langsam." - [P02]
>
> Translation: "The tool has had major delays. ... what has really only been good so far for manufacturer data and address, and all the things with certificates and product data are only now slowly coming online." - [P02]

> "Also einerseits dann mit den Daten, die sie dann haben ... da verliere ich glaube ich am meisten Zeit ... es gibt hier in einer Basic UDI verschiedene intended users. Dürfen sie eigentlich gar nicht haben." - [P03]
>
> Translation: "On one hand with the data they have ... I think that's where I lose the most time ... there are different intended users on one Basic UDI here. They aren't actually allowed to have that." - [P03]

> "for the customer that I have more than 100 [Basic UDI/SKUs], it's critical because I have the, let's say, I'm afraid that there could be losing of data, wrong typing, from the customer, I mean, overwriting." - [P04]

> "I've never had a client fill it out correctly in one go. There's always something wrong with it that I have to go back to them and ask for a correction or a clarification on." - [P05]

> "at the very beginning with the company, there are a lot of missing information. ... when they have to fulfill the Appendix ABC for the first time, they fear the white paper, like they don't know how to fulfill it." - [P06]

**Business Impact:** Staff time is spent catching and correcting externally-sourced data
errors case by case, rather than on assessment work itself; P03 specifically names the
Appendix ABC data-quality cross-check as her single biggest time cost before assessment. P04
adds that this cross-check burden scales sharply with customer size (SKU/Basic UDI count). P05
adds that no client, across her onboarding experience, has ever submitted a correct Appendix
ABC on the first attempt, extending the pattern to a new-client onboarding segment. The exact
volume of this overhead is not yet quantified across the five interviews.
**Design Implication:** The certification workflow should surface a verification/cross-check
capability at the specific points where externally-sourced data enters the process (customer
code selection; product/certificate lookups; Appendix ABC submission and updates), rather than
relying on staff to discover discrepancies during downstream review or mid-assessment.

## Recommendation
<!-- Add only when a concrete action is warranted by this insight. State it impersonally with should or shall. Leave `None yet` if the action is not clear. This is the anchor; do not create a separate recommendation note. -->
**Recommendation:** The certification workflow should provide an in-workflow, example-based
reference at the point where a customer selects a regulatory code, should offer an optional
cross-check of customer product/certificate data against EUDAMED once EUDAMED's data for that
record type is available, and should validate Appendix ABC entries against known regulatory
constraints (such as disallowed intended-user combinations) at submission time rather than
only at assessment, so discrepancies are surfaced before assessment planning rather than
corrected ad hoc later.
**Additional Supporting Themes/Pain Points:** [[../03_pains/Customers propose regulatory codes by best guess, requiring correction by certification staff]], [[../03_pains/EUDAMED product and certificate data remains incomplete during the platform's transition]], [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
**Expected Effect:** Fewer late-discovered code, product-data, and Appendix ABC discrepancies,
reducing follow-up questions and correction cycles between staff and customers.
**Risk:** The EUDAMED cross-check depends on the platform's data maturing beyond its current
transition state; until then, its verification value is limited to manufacturer/address data
and does not yet extend to the certificate/product data this recommendation relies on. The
guidance and Appendix ABC validation components do not depend on this and can proceed
independently.
**Priority:** P2, per [[Definitions]] Priority Tier matrix (Severity Medium x Confidence
Medium on all three supporting pain points).

## Reference
When evidence is thin, do not create an insight; record the gap in [[SOP-Analysis-Process]].
Recommendations live inside their anchor insight and are also listed in [[_recommendations-register]].

notes.body:
<!-- Describe the segment in neutral third-person language. Keep goals separate from recommendations. -->

# Persona: Auditor - Customer Specialist

**Before completing:** Does this rely on at least three distinct interviews with a consistent
pattern? If not, keep `status: proto-persona` and treat it as a hypothesis. See [[Definitions]]
for confidence criteria; the same logic applies here. This persona is based on exactly three
interviews (P03, P04, P06); it is retained as `proto-persona` pending further confirming
interviews, since the pattern, while consistent on the core job-to-be-done, still shows
variation in account scale, tenure, and specific sub-responsibilities across the three
interviews.

**Segment:** Internal certification staff who combine Audit responsibilities with ongoing,
direct customer-facing account management (Customer Specialist), as distinct from
account-management-only roles (P01), TD-Assessor roles without customer contact (P02), and
bounded new-client-onboarding roles (P05).
**Based on Interviews:** [[../01_interviews/P03]], [[../01_interviews/P04]], [[../01_interviews/P06]]

## Context
This persona owns the technical side of a customer's certification journey end to end:
collecting Appendix ABC data, building the assessment plan, coordinating audits and
assessments with the customer, and performing Audits directly. Account scale and specific
sub-responsibilities vary: P03 manages one large key account (Unique Company Identifier
(UCI)-based) plus smaller accounts and focuses heavily on cost/fee calculation and subcontract
coordination with Project Coordinators; P04 is newer to MDR (Medical Device Regulation, since
2023) and is also authorized for packaging/sterilization audits and Technical Documentation
(TD) Assessment for one product code; P06 manages roughly 15 companies, is also a Lead Auditor
and TD Assessor, and separately holds a secondary competency-coordination role. Across all
three, Appendix ABC is the central working document, and each independently maintains a
personal spreadsheet-based workaround (a status-tracking list for P03; a stable, essential-
fields-only extract for P06) to compensate for gaps in official tooling.

## Goals
- Extract and work from the small subset of Appendix ABC data actually needed for planning,
  without being slowed down by document volume or complexity.
- Avoid manually re-entering or reconciling the same customer data across multiple
  disconnected tools and documents.
- Maintain a reliable, shared, up-to-date view of a project's status and of Appendix ABC's
  current state with both colleagues and the customer.
- Reduce time spent on data-quality cross-checks and correction round-trips with customers.

## Related Themes
- [[../02_themes/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
- [[../02_themes/No consolidated project status view exists for certification staff]]

## Related Pain Points
- [[../03_pains/Appendix ABC is treated as single source of truth despite being the most error-prone document]]
- [[../03_pains/Certification staff must manually extract a small, essential data subset from a much larger volume of Appendix ABC information]]
- [[../03_pains/The same core certification data must be manually re-entered across multiple disconnected tools]]
- [[../03_pains/Customer-facing Appendix ABC version conflicts arise from unshared local copies]]
- [[../03_pains/Internal document templates change without staff or customer guidance on how to complete them]]
- [[../03_pains/Certification staff cannot update subcontract timelines themselves, causing duplicate work when Project Coordinators do not update them proactively]]
- [[../03_pains/Archival processing is deprioritized and often left incomplete, complicating customer handovers between staff]]

## Related Needs
- [[../04_needs/Certification staff need reliable, complete Appendix ABC data before assessment can proceed efficiently]]

# Proto-Segments

Log every processed interview here, one row per interview, regardless of how many rows exist.
Once 3+ rows cluster into a consistent segment, apply the Persona Splitting check in
[[SOP-Analysis-Process]] before creating or extending a persona note in `07_personas`.

| Interview ID | Suspected Segment | Key Characteristics |
|---|---|---|
| P01 | Internal certification staff - Manager Global Accounts (senior regulatory/account management, MDR certification requests) | Deep regulatory code expertise (MDA/MDS/MDT/EMDN/RC/MD); works with Legal Entities and multiple sites per customer; prioritizes code-driven, audit-relevant information over product-family/variant detail; oversees Customer Specialists who handle day-to-day code review and best-guess corrections; wants change traceability, consolidated status tracking, and a priority/decision escalation path. |
| P02 | Internal certification staff - Senior Product Specialist / Technical Documentation (TD) Assessor (product certification evaluation, MDR) | No direct customer contact (handled by Customer Specialists/Relationship Managers/Project Coordinators); engaged from Application Review/Assessment onward; centers work around Appendix ABC for module/authorization lookup and device/variant counts for cost calculation; desktop-only usage; raises task-assignment fairness, cross-border interface delay, and in-tool guided process display as improvement areas rather than complaints. |
| P03 | Internal certification staff - Auditor / Customer Specialist (mixed role, ~4 years tenure, ~30-40% Audits / remainder Customer Specialist for one large key account plus smaller accounts) | Direct customer contact for both large (UCI-based) and smaller (email-based) accounts; not involved in TD Assessment itself; performs Audits and coordinates who performs TD Assessment; centers work around Appendix ABC data-quality cross-checks before assessment, subcontract timeline follow-up with Project Coordinators, and cost/fee calculation for Supplier Audits and Change Notifications; maintains a personal Excel status-tracking list; wants an end-to-end workflow/ownership view ("whose turn it is"). |
| P04 | Internal certification staff - Lead Auditor & Customer Specialist (mixed role, with MDR since 2023, Italy-based, 3-4 MDR customers plus other MD-support/ISO customers; still gaining full comfort with the internal audit-planning tool) | Direct customer contact; also authorized for packaging/sterilization audits (low-risk devices) and TD Assessment for one code without clinical data; centers work around Appendix ABC review (workload scales sharply with SKU/Basic UDI count) and deficiency-report/response tracking; relies on a personal, regionally-built planning tool for audits with no equivalent support for TD Assessment or Change Notification tracking; raises conflict-of-interest verification and archival/handover completeness as manual, unsupported activities. |
| P05 | Internal certification staff - New-Client Onboarding Technical Expert / Lead Auditor (SPOS - Special Operations and Support, US-based) | Bounded, one-time-per-client role: supports Sales with technical IVDR/MDR quoting, collects application-review documents (including Appendix ABC), builds internal planning documents (assessment plan, sampling plan, Application Management Checklist), personally leads the client's first audit cycle, writes the final audit/certification package, then performs a formal handoff to Operations and typically has no further client contact; identifies as an auditor rather than a TD reviewer; centers work around getting Appendix ABC (codes, scope statement, critical-supplier list) correct for the first time; uses Mace Audit (mandatory) and ID Guard (preferred document-sharing platform). |
| P06 | Internal certification staff - Customer Specialist / Lead Auditor / TD Assessor (Italy-based, ~6 years tenure, manages ~15 companies; also holds a secondary SPS competency-coordination role for risk management) | Direct customer contact, owns the technical certification journey end to end (Appendix ABC intake, assessment planning, audit/assessment scheduling); also Lead Auditor and TD Assessor; centers work around extracting a small essential data subset from a much larger volume of Appendix ABC data, and re-entering the same core data across five disconnected internal tools; maintains a personal Excel tool holding only essential fields, stable across years of changing official systems; envisions a shared, jointly-editable device-list database with auto-suggested field values and automatic assessment-plan/schedule generation; raises customer-facing Appendix ABC version conflicts and unguided template changes as friction points; connects final-review timeline unpredictability to a new MDR Article 7 requirement to share timelines with customers. |
| P07 | Internal certification staff - Project Coordinator (commercial/backoffice, ~5 years tenure, low-risk device segment: MDSub/ISO/MDD/Taiwan; formally also recorded as Customer Specialist/Support Specialist; not customer-call-facing) | Owns the commercial/administrative side of the certification lifecycle end to end (project creation in PSE, cost calculation, quotation, signature routing, subcontract creation, scheduling trigger, SAP contract linkage, CBW audit registration); does not attend customer calls, only ad hoc customer contact for billing; centers work around Appendix ABC's redundant per-variant/per-facility row structure and cross-tab code decoding at volumes of 2,000-3,000 rows; built and rolled out a self-made Audit Pricing Tool across the Business Service Center; raises informal post-attrition customer-account assignment, unnecessary multi-party signature requirements, assessor ready-status/timeline non-compliance, and UCI's one-way file-exchange limitation as friction points; envisions centrally managed master data with code-driven auto-suggestion and a single tool spanning CBW, SAP, and the sampling/assessment plans. |
| P08 | Internal certification staff - Client Manager & Lead Auditor (originally CARE, Conformity Assessment Responsible, under MDR; ~1 large multi-site European customer plus 6-7 smaller customers in Germany/Europe) | Blends Audit with account-level Client Management and project-manager-style oversight across Project Coordinators and subject-matter teams for his accounts; one of the few staff working directly in UCI as an Auditor; also involved in commercial/quotation matters for tailored offers to existing key accounts and manages his own cost/hour escalation path; centers work around Appendix ABC data-inconsistency/traceability issues (relies on informal consistency-check macros), two separately-built status filters across BSE and PSE, and reassembling project communication scattered across email, Teams, and UCI/PSE; raises new-customer feasibility-review gaps, rigid step-by-step process sequencing for priority projects, and cost-estimation cross-department coordination as friction points; envisions a single daily-use tool with project overview, automatic team assignment, and in-tool chat. |

## Reference
See [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] "Persona Splitting" and Step H in the vault instructions. P03,
P04, and P06 all combine Audit and Customer Specialist responsibilities and form a consistent
"Auditor / Customer Specialist" segment cluster; with P06 this reaches 3 of 6 rows, meeting the
persona-creation threshold. The Persona Splitting check in [[SOP-Analysis-Process]] was applied
before creating the persona note: despite some variation in account scale, tenure, and specific
sub-responsibilities (P03: larger key-account focus, cost/fee calculation, subcontract
coordination; P04: newer to MDR since 2023, packaging/sterilization audit authorization; P06:
signal-extraction/data-consolidation focus, secondary SPS role), all three share the same core
job-to-be-done (managing the customer relationship while performing audits) and the same
required solution shape (a consolidated Appendix ABC-centric data source with less redundant
manual entry). This is not a fundamental axis requiring different product recommendations, so
one persona note was created rather than split sub-personas: [[Auditor - Customer Specialist]].

P05 does not cluster with any existing segment: unlike P01 (account management), P02 (TD
Assessor, no customer contact), and P03/P04/P06 (Auditor/Customer Specialist for ongoing
accounts), P05's role is scoped specifically to the one-time new-client onboarding lifecycle,
ending in a formal handoff to Operations. This is the first row in this cluster — well below
the 3-row threshold for a persona note.

P07 does not cluster with any existing segment either: unlike P01 (account management), P02
(TD Assessor, no customer contact), P03/P04/P06 (Auditor/Customer Specialist, customer-facing),
and P05 (one-time new-client onboarding), P07 is a commercial/backoffice Project Coordinator
who owns the administrative and financial side of the lifecycle (quotation, signature routing,
scheduling, invoicing) and explicitly does not attend customer calls. This is the first row in
a new "Project Coordinator / commercial-backoffice" cluster — well below the 3-row threshold
for a persona note.

P08 does not cluster with any existing segment either: unlike P03/P04/P06 (Auditor/Customer
Specialist for ongoing accounts, without account-level client-management or project-manager
oversight duties), P08 explicitly blends Audit with account-level Client Management and
project-manager-style oversight across Project Coordinators and subject-matter teams, and is
also directly involved in commercial/quotation matters and the very front end of the process
(Pre-Application/Application) in more depth than the earlier Auditor/Customer Specialist
interviews. This distinction is made explicitly in [[../01_interviews/P08]] Context. This is
the first row in a new "Client Manager & Lead Auditor" cluster — well below the 3-row threshold
for a persona note.
